We therefore command you either to act in accordance with the judgment given, or, if you believe yourself grievously burdened, to present yourself before the hearing of that legate in order to argue your case. But if even now you are unwilling to comply, we confirm by our authority the sentence which he pronounced.

Given at the Lateran on the Kalends of May (1103).

XCV. To D[idacus], bishop of Compostela. (A.D. 1103, May 1.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, as above, p. 92.]

[Col. 0114B]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother D., bishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The nature and greatness of the affection which your brotherhood bears toward us are openly demonstrated by faithful services and deeds. Although separated from us by long stretches of land, you nevertheless make yourself present to us both by the affection of your spirit and by the performance of frequent services. Therefore we too, repaying you as our brother with the gift of mutual affection, admonish and request you never, on any occasion, to turn your mind away from the course of goodness which you have begun [Col. 0114C] or from the display of affection which you have begun.

Concerning the administration of the office entrusted to you, strive, like a valiant soldier, to exercise care and diligence; enjoy such abundance of earthly goods that you are not deprived of love for heavenly rewards. Let external and transitory things not so entangle your mind that you are deprived of eternal and abiding goods. Always set heavenly things before earthly, eternal things before perishing ones. In every respect show yourself such a man that you may deserve to receive from the Shepherd of shepherds the reward of a good shepherd. We have gratefully received the offerings which you sent us through your messengers, and we render thanks for them. But that we have at present been unable to grant assent to certain of your requests [Col. 0114D] is for a definite reason. Concerning the abbot of Cinis, regarding whom you consulted us, we command that you restore him to the monastery, so that there he may maintain the regular order and monastic life with the brethren. The nuns, however, having been placed in some suitable location, we decree that food and all necessities shall be supplied by the same abbot.

Given at the Lateran on the Kalends of May.

XCVI. To the abbot of Saint Mary at Bantium.—Privilege of this monastery. (A.D. 1103, May 22.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1056.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ, the abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary, which is situated [Col. 0115A] at Bantium, and to his successors to be regularly advanced for ever.

Although we are bound to all the children of the holy Church by both the authority and benevolence of the Apostolic See, it especially befits us to apply ourselves with greater zeal to those places and persons which are more especially and closely attached to the Roman Church and which stand out by reason of fuller religious observance. Since, therefore, the monastery of Blessed Mary, over whose house [perhaps: “to whose house,” H.] you preside by the authority of its lawful sons, is known hitherto to have adhered by its own right to the Roman and Apostolic Church, we, out of devotion and reverence for God himself and for Mary, ever-virgin Mother of God, specially cherish and protect it under the protection of our hand. Therefore we grant and confirm to you and your successors [Col. 0115B] authority for the governance of the aforesaid house: namely, the monastery itself and all that belongs to it, whether dependent cells with their appurtenances, namely the Church of Saint Saviour, etc.

(Here are enumerated the possessions of that monastery.)

Therefore we establish that whatever the aforesaid monastery rightfully possesses today, and whatever it may in future rightly and canonically acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, and the offerings of the faithful, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors, wholly beneficial to the uses of those for whose support and governance they were granted [perhaps: “are for the uses,” etc.], while preserving, however, the canonical right which the bishops are known to have had in them. [Col. 0115C] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the same monastery, invade possessions belonging to it, retain, diminish, take away, or apply to his own uses possessions which have been seized, or harass it with rash vexations.

Upon the death of you, abbot of the same place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of fraud, except one whom the brethren of that monastery, by common consent or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall customarily elect in the fear of God. The person elected shall come to the Roman pontiff for consecration. The brethren of your cells shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of clerics from the diocesan bishops [Col. 0115D], provided that these are Catholic and enjoy the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and are willing to confer these things freely and without corruption. Otherwise the brethren may receive the same consecration and sacraments from whatever Catholic bishop they choose. For the ordination of monks of the cloister, we grant you and your successors leave to summon [a bishop] into the monastery itself, provided that he agrees, supported by our authority, so that occasion for wandering outside may not be permitted.

Furthermore, if, burdened by any oppression, you appeal to the Roman See, no bishop may inflict any violence upon you or your successors under pretext of a judicial proceeding, except before the Roman pontiff or his legate. Therefore, most beloved sons, you ought to labour diligently and devotedly in the pursuits of regular discipline [Col. 0116A], so that, the freer you are from secular disturbance, the more eagerly you may strive with all the strength of mind and soul to please God. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, pay yearly one ounce of gold to the Lateran palace. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act contrary to this charter of our constitution, etc., as in Epistle 18.

Written through the hand of Raynerius, regional scribe and notary of the sacred palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal-deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of July, in the first indiction, in the year 1103 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fifth year of the pontificate [Col. 0116B] of Pope Paschal.

XCVII. At the request of Provost Manegald, he receives the monastery of Marbach under the protection of the Apostolic See. (A.D. 1103, August 2.)

[WURTWEIN, *Nova subsidia diplomatica*, VI, 277.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons professing the canonical life in the Church of Marbach, and to their successors who shall remain in the same religious life for ever.

Just as no effect ought to be granted to those who ask unjustly, so the petition of those who desire what is lawful ought not to be delayed. Accordingly, we readily grant effect both to your petitions and to those of your most beloved [Col. 0116C] son Manegald, your provost. Following the footsteps of our predecessor Urban II of holy memory, we receive both you and all that is yours under the protection of the Apostolic See and fortify you by the authority of the present privilege. We establish that no one among you, after making profession, may possess anything as private property or be free to leave the cloister without permission of the provost or of the whole community. If anyone leaves and, after warning, scorns to return, the provost and his successors shall have authority to suspend such a person from his offices wherever he may be; and no bishop or abbot may absolve one thus suspended without the provost’s consent.

Moreover, by the charter of this present privilege, we establish by apostolic authority [Col. 0116D] that whatever your Church rightfully possesses today, and whatever it may hereafter rightly and canonically acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, or the offerings of the faithful, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We likewise decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the same church, take away its possessions, retain or diminish what has been offered, or harass it with rash vexations; rather, let all things be preserved intact, wholly beneficial to the uses of those for whose support and governance they were granted.

In addition, we establish that no one may be imposed upon you as provost through violence or any deceit, except one whom all the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel [Col. 0117A], shall provide to be regularly elected according to the fear of God. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of clerics from the bishop in whose diocese you are, provided that he enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to confer them freely and without corruption. Otherwise you may approach whichever Catholic prelate you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts to act contrary to this charter of our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects himself by suitable satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him acknowledge himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred [Col. 0117B] body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for the same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of August, through the hand of Equitius acting in place of the chancellor, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1103 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

XCVIII. To D[idacus], bishop of Compostela. (A.D. 1103, October 15.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 76.]

[Col. 0117C]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother D., bishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

At the request of the clerics of your Church, who had formerly come to us, we remember having written to the bishop of Mondoñedo that he should restore to your authority the two and a half archpresbyterates which the Church of blessed James was said to have held in his diocese. But clerics of the aforesaid Church of Mondoñedo, coming to us, stated that for forty years after that land had been taken from the hands of the Saracens, the aforesaid church had peacefully possessed [Col. 0117D] those archpresbyterates. If, therefore, the truth is so, we command your belovedness to leave the said two and a half archpresbyterates peacefully in the possession of that Church. Further, we wish you to restore to the said Church the customs which it says it had possessed on an equal footing in certain churches and which your brotherhood is said to have taken away. Yet if, in all these matters, the Church of blessed James has any right, it shall send messengers at the next Kalends of October together with the envoys of the bishop of Mondoñedo, who are to come to us at the same term.

Given at the Lateran on the Ides of October.

XCIX. Bull for Ferrières. (A.D. 1103, November 11.)

[Gallia Christiana, X, Instrument 15.]

[Col. 0118A]

PASCHAL, servant of the servants of God, to his son in Christ ATGERIUS, most reverend abbot of the monastery of Ferrières, or Bethlehem, consecrated in honour of blessed Mary, Mother of God, and of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and to his successors to be regularly appointed for ever.

A devout request ought to be fulfilled by the ensuing result of its wish, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the benefit sought may assuredly gain strength. Since, therefore, your belovedness has fled to the harbour of the Apostolic See and has duly sought its protection with devotion [Col. 0118B], we mercifully assent to your petitions. Following the practice of our predecessors, we receive under the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Saint Peter, over which, by God’s ordering, you preside, with all that pertains to it, as your devotion has requested. It is known that a certain venerable duke, named Wandebertus, of holy memory, formerly built this monastery and enriched it with gifts from his own property.

Therefore, by the charter of the present privilege, we establish by apostolic authority that whatever estates and possessions the same venerable Duke Wandebertus granted to that monastery; whatever appears to belong to it through lawful gifts of other faithful persons; and whatever it may hereafter rightly and canonically acquire by the grant of pontiffs [Col. 0118C], the generosity of princes, or the offerings of the faithful, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We decree that a certain cell of Saint Josse, situated in the district of Ponthieu on the river Canche, in the place called Schaderias, with all that belongs to it by right and law, shall remain for ever under the lordship and administration of the rulers of the said monastery of Ferrières, or Bethlehem, together with the Church of Saint Eligius, which lies in view of that monastery, the Church of Saint Martin of Courtemaux, the Church of Saint Victurius of Fontenay, the Church of Saint Amand of Boursiac, and all their goods and possessions.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any one of your successors, no other person shall be set over it by any cunning of fraud [Col. 0118D] or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. The person elected shall receive blessing and the other things according to the custom of our predecessors. We decree, therefore, that no person may rashly disturb the same monastery, nor its rulers and the brethren entrusted to them by God; take away its possessions; retain or diminish goods taken away; or burden it with arbitrary exactions. Rather, let all things be preserved intact, wholly beneficial to the uses of those for whose support and governance they were granted. Whatever immunity, liberty, or grant this monastery is known hitherto to have received from the pontiffs of this holy Roman [Col. 0119A] Church, or from other archbishops, bishops, Catholic kings, and other faithful persons, we hold confirmed and firm. If any ecclesiastical or secular person [acts contrary to] this charter of our constitution, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal-deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of November, in the twelfth indiction, in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II.

C. To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He confirms his primacy. (A.D. 1103, November 16.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1023.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ANSELM, bishop of Canterbury, greeting [Col. 0119B] and apostolic blessing.

The authority of your wisdom and religion persuades us to grant your brotherhood’s requests. For formerly, in letters sent to you from the Apostolic See, we granted you the primacy of the Church of Canterbury in its full extent, as it is known to have been possessed by your predecessors. Now, assenting to your petitions, we confirm by this present letter to you and to your lawful successors that same primacy, and whatever dignity or power is known to belong to that holy Church of Canterbury, or Dorobernia, just as your predecessors are known to have possessed it by authority of the Apostolic See from the time of blessed Augustine.

[Col. 0119C] Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of December, in the twelfth indiction.

CI. To Henry, King of England.—For Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, defending by right against the king the matter of ecclesiastical investitures. (A.D. 1103, November 23.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1000.]

PASCHAL, bishop, to King HENRY, greeting.

In the letter which you recently sent to us through your chaplain, William, the son of our affection, we learned both of your personal well-being and of the prosperous successes which divine goodness has granted you after you overcame the enemies of the realm. We further heard that you have received a desired male child by your noble and religious wife. Since this has indeed gladdened us, [Col. 0119D] we judged it timely now to impress upon you more forcefully the commands and will of God, since you perceive yourself to be indebted to His goodness for ampler benefits. We too desire to join our good will toward you to the divine benefits; but it is grievous to us that you seem to seek from us what we absolutely cannot grant. For if we consent to, or permit, investitures to be made by your highness, both ours, beyond doubt, and yours will be an immense peril.

In this matter we wish you to consider what you lose by not doing it, or what you gain by doing it. For in this prohibition we obtain for ourselves nothing further in the way of obedience, nothing in the way of generosity, through the churches; nor do we strive to take away anything from the power or right due to you, except that God’s wrath may be lessened toward you and that thus every prosperity may befall you. For the Lord says: “Those who honor me I will honor, but those who despise me shall be held in contempt” (1 Kings [1 Samuel] 2). You will therefore say: “This is mine by right.” Certainly not: it is not imperial, not royal, but divine. It belongs to Him alone who said: “I am the door” (John 20). Therefore, for the sake of Him whose gift this is, I ask you to render it to Him, to leave it to Him, to whose love you owe even those things which are yours. But why should we resist your will, why oppose your favor, unless we knew that, by consenting in this business, we should oppose God’s will and forfeit His favor? Why should we deny you anything which ought to be granted to any mortal, when we have received more ample benefits from you?

Consider, dearest son, whether it is an honor or a disgrace [Col. 0120B] to you that Anselm, the wisest and most devout of English bishops, because of this matter fears to remain attached to your side and to remain in your kingdom. What will those who have hitherto heard such great good things about you think and say of you when this has been spread abroad through the lands? Those who in your presence praise your excesses will, when deprived of your presence, denounce this all the more strongly. Return then, dearest son, to your heart for the mercy of God; and, for love of the Only-Begotten, we beseech you: call back your shepherd; call back your father. And if anyone—though we do not expect it—should behave more harshly toward you if you reject investitures, we shall, according to your will, moderate the matter as far as, with God, we can. Yet remove from your person and kingdom the disgrace of such a rejection.

If you do this, then, even should you ask grave things of us, which it is possible, with God, to grant, you will certainly obtain them; and, with His help, we shall take care to entreat the Lord for you, and through the merits of the holy apostles we shall grant pardon and absolution from sins both to you and to your wife. Your son, moreover, whom you received from your distinguished and glorious wife, and whom, as we have heard, you named after your eminent father William, we shall cherish with such special solicitude together with you that whoever injures you or him will seem to have injured the Roman Church.

Given at the Lateran, on the ninth day before the Kalends of December [23 November].

## CI bis. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Casale Benedicti. (1103, 27 November.)

[MABILLON, *Annals*, book LXX, vol. V, p. 468.]

[Col. 0120D]

To the beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of St. Peter . . . . . . . that regular discipline may be preserved in that monastery, which there, from its very beginnings, [the same Andrew had established] according to the custom of the Vallombrosan brethren . . .

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of December [27 November], through the hand of Equitius, acting in place of the chancellor, in the twelfth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1104 [1103], and in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II.

## CII. He exhorts G[ebhard] of Hirsau and the other Catholic abbots and monks throughout Swabia to bear misfortunes with equanimity and to honor G[ebhard] of Constance. He announces that Arnold, invader of the Church of Constance, is excommunicated. (About 10 February 1103.)

[NEUGART, *Diplomatic Codex of Alemannia*, II, 40.]

[Col. 0121A]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons G. of Hirsau [Note: [Col. 0121D] Gebhard, of the family of the counts of Urach, a canon of Strasbourg, withdrew to Hirsau. There, by the votes of the brethren, he was called from the office of prior to the dignity of abbot in 1091, and presided for twelve years and three months. Trithemius, *Chronicle*, and Crus., *Annals*, book VIII, part II, ch. 9, p. 276.] and to the other Catholic abbots and monks throughout Swabia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have heard, dearest sons, that the world rages against you more fiercely than usual, that persecutions increase, and that the swelling waves of the sea rise more violently against you. But the Lord is wonderful on high, He who treads them under His feet. Therefore we ask you not to lose heart in your tribulations, which are your glory. For, as the Apostle says, “The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the future glory [Col. 0121B] which shall be revealed in us.” Our fathers, desiring the revelation of this glory, went rejoicing from the presence of the council; so we too, who ought to become their imitators, should rejoice while placed amid sorrow and distress. For our sorrow shall be turned into joy.

For we hope in the Lord, trusting in the merits of the holy apostles, that He who says, “I have overcome the world,” will put an end to your persecutions. Therefore, most beloved, striving toward the prize of the heavenly calling, contend manfully in the present contest; encourage yourselves by mutual assistance; look all of you to the burning lamp among you—namely, our brother G., bishop of Constance [Note: [Col. 0121D] Gebhard, bishop of Constance and legate of the Apostolic See under Urban II, was confirmed by Paschal II in the same office. Berthold of Constance, under the year 1100.]; all of you unanimously honor him, and, joining the arms of love, assist both him and yourselves in [Col. 0121C] these tribulations.

Moreover, know that A., the invader of the Church of Constance [Note: [Col. 0121D] This is Arnold, a monk of St. Gall. Through the intervention of Ulrich, abbot of the same monastery and patriarch of Aquileia, he was appointed by Henry IV to Gebhard’s see. He was ordained bishop at Rome by the antipope Clement III and was finally intruded there by force on 2 February 1103. He had a brother, Henry of St. Mountain, commonly Heiligenberg, a most zealous partisan of his cause. *Chronicle of Petershausen*, book III, §§26–28. Burchard, *On the Monastery of St. Gall*, ch. 7.] has been excommunicated by the Roman Church and cut off from the unity of the Catholic Church as a rotten member. Flee from him everywhere as from deadly poison, and avoid him by every means.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth Ides of February [10 February] . . . .

## CIII. To Duke Welf of Bavaria, Duke Berthold of Swabia, and others.—He calls them back to the Catholic Church. (About 10 February 1103.)

[NEUGART, *Diplomatic Codex of Alemannia*, II, 41.]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the distinguished men Duke WELF [Note: [Col. 0122D] This is Welf V, formerly the husband of Matilda, marchioness of Tuscany, whom he left in 1095. Shortly afterwards he was reconciled to Henry IV, together with his father Welf IV, as Berthold of Constance reports under this year.] and his brother HENRY [Note: [Col. 0122D] Called Henry the Black, son of Welf IV. On these men see R. P. Hess, *Monuments of the Welfs*, part I.], duke, [Col. 0122A] BERTHOLD [Note: [Col. 0122D] Berthold II of Zähringen, brother of Gebhard, bishop of Constance, is accused by the writer of the *Chronicle of Petershausen* of having abandoned Gebhard’s party, like many others, corrupted by gifts. Book III, ch. 27.] and his nephew HERMANN [Note: [Col. 0122D] Hermann I, margrave of Baden, was the brother of the Berthold II of Zähringen just mentioned, who died at Cluny in 1074. By Judith of Calw he had a namesake son, who is the person mentioned here. See Schoepflin, *History of Zähringen-Baden*, vol. I, p. 267 ff.], and to the other princes throughout Swabia . . .

Although, having turned after Satan, you have for a long time been forgetful of your salvation, nevertheless we, whom the obligation of our office and the authority of the Apostolic See compel, cannot forget your salvation. We therefore thought it fitting by these present letters to bring you back to your own hearts and, though absent in body, to awaken you from the sleep of death. God’s patience awaits your repentance, but you are storing up wrath for yourselves on the day of wrath.

It is long since you separated yourselves from the members of the Catholic Church and adhered to a perverse head, inflicting injuries upon the members of that Church which bore you in Christ, and, together with the head of all evils, oppressing your very mother with persecutions. [Col. 0122B] We judge this all the more unworthy and endure it the more grievously because we knew you as her defenders and her lovers. Yet she who daily intercedes with her bridegroom for her children will gladly receive you if you recover your senses and recognize yourselves as her members; she will restore you to the number of her children.

You have near you a member of the supreme Head and an eye of the Church—namely, our brother G., bishop of Constance—who can more fully instruct you concerning your salvation and lead you from darkness into light. Whoever hears his voice should believe that he hears Him who says: “He who hears you hears me, and he who despises you despises me.” Therefore have recourse to him as to a father, and obey his admonitions in all things as you would those of Blessed Peter and ourselves. If you do this, you shall be released from the bond of the curse. Moreover, know that A., the invader of the Church of Constance, has been excommunicated by the Roman Church and cut off from the unity of the Catholic Church as a rotten member. [Col. 0122C] Flee from him everywhere as from deadly poison, and avoid him by every means.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth Ides of February [10 February] . . . .

## CIV. To the French.—He lifts the interdict by which the bishop of Autun had placed the Church of Vézelay under restriction. (About 30 October 1103.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1029.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the clerics, knights, and all other laypeople throughout the churches of Gaul, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have heard, and could scarcely believe, that our brother the bishop of Autun, and his archdeacons or archpriests, led not by justice but compelled by jealousy, have forbidden you to visit the monastery of Vézelay out of devotion, to enter the church, to approach the tomb of Blessed Mary, which is venerated in that church, or to make any offerings there. This is indeed a novel, a novel interdict of priests, since it seems to be the duty of the priestly office to call people to devotion, not to call them back from devotion. Therefore, annulling this interdict as contrary to priestly office, we wish you to know that, unless the bishop or his ministers desist from this presumption, they shall be punished by the indignation of the Apostolic See.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of November [30 October].

## CV. * He informs the clergy and people of Pavia that he will not permit the privileges of the monastery of St. Peter in Ciel d’Oro to be infringed by Bishop William. (Within the years 1100–1103, 25 June.)

[Only a mention survives in ROBOLINI, *Notices Relating to the History of His Native Country*. Pavia, 1823, octavo, vol. III, pp. 224, 226.]

[Col. 0123B]

## CVI. To Peter, king of Aragon. (About 1103.)

[*General History of Languedoc*, Paris, 1730, folio, vol. II, Documents, p. 365.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, king of the Aragonese, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is very widely known that the church of St. Saturninus, martyr of Toulouse, has from ancient times been specially subject to the jurisdiction of Blessed Peter, so much so that our predecessor Pope Urban, of good memory, consecrated it with his own hand together with seventeen archbishops and bishops, and secured it by the privileges of the Apostolic See under the bond of anathema, etc. Our brother Peter, bishop of Pamplona, gave a little church to the aforesaid martyr and his canons with the counsel of Lord Sancho, your father the king, etc.

## CVII. To Bertrand, count of Toulouse.—A rebuke because he invaded the borough of St. Giles and offered the altar’s oblations for sale like common merchandise. (Within the years 1101–1104, 14 November.)

[Dom BOUQUET, *Collection*, vol. XV, p. 32.]

[Col. 0123D] PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Count BERTRAND, greeting—if he obeys—and apostolic blessing.

What your father, the count of distinguished valor [Note: [Col. 0123D] Raymond IV, called of St. Giles, is reported to have died in 1105 on the day before the Kalends of March [28 February].], did concerning the altar of St. Giles and concerning the whole borough, you yourself know well. We believe that you have either heard or seen the decree and excommunication issued at the Council of Nîmes by Pope Urban, of most holy memory, at your father’s request. We therefore wonder that you have presumed to invade the borough and to erect new fortifications beside the church of Blessed Giles. [Col. 0124A] Indeed, what is more serious, after receiving money, you put the offerings of the same altar up for sale as if they were common merchandise. We therefore admonish you as a beloved son not to allow yourself to remain burdened any longer with so grave a sin.

And even if, as is said, you have begun the journey to Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 0124D] Bertrand reached Palestine in 1109; but after his father’s death in 1105 he was already contemplating that journey.], it will profit your soul nothing, because you are bound by the bond of excommunication and anathema promulgated in that same Council of Nîmes. Otherwise you shall undoubtedly feel more severely the wrath and indignation of almighty God and of the holy apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of December [14 November].

## CVIII. To Bishop Rangerius and the canons of the Church of Lucca. (Within the years 1103–1104, 14 October.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1096.]

[Col. 0124B]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother and fellow bishop RANGER[IUS] and to the canons of the Church of Lucca, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have heard that Leo, bishop of the Apostolic See, of holy memory in Christ, decreed that if any canon of your church who was not living in community should die, all his ecclesiastical goods should be transferred for the use of the brethren living in community; and we know that the same has been established in other churches by other Roman pontiffs. We therefore wonder that, after your fellow brother Hildebrand was transferred to the Church of Roselle, his prebend and [Col. 0124C] the entire ecclesiastical benefice which he had held passed to private use, and that, in contempt of the authority of the Apostolic See, the community of brethren living canonically was deprived of so considerable an increase.

This fault is especially laid to your charge, dearest brother R., because you ought to have observed inviolably the decrees of the Apostolic See and to have invited your subject clerics, even against their will, to the good of this life. We therefore command that the entire benefice of Hildebrand, now bishop of Roselle, be restored to the common fund. Those who refuse to obey shall be punished by the judgment of the Apostolic See.

Given at the Lateran, on the eleventh Ides of October [15 October].

## CIX. To Lanuin, master of the hermitage of St. Mary of the Tower. (1104.)

[CAPIALBI, *Memoirs Serving the History of the Holy Church of Mileto*, compiled by Vito CAPIALBI. Naples, 1835, octavo, p. 143.]

[Col. 0124D]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LANUIN, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have repeatedly sent letters to the canons of the Church of Mileto concerning the celebration of a canonical election. Recently we ordered them to elect a suitable shepherd for themselves by the octave of the coming Easter; [Col. 0125A] if they delayed, we forbade them entry into the church. We therefore wish you to meet with them, the countess, and the worthy barons, and in our stead admonish them to elect a shepherd. But if, as hitherto, they prove contemptuous, forbid them altogether entry into the church until they make satisfaction, and, after taking counsel with the countess and the barons, conduct a canonical election.

Require the abbot of St. Julian to make satisfaction in your presence concerning the charges brought against him. If that monk who was formerly installed as abbot in the monastery of St. Euphemia [Note: [Col. 0125] Not only this monastery, but other monasteries of Calabria also, Pope Paschal entrusted to the care of Lanuin. See Mabillon, *Benedictine Annals*, book LXX, §§55–56.] refuses, after your admonition, to relinquish [variant: withdraw from] his occupation of that monastery, then, supported by our authority, subject him to excommunication. In all these matters we wish you diligently and fully to exercise our authority.

## CX. He receives under his protection the Church of the Holy Cross and Blessed Eulalia at Barcelona, and confirms its possessions and privileges. (1104, 27 January.)

[FLOREZ, *Sacred Spain*, XXIX, 465.]

[Col. 0125B]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ RAYMOND, provost of the church of Barcelona, dedicated in honor of the Holy Cross and Blessed Eulalia, and to his successors canonically appointed forever.

It befits us to grant assent to just vows and to give ear to just petitions, for though unworthy, by the Lord’s disposal we are placed as guardians and proclaimers of justice upon the lofty watchtower of the princes of the apostles, Peter and Paul. [Col. 0125C] Therefore, dearest son Raymond, assenting to the prayers of your devotion, we receive under the protection of the Apostolic See the canonical community of the Holy Cross and Blessed Eulalia, over which, by God’s favor, you are known to preside; and through it, with the Lord’s favor, we remove the burdens imposed by secular persons.

Accordingly, by this document of privilege we grant and confirm to you and to your successors canonically appointed, in perpetual right, all those things which the bishops of Barcelona, for the support of the common livelihood, or other faithful persons by lawful donations, are known to have conferred upon that canonical community. Among these we have judged it proper to specify by their own names: the church of St. Mary beside the sea; the church of St. Michael within Barcelona, with its appurtenances and freeholds; the church [Col. 0125D] of St. John of the Pine, with its appurtenances; the church of St. Vincent of Sarrià, with its appurtenances; the church of St. Cecilia; the church of St. Andrew of Palomar, with half of its tithes; the church of St. Mary of Badalona and of St. Columba of Gramenet; St. Saviour of Polinyà; St. Mary of Llinars; St. Saturninus of the hill of Sabadell; St. John of Senata; St. Mary of Ulpereras; freeholds in the city of Barcelona and in its suburb, territory, or county; likewise, freeholds in the bishopric of Girona and in the bishoprics of Vic and Urgell.

Moreover, whatever goods you now justly possess, or may in future be able justly and canonically to acquire by grants of pontiffs, liberality of princes, or offerings of the faithful, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. [Col. 0126A] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may disturb that canonical community, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, claim for personal use what has been unjustly given, diminish them, or harass it with rash vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Barcelona.

Furthermore, we establish that, as is known to have been instituted in ancient times and is contained in the books of that church, the brethren of your college shall never [Col. 0126B] exceed the number of forty. And because it is fitting for us to provide alike for present and future matters, we decree that no one may have authority to appoint there a canon beyond the prescribed number.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes amends by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be liable to severe vengeance. But upon all who observe what is right toward that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here [Col. 0126C] they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Written through the hand of Raynerius, regional scrivener and notary of the sacred palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Equitius, acting in place of the chancellor, on the sixth day before the Kalends of February [27 January], in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1104 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II.

## CXI. * He receives the monastery of Pegau under protection and confirms its privileges, imposing on the monks an annual payment of one gold piece. (1104, 30 January.)

[It survives, according to Jaffé, in SCHOETTGEN, *History of Count Wiprecht of Groitzsch*. Regensburg, 1749, octavo, documentary appendix, p. 4: “The desire which pertains to . . .”]

[Col. 0126D]

## CXII. Privilege for the monastery of Jesus of Nazareth. (1104, 23 March.)

[AYNSA, *Foundation of Huesca*, p. 455.]

Pope Paschal II, in the year 1102, among other things which he grants to the abbot of this royal house, confirms the donations made by Kings Don Sancho and Don Pedro, and likewise the agreement which he renewed between the bishop of Huesca and the abbot of Montearagón.

Its date is: At the Lateran, through the hand of John, cardinal of the Holy [Col. 0127A] Roman Church, on the second Ides of January [12 January], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1102 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

## CXIII. He orders Lambert, bishop of Arras, to judge before the feast day of the apostles Peter and Paul (29 June), together with John, bishop of Thérouanne, between Landfrid, abbot of St. Wilmar, and Heribert, deprived of that abbey by the count of Boulogne. (1104, 25 April.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, Luc[a] edition, II, 146.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

This brother, bearer of the present letter, came to us with letters from the chapter of Thérouanne, complaining that he was long ago expelled from the abbacy of his monastery by the hand of the count of Boulogne. But the brother who is said to preside over that monastery, when he was coming to us, was prevented by illness, as has been reported to us, and could not reach us. We therefore commit this case for examination by your brotherhood in our stead: taking with you our brother, the bishop of Thérouanne, examine more diligently the allegations of each abbot, and by the coming solemnity of the apostles Peter and Paul completely decide this business canonically, as justice dictates.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Kalends of May [25 April].

## CXIV. To the inhabitants of San Gimignano.—That their town and its territory may never be alienated from the possession of the Church of Volterra. (1104, 24 May.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1051.]

[Col. 0127C]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all clerics and laypeople of the castle of San Gimignano, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We must provide, by our enactment and by your observance, for the peace and stability of your Church. Therefore, by the ordinance of this present letter, we command all of you and order your successors to observe forever that you shall never, in any manner or under any pretext, permit your town called San Gimignano, together with the neighboring Mount Stafili and its entire territory, to be alienated [Col. 0127D] from the possession and ownership of the Church of Volterra. Rather, as it is today, so it shall always remain under the Church of Volterra’s own right.

Nor shall the bishop or any minister of that Church have authority to give, lease, sell, pledge, or transfer by exchange that town with the aforesaid mountain to any person as a fief. Neither margrave nor count nor any authority may seize that town or the aforementioned mountain, withdraw it from the Church’s authority, or alienate it under any pretext. As stated above, it shall always remain under the Church’s own right. If anyone presumes to act otherwise, both the person who does so and the person who consents shall be subject to excommunication. [Col. 0128A]

You should know that our brother Roger, bishop of the Church of Volterra, has consented to us in this provision of the present constitution, so that he himself asked, together with the brethren who accompanied him to us, that it be made, and himself subscribed it.

I, Roger, unworthy bishop of the Church of Volterra, asked that it be made and myself subscribed it.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, on the ninth day before the Kalends of June [24 May], in the second indiction, in the year 1104 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

## CXV. * He orders G[arcia], bishop of Burgos, to go to Astorga, where, in his presence, “five persons among the elders of the Church of Mondoñedo” are to swear that they “have possessed without disturbance for a period of forty years” the two archpresbyterates which the Church of Compostela claims for itself.

(1104, 1 October.—See the *History of Compostela* in FLOREZ, *Sacred Spain*, XX, 77.)

[Col. 0128B]

## CXVI. To the archbishops and bishops of the provinces of Reims, Sens, and Tours.—That they may absolve King Philip and his concubine from the bond of excommunication. (1104, 5 October.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1015.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers the archbishops and bishops throughout the provinces of Reims, Sens, and Tours, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0128C] We have been informed by letters from some of you that our son, the king of the Franks, has resolved, in accordance with our command, to renounce the woman on whose account he was so often admonished and indeed excommunicated; and that the woman herself is prepared to renounce the king. We have rejoiced greatly at the conversion of these persons, because, as the Lord Himself testifies, we know that there is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents.

You will remember that we committed this matter to our brother Richard, bishop of Albano. If, therefore, that brother has already left the borders of France, then, with the Lord’s help, we entrust this same matter, to be conducted together with you, to our venerable brother Lambert, bishop of Arras. Therefore, when you have assembled, if [Col. 0128D] our common son the king of the Franks and that woman at his side, having touched the most sacred Gospels, renounce every practice of carnal union, as well as mutual conversation and cohabitation, except under the testimony of persons wholly beyond suspicion, and declare that they will never return to the same offense—as has been signified in letters from some of you—then the bishop of Arras, together with you, shall receive their satisfaction in our stead and absolve them from the bond of excommunication. Thus, by the Lord’s gift, the Church may rejoice through episcopal ministry that her son is reconciled, and France that her king is reconciled to her.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, on the third Nones of October [5 October].

## CXVII. He receives under protection the monastery of St. Mary of Bornhem, and confirms its goods and privileges, at the request of Manasses, bishop of Cambrai. (1104, 11 October.)

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, I, 519.]

[Col. 0129A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Blessed Mary at Bornhem, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have graciously heard the petitions of your devotion, and at the request of Manasses, bishop of Cambrai, we have undertaken to cherish with the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Blessed Mary at Bornhem, in which you lead a regular life.

For we decree that whatever goods have been offered to that church by Wenemar of Ghent, founder of that place, [Col. 0129B] or by any of the faithful, or shall be offered in future, and likewise whatever has been granted by the concession of our venerable brother Manasses, bishop of Cambrai, shall be confirmed secure and entire.

Furthermore, whatever protection and liberty that same brother Manasses has bestowed upon your place and community, we confirm by the authority of this present decree. We forbid anyone to presume rashly to disturb that church, plunder its goods, or alienate them in any way, so that through the grace of God you may render with freer minds the duties of service owed to almighty God. If anyone, knowing the tenor of this decree, should rashly [Col. 0129C] attempt to act against it, let him be punished by the strict censure of the prince of the apostles Peter and of ourselves.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth Ides of October [11 October], in the thirteenth indiction, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

## CXVIII. * He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Göttweig. (1104, 24 October.)

[Of this privilege there survives only a mention in Jaffé, *Registers of the Roman Pontiffs*, p. 487, with this note: “Wattenbach supplied it.”]

## CXVIII bis. He confirms the possessions of the monastery of St. Blaise at Admont. (1104, 25 October.)

[PEZ, *Treasury of Anecdotes*, III, III, 659.]

[Col. 0129D]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable son HENRY, abbot of the venerable monastery called Admont, situated in the diocese of Salzburg, and to his successors regularly appointed forever.

The Lord commands through the prophet that the inhabitants of the land of the south meet the fugitive with bread. Therefore, dearest son Henry, we gladly receive you and your brethren, who have turned from the world to the service of almighty God and flee toward His face. This monastery, as is known, was built in the mountainous region of his diocese by Gebhard, bishop of Salzburg, of reverend memory, in honor and in the name of Blessed Blaise the martyr. [Col. 0130A] Therefore, by this document of privilege, we decree by apostolic authority that whatever goods or possessions belong today to that monastery—whether by lawful gifts of the aforesaid Bishop Gebhard, of his successor Tyemo, of equally happy memory, or of other faithful persons, or by any other right—or may in future be justly and canonically acquired by grants of pontiffs, liberality of princes, or offerings of the faithful, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with rash vexations. Rather, all things shall be kept entire, for the benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Salzburg. Yet he himself may by no means impose any vexation or custom harmful to the peace of the religious. [Col. 0130B] Neither the bishop, nor the abbot himself, nor any person may have authority to grant the goods of the monastery as a fief or benefice to any persons, even with the consent of the better brethren, or to alienate them by other means.

Moreover, we decree that the burial ground of that place shall be wholly free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wishes of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. Let no opposition of any bishop or provost hinder you from receiving secular laypeople or clerics into conversion. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be set over it through any cunning of deception or violence, except the person whom the brethren unanimously, or the sounder part of the brethren, elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. [Col. 0130C]

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes amends by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be liable to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right toward that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Written through the hand of Rainerius, regional scrivener and notary of the sacred palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of November [25 October], in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1105 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

## CXIX. He confirms the possessions and rights of the Church of St. Frigidianus at Lucca. (1104, 28 October.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, Luc[a] edition, IV, 583, from the manuscript codex of St. Frigidianus at Lucca.]

[Col. 0131A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, Rothon, provost, and his brethren professing the regular life in the church of Blessed Frigidianus, and to his successors professing the regular life in the same church, and to their successors remaining in the same religious observance forever.

Desire that is shown to pertain to a religious purpose and the salvation of souls ought, with God as author, to be fulfilled without delay. [Col. 0131B] Since therefore you, most dear sons in Christ, inspired by divine grace, have resolved to restrain your conduct under the discipline of the regular life and to serve almighty God together according to the institution of the holy Fathers, we rejoice with paternal affection at your wishes. We therefore grant your petition the assent due in kindness; for we confirm by the authority of this privilege the order of canonical life which you have professed. We forbid anyone, after making profession, to possess anything as private property or to leave the cloister without the permission of the undertaking or the community; and we fortify both you and all that is yours with the protection of the Apostolic See. [Col. 0131C] To you, therefore, and to your successors remaining in the same religious observance, we confirm in perpetual possession all things which, at present, you appear to possess for the maintenance of the common livelihood, whether by lawful donations of the bishops of the Church of Lucca or of other faithful persons, or by another reasonable title; and whatever you may hereafter be able to acquire justly and canonically through the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of princes, or the offerings of the faithful. Moreover, we grant and confirm by the sanction of this present decree that you and your successors persevering in the same religious observance may receive tithes from all parishioners of your church, free from the interference of any persons, and distribute them for canonical uses. For it is fitting that you reap, with the Apostle, their temporal goods among those for whom you sow spiritual goods.

[Col. 0131D] Upon the death of yourself, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any device of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren in counsel, fearing God, shall have provided for election, whether from their own community or, if expedient, from another community of regular discipline—saving the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Lucca, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See. We further declare that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb this monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support and government they were granted.

[Col. 0132A] If, indeed, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly attempting rashly to act against this document of our constitution, after a second or third warning fails to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the wrongdoing committed, be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who uphold justice for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional scriniary and notary of the sacred palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

[Col. 0132B] Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of November, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year 1105 [1104] of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

## CXX. Privilege for the monastery of St. Orientius at Auch. (A.D. 1104, October 29.)

[Dom Bouquet, *Recueil*, XIV, 322.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OTGERIUS, prior, and the other monks of St. Orientius: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We recognize that, by the Lord’s ordering, we have been raised to the service of the Apostolic See so that we ought effectively to assist its children when they seek aid, and, as the Lord grants, to defend and protect those obedient to it. [Col. 0132C] Therefore, out of love for our venerable brother Hugh, abbot of Cluny—to whose care your place belongs by right from the monastery of Cluny—and acceding to your prayers, most dear sons in Christ, we do not refuse your monastery the safeguard of our protection. [lacuna] Furthermore, following in the footsteps of our predecessors Leo and Urban II, we decree that the ancient establishment of your cemetery shall not be disturbed by the hostility of any adversaries whatsoever, but shall remain perpetually undisturbed, as was sanctioned by the authority of our most holy predecessor Leo IX. Accordingly, neither outside nor within the city may the archbishop of Auch and his canons establish a new cemetery; but archbishops, regular or irregular clerics, and laypeople, in accordance with the custom hitherto observed, shall in future obtain a place of burial with you, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of November, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year 1105 [1104] of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

## CXXI. He grants Bishop Didacus of Compostela the use of the pallium. (A.D. 1104, October 31.)

[Flórez, *España sagrada*, XX, 48.]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother DIDACUS, bishop of Compostela, of the Church of St. James: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0133A] The Western Church believes and venerates that the body of the apostle James was brought into the regions of Spain. His honour, indeed, in accordance with David’s prophecy—“But exceedingly honoured to me are thy friends, O God; exceedingly strengthened is their dominion”—has also, by God’s ordering, increased among men in succeeding times. The very place where those most sacred relics rest was first a rural settlement and then a town, which received the name Compostela. Soon thereafter, by the disposition of the Apostolic See, the episcopal see which had been in the nearby town of Iria was transferred to Compostela. Although it had itself been subject to the metropolitan church of Braga, it was soon granted such freedom that it became a special member of the Apostolic See. We too, [Col. 0133B] considering so great a favour of our predecessors, have judged that the requests of our son Alfonso, the illustrious king—through whose agency the place of that apostle has been greatly enlarged in our times—and of the clergy of Compostela should be granted, by adorning that Church with the honour of the pallium on account of so great an apostle.

Therefore, most dear brother in Christ Didacus, bishop of the city of Compostela, we grant you the dignity of the pallium from the liberality of the Apostolic See, so that you may recognize that you and your Church are always more greatly indebted to that same Apostolic See. You shall understand that you may use it only within the church, for the celebration of the solemnities of Mass, on the days designated below: the Nativity of the Lord, Epiphany, the Annunciation of the Lord, the Lord’s Supper, Palm Sunday, Easter, Ascension, Pentecost, the three feasts of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, the feast of St. Michael, the Nativity of St. John the Baptist, the solemnity of Blessed James and of the other apostles, the Commemoration of All Saints, dedications of churches, and also the feasts of the martyrs St. Lawrence and St. Vincent, and of the confessors Martin and Isidore.

[Col. 0133C] Since the honour of this garment must be maintained by the modest vigour of one’s conduct, we exhort you to make the adornments of your morals correspond to it, so that, with God as author, you may rightly be conspicuous in both respects. Therefore, most dear brother, bound by the duty of pastoral care, love the brethren; let even adversaries, because of the Lord’s commandment, be joined to you by affection toward you. Pursue peace with all, and holiness, without which no one shall see God. Devote yourself to pious works; abound in virtues. Let the breastplate of judgment shine upon your breast, joined to the shoulder-piece of action. Thus proceed before God and the whole Church that you may provide examples for the flock entrusted to you, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven. Let truthful speech be on your tongue, and fervour of zeal in your soul. Cultivate the Lord’s field entrusted to you while you may; sow in fear while there is time; do not cease from doing good, for in due time you shall reap if you do not fail.

[Col. 0133D] Therefore, vigilantly abandoning earthly affairs, strive after heavenly things. Forgetting what lies behind, stretch yourself more earnestly toward what lies before. Let not your mind be dissipated amid secular variety, but let it run and flow wholly into one. Look to the end, which David beheld with wonderful sweetness when he said: “One thing have I asked of the Lord; this will I seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.” May the Holy Trinity surround your brotherhood with the protection of its glory and grant you to attain the end that has no end.

[Col. 0134A] Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of November, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year 1104 from the Lord’s Nativity.

## CXXII. To princes, knights, and other laypeople throughout Spain and Galicia—Concerning an unlawful union. (A.D. 1104, October 31.)

[Flórez, *España sagrada*, XX, 90.]

[Col. 0134B]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to princes, knights, and other laypeople throughout Spain and Galicia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

A very grave and horrifying crime is reported from your regions. For not only, as the prophet says, does “blood touch blood,” but, under the appearance of receiving penance, certain persons are said voluntarily to be promoters of this wickedness, as though a way of penance lay open to those remaining in the crime; while some, nevertheless, commonly invent sins against persons who resist them. But to offend God in hope of penance is to deny oneself access to penance. Therefore, whoever join their sons or daughters in incestuous marriages should know themselves bound by the same guilt as those who are joined [Col. 0134C] in marriage, unless, setting aside deceit, they take care with sincere intent to dissolve those unions, insofar as their means allow. Therefore, lest such things happen in future, we forbid them by every means and command our brother bishops to suppress them completely.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of November.

## CXXIII. Privilege for the monastery of Usenhofen. (A.D. 1104, November 7.)

[*Monumenta Boica*. Munich, 1763, quarto, vol. X, p. 439.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable son HERCHENBALD, abbot of Usenhofen, and to his successors to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0134D] To those inhabiting the land of the South, the Lord commanded through the prophet to meet fugitives with bread. Therefore we gladly receive you, most dear sons in Christ, fleeing from the world, and cherish you through the grace of the Holy Spirit under the protection of the Apostolic See. We decree that your community shall remain forever at the place of Usenhofen; and that whatever estates or goods Counts Berthold and Otto, or Azecha of good memory in Christ, together with her two sons, Counts Bernard and Eckhard, are known to have offered for the salvation of their souls to blessed Peter, by whose name your place is distinguished, and to your community; and whatever you may hereafter be able to acquire justly and canonically by grants of pontiffs, the liberality of princes, or the offerings of the faithful, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors.

[Col. 0135A] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb this monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support and government they were granted. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars and churches, and ordinations of monks to be promoted to sacred orders from the bishop in whose diocese you are, provided that he enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide these things freely and without abuse. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration; supported by the authority of the Apostolic See, he shall grant what you have requested.

[Col. 0135B] Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any device of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or the sounder part of the brethren, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall choose from their own community or, if necessary, from another community. Moreover, we decree that the burial-place of your house shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. We grant you as advocate the aforesaid Count Berthold, or after him Otto, son of Otto, whichever one you choose in preference.

[Col. 0135C] Yet neither they nor any others may claim the advocacy of the place as hereditary. Otherwise, let the abbot and brethren, by the authority of the Apostolic See, appoint whom they judge more useful to the monastery. If in future any archbishop or bishop, emperor or king, prince or duke, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly attempts rashly to act against this document of our constitution, after a second or third warning fails to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the wrongdoing committed, be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, [Col. 0135D] and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who uphold justice for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional scriniary and notary of the sacred palace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of November, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year 1104 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

## CXXIV. He confirms the privileges and possessions of the collegiate church of St. Amatus at Douai. (A.D. 1104, November 10.)

[Miraeus, *Opera diplomatica*, II, 1361.]

[Col. 0136A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to HERIBERT, dean, and his brethren serving the Lord in the church of St. Mary and St. Amatus at Douai, in perpetuity.

As no effect should be granted to those demanding unjust things, so the petition of those desiring lawful things should not be delayed. Therefore, considering your lawful desires, and at the request of our fellow-brother Lambert, venerable bishop of Arras, we grant your prayers our paternal assent, so that [Col. 0136B] your church, situated in the diocese of Arras, may be protected by the guardianship of the Apostolic See.

Therefore, through the document of this present privilege, by apostolic authority we confirm to your church of St. Amatus at Douai those possessions which appear presently to belong to that same church by the lawful donations of the illustrious Duke Macerontus or of other faithful persons:

Namely, in the district of Mempisque, Tatem; Macrivilla, with its altar, the tithe of the entire village, and all its appurtenances; in the same village, a church in honour of St. Amatus, wholly free; the canons’ court, wholly free, on the River Escrae; the entire village of Fleterna with its tithe; at Gunevelt, half a sheepfold; among the Heldenses, that tithe [Col. 0136C] which lies between Neppa and Guarnama, together with the swine-right called *becca* and the authority of Guarnestum.

At Bonennias near Abartianas, the entire tithe belonging to the body of the church. Whatever else the aforesaid church of Blessed Mary and St. Amatus justly possesses today, and whatever it may hereafter be able to acquire lawfully and canonically by grants of pontiffs, the liberality of princes, or offerings of the faithful, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors.

No dean or provost shall be placed over your college except one who has been canonically provided, in the fear of God, by the due consent either of all the brethren or of the better part of them.

The bishop shall commit the care of the church to the dean; [Col. 0136D] yet he may not burden that church or impose any exactions or customary dues upon it.

The canons and all other clerics serving that same church shall be corrected under the dean’s discipline; nor may they be admitted to ordination by the bishop without his permission, nor restrained at the discretion of anyone other than himself and the brethren.

Furthermore, neither the dean nor the provost shall have power, without the common or sounder counsel of the brethren, to give the church’s goods in fief, dispose of prebends or other offices, or establish anything of greater consequence concerning the church’s property.

We also command that the precinct, cloister, and residences of the canons within the castle be kept free from every secular power, so that neither in them nor [Col. 0137A] in their property or servants may a hand be laid against their will.

As you possess, by the grant of Bishop Gerard of revered memory, the power to excommunicate, after canonical warning, invaders and plunderers of your property if they do not make satisfaction, so we grant you that power also for the future. No one in the province shall receive those expressly named before they have made satisfaction, saving in all respects the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Arras. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, oil for the sick, and water for reconciling the cemetery, precinct, or churches from the mother church of Arras, with every abuse removed.

Moreover, we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, [Col. 0137B] take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support and government they were granted, saving, as stated, the canonical reverence due to the aforesaid bishop of Arras.

If, indeed, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly attempting rashly to act against this document of our constitution, after a second or third warning fails to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the wrongdoing committed, be excluded from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, [Col. 0137C] and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance.

But upon all who uphold justice for that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and, before the strict Judge, obtain the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, scriniary and notary of the sacred palace.

+ I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of November, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year one thousand one hundred and four of the Lord’s Nativity, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

## CXXV. To Lanuinus, master of the hermitage of St. Mary of the Tower. (A.D. 1104.)

[CapiAlbi, *Memorie della Chiesa Miletese*, p. 144.]

[Col. 0137D]

PASCHAL, etc., to his beloved son LANUINUS, etc.

Know that we greatly rejoice at the promotion of Brother Hugh and at the expulsion of the abbot of St. Julian, because almighty God has provided the former for the monastery of St. Euphemia, which has now for two years been deprived of an abbot’s assistance, and has removed the latter from his occupation of that place. [Col. 0138A] Take care, therefore, son, that an abbot be chosen for the monastery of St. Julian according to the Rule of blessed Benedict; by the Lord’s grace, you shall send him to us for consecration. Even if our brethren have protested, we shall by no means allow the rights of St. Peter to be diminished. We greet in the Lord your brethren who dwell with you in the hermitage, and earnestly exhort them to remain in charity. We more diligently commend ourselves to your and their prayers. Take such care for the affairs of St. Peter as you know to be expedient.

[Note: [Col. 0137D] The abbey of St. Julian, situated in Calabria, is the same one recalled in various bulls in Ughelli and in various diplomas. St. Euphemia’s too was in Calabria, and later became famous for the many bishops whom it gave especially to the Churches of [Col. 0138D] Sicily. For both, see Lubin, *Abbatiarum Italiae brevis notitia* [A Brief Account of the Abbeys of Italy], the Benedictine Annals of the celebrated Father Mabillon, and the writers on our native affairs.]

## CXXVI. *He sends the pallium to Ascer, archbishop of Lund and primate of Luccia. (A.D. 1104.)

[Only a notice of this bull survives in the *Chronicle of the Bishops of Lund*, in Langebek, *Scriptores Rerum Danicarum* [Writers on Danish Affairs]. Copenhagen, 1772, folio, vol. VI, p. 623.]

[Col. 0138B]

## CXXVII. He writes to Manasses, archbishop of Reims, concerning the abbot of St. Medard, accused of simony by a knight hostile to him. (Between A.D. 1100 and 1105, March 29.)

[Baluze, *Miscellanea*, II, 149.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother and fellow bishop MANASSES of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Your affection had informed us that the abbot of St. Medard, unexpectedly accused of simony in the council of his provincial bishops by a certain knight, had been adjudged bound to clear himself by an oath with six compurgators. He afterwards came to [Col. 0138C] us and complained that he had been treated unfairly in that case, because an accusation by a single person, long his enemy, had been admitted against him without the corroboration of any witnesses. In this matter we greatly wonder at the provision made by your wisdom. For although ecclesiastical custom permits even persons of an inferior fitness, of whatever rank, to bring accusations of the crime of simony, who would dare to disregard the saying of the divine mouth: “One witness shall not stand against anyone, whatever the sin or crime may be; but every word shall stand on the testimony of two or three witnesses”? Moreover, concerning those who were enemies the day before yesterday and three days ago, one and the same determination of the Fathers applies in every case.

Therefore, even if the same abbot is judged less than upright in other aspects of his conduct, in this matter, where no witness at all is said to have appeared, we judge it sufficient, solely because of the stigma of an ineffective accusation, that he clear himself by an oath with six compurgators—unless witnesses of that crime should emerge.

[Col. 0138D] Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.

## CXXVIII. To Abbot Stephen and the monks of St. Giles—He announces that he will excommunicate Count Bertrand of Toulouse and certain of his knights unless they desist from wrongs inflicted upon the monastery. (A.D. 1105, April 15.)

[Dom Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 39.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son STEPHEN, [Note: [Col. 0139D] Stephen died in 1105 or the following year, since in 1106 he had as successor Hugh, to whom Paschal granted a bull, dated at [Col. 0140D] Parma on the fourth day before the Nones of November, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1106 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.] abbot, and the monks of St. Giles: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We had greatly commended the good which Count Bertrand had done from the offerings of the altar of St. Giles; but we are more deeply troubled because, while almost all the possessions of St. Giles are said to have been put under pledge on account of the contumacy of certain persons, the same Count Bertrand and some of his knights are attempting to seize those very offerings. Moreover, they are now inflicting many injuries upon your monastery. By these present letters we announce to them that, [Col. 0139B] unless they desist, we shall subject them to excommunication.

Given on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May.

## CXXIX. To the monks and other faithful of St. Giles—No one may presume, against the abbot’s will, to alienate or defraud anything from the altar offerings. (A.D. 1105, October 31.)

[Dom Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 32.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the monks and other faithful of St. Giles: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since great things fall apart through discord and small things grow strong through concord, we admonish you and command you, while entreating you, to love your abbot in one mind and one feeling, fearing him; to fear him while loving him; and, persisting in obedience to him, to preserve the property of the monastery more diligently. This property is known to have been much scattered and ruined, partly by your factions and partly by military violence. By the obedience due to the holy apostles, we forbid anyone to presume to seize the altar offerings, alienate them against the abbot’s will, or defraud them; rather, let them be kept in the fear of the Lord for the uses for which they have been or are to be given. But if any perhaps presume otherwise, we exclude both those acting and those consenting from the thresholds of the Church.

[Col. 0139C] Given on the second day before the Kalends of November.
