We therefore confirm by the authority of this present decree, through the Lord’s bounty, to you and your successors all things lawfully belonging to it: namely, in the diocese of Thérouanne, adjoining the same monastery, the church of Saint Margaret [Note: [Col. 0243D] Abbot Lambert granted this church of Blessed Margaret to a certain cleric, Gunzelin, in return for an annual rent of sixteen pounds, payable at fixed terms. [Col. 0244D] In the margin of the manuscript.], the church of Saint John, that of Saint Martin, the church of Herbel(a), the church of Peternesse, and the church of Torbodeshem, free, as in former times, from every episcopal payment.

We also confirm to you the church of Broburg with its chapels; the churches of Graveninga and Lo; the church of Arkes with the same village; the church of Poperingehem with the same village; the church of Stenkerka; the church of Brusele; the church of Scales; the church of Boveringhem with their villages; the villages of Aldenfort, Ostresela, and Rokestor, with the land which you bought from Arnold of Wenti and the other adjacent lands; the allod which Clarenbald gave in the village of Lustingehem; the church of Coieka and the church of Helcin with their villages, and a share of the church of Walnas; the churches of Locanes and Aquina; the church of Hunela with the same village; and the altar of Merchem, which the venerable Bishop John granted to you.

In the diocese of Noyon, Kanetecurtin. In the diocese of Tournai [Note: [Col. 0244D] Read, as in Miraeus: “of Tournai.”], the church of Rokeshem, the church of Hetlingehem, that of Hitlingehem, that of Westkerke, and the tithe of Clemeskerke; in the diocese of Cologne, the church [Col. 0244C] of Frekena and the church of Gildestorp with their appurtenances. From these we command that no levy whatsoever, under any pretext, be exacted by bishops or their officers, saving the bishops’ annual dues.

We likewise confirm the church of Coclers, which Baldric, bishop of the church of Tournai, granted to you and your successors to administer, together with the altar of Rusletha, free from every exaction except ten solidi in coin, which are paid annually from Rusletha to the bishop. Furthermore, we grant that the appointment of an abbot at the monastery of Saint Silvin at Alciacum shall always remain in your disposition, according to the custom of former times.

We absolutely forbid public episcopal visitations to be held among you; nor may the bishop come there more frequently, unless summoned by the abbot, lest any occasion for popular gatherings be afforded in the retreats of God’s servants and lest simpler minds be drawn thereby, as God forbid, into scandal. We decree that in all your parishes no one may presume, against your will, to build a church or monastery, or to retain possession of one already built. No priest or cleric may remain in your churches or chapels, by his own initiative or through another’s compulsion, without your consent, or assume any office there. But if it should happen, God forbid, that the bishop of your diocese is not catholic or does not enjoy the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, we permit your brethren, for the purpose of ordination, to resort to a catholic bishop, and, under a general interdict of the diocese, to celebrate the divine offices secretly behind closed doors.

Finally, we confirm to your church by this present decree the whole area of the enclosure which lies on every side of your basilica as far as the middle course of the river Agnion, together with the fisheries of Mera and Grath, Mardic and Strangnerh, and Laugha, and the adjacent cultivated and uncultivated lands, as you possessed them in ancient times.

Let no one, therefore, be permitted rashly to disturb this monastery or, under any pretext, to take away anything which belongs or shall belong to it; but let all things be preserved intact, to be of every benefit for the use of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, then, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 0245C] Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional scriniary and notary of the Sacred Palace.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of John, deacon-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of June, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1107, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II [Note: [Col. 0245D] More correctly, the eighth.].

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

CCLX. To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He promises to provide for the privilege of the Church of Canterbury. (1108, 12 October.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1023.]

[Col. 0245D]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother ANSELM, Archbishop of Canterbury: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the letters of your affection, through which we have recognised the sweetness of your gracious manner. You acted well and wisely in rendering us forewarned and cautious concerning the cause and honour of the Church of Canterbury. For in you we reverently behold the person of Blessed Augustine, apostle of the English; and therefore we utterly shrink from detracting from your honour or that of your church. Accordingly, we have willingly received what you requested, and, for preserving your honour and that of your church, [Col. 0246A] we apply our protection and concern.

Moreover, as to what you stated in those letters—that some are scandalised because we tolerate the German king’s granting of investitures of churches—know that we have never tolerated it and will never tolerate it. We await the taming of the fierceness of that nation. But if the king persists in the path of his father’s wickedness, he will without doubt experience the sword of Blessed Peter, which we have already begun to draw.

Given at Benevento, on the fourth day before the Ides of October.

CCLXI. Privilege for the monastery of Selbold. (1108, 16 October.)

[WENCK, *Hessische Landesgeschichte*. Darmstadt and Giessen, 1783, 4to, II, 57.]

[Col. 0246B] PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son DIEDMAR, illustrious count: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We ought not merely to favour the good undertakings of laymen, but also to invite their minds to such works, since in virtue of our office we provide for their salvation. Therefore, beloved son in Christ, Count Dietmar, we have taken note of your devotion: at the church called that of Saint John the Baptist, situated in the place called Selboldt, you propose to gather regular canons, both for the soul of your deceased wife and as a remedy for the sins of yourself, your family, and those who belong to you. Through the ministry of the religious priest Robenuld, you have devoutly and faithfully offered that church to Blessed Peter and to the holy Roman Church itself.

[Col. 0246C] Therefore, receiving both that church and the brethren to be gathered there under the protection of the Apostolic See, we decree that the brethren to be gathered there shall live in perpetuity according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine. We also decree that whatever possessions that church now lawfully possesses, or shall in future lawfully possess, by the Lord’s grant, through your gift or that of any other faithful persons, shall always be kept firm and whole, for the benefit of the clerics serving God there. Therefore no bishop, cleric, king, or prince, nor any one of your successors, may have licence rashly to disturb that church or, under any pretext, to take away anything which is or shall be its own.

Moreover, as a token of the liberty thus received from the Roman Church, the clerics of that church shall pay one gold coin each year to the Lateran Palace. But if anyone, God forbid, having learned the tenor of this decree, should rashly attempt to oppose it, let him suffer loss of his honour and office unless he corrects his presumption by fitting satisfaction.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Benevento through the hand of Leo, deacon-cardinal of the Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November, in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1108, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

CCLXII. To D[idacus], Bishop of Compostela.—No one is to celebrate Mass upon the altar of Blessed James except bishops or the seven cardinals. (1108, 30 October.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 93.]

[Col. 0247A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother D., bishop of the see of Compostela: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The impulse of pious intention ought to be fostered by supporting zeal, so that ecclesiastical advantage may receive strength and increase through the favour of the Apostolic See. Your fraternity has informed us that, in accordance with the custom of the Roman Church, you have ordained seven cardinal-priests in your church, so that they may administer in succession the offices of the Mass at the altar of Blessed James; and you request that this be secured by the protection of our letters.

We therefore assent to the petitions of your affection and confirm your arrangement by these present letters and apostolic authority, decreeing that this established number of priests may be neither diminished nor changed by you or by any of your successors; and that the solemn rites of Mass upon the altar of Blessed James shall be celebrated by no other person than the aforesaid priests, bishops, or legates of the Roman Church.

Given at Benevento, on the third day before the Kalends of November.

CCLXIII. He confirms the exemption of the Church of Burgos and the boundaries established for it in a council. (1108, 8 November.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XXVI, 466.]

[Col. 0247C]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GARCIA, bishop of Burgos, and to his successors to be canonically promoted in perpetuity.

The writings and monuments of the distinguished pontiffs and martyrs who shone in them testify that certain cities in Spain once flourished with the high rank of episcopal dignity. Among these, the church of Oca had been raised to the dignity of an episcopal see. We have learned from trustworthy reports that it was afterwards occupied for many years by the Moors or Ishmaelites.

[Col. 0247D] But since in our own times it has pleased almighty God that the same church should be restored at Burgos by the illustrious King Ildefonsus, and that episcopal dignity should be restored to it—something which our predecessor Pope Urban, of venerable memory, also confirmed by the authority of his privilege—we therefore command that those boundaries of the same church, concerning which a dispute was pending between you and the bishop of Osma, shall, as we have learned from the brethren and fellow bishops of that land whom we ordered to investigate them, remain forever subject, without any challenge, to the parochial jurisdiction of you and your successors. They are: Canatanazor, Murellum, Arganza, Mesela, Speia, Congosto, Buezo; and also, beyond the river Duero, the castle of Maderolum and Bozikellas as far as the public city of [Col. 0248A] Septi, together with all places lying on this side of the aforesaid boundaries.

Furthermore, since the metropolitan see of Tarragona, in whose diocese the Church of Oca is known to have been, has been so ruined by barbarian attacks that no one can inhabit it, we decree, out of singular love for the Church of Burgos, that both you and your successors shall be subject to no metropolitan except the Roman pontiff. And just as your fraternity is known to have been advanced to episcopal government by our aforesaid predecessor, so all who hereafter succeed in the same see shall be consecrated by the hand of the Roman pontiff as special suffragans of the Roman See.

If, then, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Benevento through the hand of Leo, deacon-cardinal of the Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of November, in the [Col. 0248C] first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1108, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

CCLXIII *bis*. He confirms the boundaries and liberty of the Church of Burgos. (1108, 12 November.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XXVI, 466.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GARSIA, bishop of Burgos, and to his successors to be canonically promoted in perpetuity.

The writings and monuments of the distinguished pontiffs and martyrs who shone in them testify that certain cities in Spain once flourished with the high rank of episcopal dignity. Among these, the church of Oca had been raised to the dignity [Col. 0248D] of an episcopal see. We have learned from the legally attested report of certain persons that it was occupied many years afterward by the Moors or Ishmaelites. Yet in our own times it has pleased almighty God that the same church should be restored in the city of Burgos by the illustrious King Ildefonsus, and that episcopal dignity should be restored to it; this, indeed, our predecessor Pope Urban, of venerable memory, confirmed by the authority of his privilege.

We have learned from our brother bishops of that land, whom we had ordered to investigate the matter, that the following boundaries of that diocese, concerning which a dispute was pending between you and the bishop of Osma, belong to the possession of the Church of Burgos. Therefore we decree that they shall remain forever, by parochial right and without any challenge, subject to the jurisdiction of you and your successors: Canathanozor, Murelum, Airhunza, Messella, Speia, Congosto, Buezo; and also, beyond the river Duero, the castle of Madiolum and Bocigelas as far as the city of Septempublica, together with all places lying within the aforesaid boundaries.

Furthermore, since the metropolitan see of Tarragona, in whose diocese the Church of Oca is known to have been, has been so destroyed by barbarian attacks that no one dares inhabit it, we too, as was established by our aforementioned predecessor, bishop of the Apostolic See, enact by the authority of this present decree that both you and your successors shall be subject to no metropolitan except the Roman pontiff. And just as your fraternity is known to have been promoted by that same predecessor to the dignity of episcopal office, so all who hereafter succeed in the same see shall be consecrated by the hand of the Roman pontiff as special suffragans of the Roman See.

If, then, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here [Col. 0249C] the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional *scriniarius* [registrarial officer] and notary of the Sacred Palace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of November, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1109, in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

CCLXIV. To Henry, King of the English.—On the same subject. The king’s letter to which he replies has been lost. (1108, 21 November.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1064.]

[Col. 0249D]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ HENRY, glorious king of the English: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We give thanks to almighty God, who has established you as such a king in our times: one who wisely governs an earthly kingdom to God’s honour and bears before the eyes of his mind concern for the eternal King. In a letter you asked us that a new bishopric be established by apostolic authority in the place called Ely, because, as you said, the bishopric of Lincoln is so extensive that one bishop cannot possibly suffice to perform the duties of the episcopal office.

For this we praise the devotion of your purpose and give assent to your arrangement, provided that it be established in a distinguished place, lest the name of bishop, God forbid, be diminished in esteem. For a bishop is appointed so that he may teach the people of God by word, form them by life, and bring to the Lord, the true shepherd, the gain of the souls entrusted to him.

In the other matters about which you asked, although certain things there appear disordered, we are nevertheless in no way able to oppose your will. Moreover, your Highness knows that Lord Hervey, a bishop commended in no small degree by life and learning, was driven from his see by the excessive savagery and persecution of barbarians, and was put to flight amid great slaughter of the faithful and his brethren. We desire and request that, if any vacant church among you calls him, he be established there by apostolic authority, so that his learning may bring forth imperishable fruit and his life may offer the people of God a good example, and so that one who bears in his learning and character the lessons of heavenly life may not languish long in unfruitful silence.

May almighty God, through the prayers of His apostles, preserve both you and your offspring and grant you the heavenly kingdom after the earthly one.

Given on the eleventh day before the Kalends of December.

CCLXV. To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He grants what Anselm had requested. (1108.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1064.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0250C] brother Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, and the other bishops of the same province: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The writings of the Apostolic See and the sequence of English histories make clear that, among the other kingdoms of the earth, the kingdom of the English belongs in a special manner to the affection and obedience of the Apostolic See. This reason indeed more strongly moves our concern to foster the churches of that kingdom more intimately and to watch more carefully over their administration.

From the letters of our son the king and of you, we have learned that the bishopric of Lincoln is so extensive that one bishop cannot possibly suffice for the performance of episcopal duties. Therefore our dearest son and most Christian King Henry of the English asks us, with the consent of the bishop of Lincoln, that by permission of the Apostolic See a new bishopric be established in one part of his bishopric, namely in the place called Ely. Since his petitions appeared religious, we have willingly given our consent and grant, by apostolic authority, permission to establish a bishopric in the aforesaid place, decreeing that the episcopal see established in that place shall endure for all time hereafter. Let it also possess in perpetuity the diocese which your fraternity, together with the aforesaid brother bishop of Lincoln and under the king’s direction, shall assign to that bishopric.

Moreover, with regard to the monastery in which the episcopal see is established, the custom shall be observed of English monasteries in which bishops have been appointed. May the guardians of this constitution enjoy forever the blessing of almighty God and His apostles. Amen.

CCLXVI. He exhorts Ildefonsus, king of the Spaniards, not to allow the dioceses of churches, confirmed by Roman pontiffs, to be thrown into confusion. (Between 1099 and 1108.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XLVI, 246.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ILDEFONSUS, king of the Spaniards: greeting and apostolic blessing.

During your rule many evils and many dangers have occurred in the kingdom of Spain. Therefore scandals in the kingdom ought not to be added to scandals in the Church. Accordingly, we admonish your nobility not to allow, through the presumption of any persons, the boundaries of the churches—which were delineated by kings of glorious memory, your father and brother, and confirmed by the Roman Church—to be confused. For we desire that the diocese of the Church of Huesca or Barbastro be preserved wholly peaceful and intact, as defined by their documents and by our privileges. But whoever presumes anything to the contrary shall incur the indignation of the Apostolic See.

CCLXVII. He commands the Bishop of Huesca to make satisfaction to the Bishop of Barbastro for the injuries inflicted. (Between 1099 and 1108.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XLVI, 246.]

[Col. 0251C]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother, the Bishop of Huesca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Brother, you have lifted your mouth to heaven while despising the ordinances of the Apostolic See, and have instructed the people of Barbastro not to render what was due to their bishop. This is indeed to plunder episcopal rights and trample Roman privileges underfoot. Furthermore, invading the house of the bishop of Barbastro, you dispersed the goods kept there, and on solemn days carried off by armed force booty from the little estate of the church. When warned about these things by that bishop, you scorned to restore his own property; moreover, you attempted to stir up the king against him and received into fellowship a knight whom he had excommunicated.

We therefore command that, within two months after receiving these present letters, you make satisfaction to the aforesaid bishop and henceforth wholly desist from this presumption. Otherwise, until you make satisfaction, we prohibit you from exercising episcopal and priestly office.

CCLXVIII. To Baldric, Archbishop of Dol.—Privilege concerning the pallium of Baldric, Archbishop of Dol. (1109.)

[MARTENE, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, 883.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0252A] brother B. [BALDRIC], Archbishop of Dol.

If shepherds of sheep, intent day and night in sun and frost upon protecting their flock, keep watch with ever-vigilant eyes lest any sheep perish by straying or fail when torn by the bites of wild beasts, how much toil and how great a care ought to keep us wakeful, who are called shepherds of souls. Let us therefore take heed that we do not cease to fulfil the office undertaken for the guarding of the Lord’s sheep, lest on the day of divine examination the charge of negligence torment us before the supreme Judge because of our idleness—the very charge from which we are now judged more exalted than others by reason of the reverence paid to our office.

We grant to your fraternity the pallium, according to custom, for celebrating the solemnities of Mass, as it was granted to your predecessors: namely, at the Nativity of the Lord; the Octave of the Lord; the Purification and other feasts of Holy Mary; Palm Sunday; the Lord’s Supper; Holy Saturday; the Sunday of the Resurrection; the Octave of Easter; the Ascension of the Lord; Pentecost; the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist; the feast day of all the apostles; the feasts of Saint Lawrence and Saint Maurice; the feast of Saint Michael; All Saints; Saint Martin; the feasts of your saints whose bodies are kept among you; at the dedication of churches; on your anniversary; and when you conduct ordinations.

Finally, we exhort your charity that the habits of your life may correspond to so great an honour, so that by God’s help you may be conspicuous in example and word. Let your life therefore be a rule for your children, so that whatever strength is discerned in them may be directed by it. Let neither prosperity, which flatters only for a time, exalt your heart, nor adversity cast it down; rather, whatever may occur, let it be overcome by purity of virtue.

Let hatred find no place with you, nor undiscriminating favour. Let the just … of your sacred blessing [the text is defective] ensure that no exercise of judgment is sullied by any intrusion of venality. Let there be in you both the gentleness of the good shepherd and the stern rigor of the judge: the one to cherish those living innocently; the other to restrain the restless from wickedness. Show yourself merciful to the poor as virtue permits; let your protection aid the oppressed; let measured reason oppose oppressors. Accept no person against justice; despise none who seeks what is just. Let the guardianship of your life excel in equity, so that neither the rich, by their power, may persuade you to heed anything outside the path of reason, nor the poor, by their lowliness, make himself despair of you. Thus, by God’s mercy, may you be such as sacred reading commands when it says: “A bishop must be blameless.”

You will be able to employ all these things beneficially if you have charity as your teacher; whoever follows it does not depart from the straight path. But behold, dearest brother: among many other matters, these are the duties of priesthood, these the duties of the pallium; if you observe them diligently, you will possess inwardly what you show outwardly that you have received.

May the Holy Trinity surround your fraternity with the protection of its grace and direct us in the way of its fear, so that after the bitterness of this life we may together deserve to attain eternal sweetness.

CCLXIX. To the suffragans, clergy, and people of Dol.—He grants the pallium to Baldric, Archbishop of Dol. (1109.)

[MARTENE, *ibid.*, 882.]

[Col. 0253A]

As we have learned from certain persons, iniquity now so abounds in your regions that the Christian religion appears to have wholly perished there; and, what we cannot say without grief, not only laypeople but even clerics and monks, plunging into forbidden and unlawful acts, do not fear to commit deeds hateful to God and humankind. Therefore we sent our venerable brother Girard, bishop of Angoulême, into your regions, so that there, by the Lord’s grant, he might correct what needed correction and establish what needed establishing.

[Col. 0253B] As we have learned from his letters, in order that he might be able to exclude the aforesaid iniquities and impieties from your regions, he ordained our venerable brother [Note: [Col. 0253D] Concerning him Orderic Vitalis, *Ecclesiastical History*, book IX, has the following: “He was a citizen of Orléans, a monk and abbot of Bourgueil, trained in the liberal studies and venerable for the merits of his religious life; thence, because of his religious devotion and wisdom, he was advanced by ecclesiastical election to the rank of the archbishopric of Dol. In his episcopate he maintained monastic life and, as opportunity allowed, often lived with the monks,” etc. [Col. 0254D]] Baldric as fellow bishop in the Church of Dol.

Therefore, because of so great and urgent a necessity, we have granted the pallium—that is, the fullness of the pontificate—to our venerable brother Baldric, Archbishop of Dol, in order that he may use it according to the custom of his predecessors. We command your affection, therefore, to fear him as a father, obey him as a teacher, and diligently love him as the shepherd of your souls, so that through his admonitions and prayers the honour of your church may be increased, the Christian religion restored, and, once restored, preserved with the Lord’s help.

CCLXX. *He confirms the possessions and rights of the Church of Saint Frigdianus of Lucca.*

(1109, 7 March.—See *Bullarium Lateranense*, no. 4.)

[Col. 0253C]

CCLXXI. He commands the catholic brethren of the Church of Verdun to avoid Richard, the excommunicated bishop, etc. (1109, 18 March.)

[*Spicilegium*, ed. de La Barre, II, 248.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the catholic brethren of the Church of Verdun: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although you may not hitherto have read that Richard, the usurper of your church, has been excommunicated by the holy Roman Church on account of his deeds, we nevertheless believe that you have certainly heard and known it. Now, however, we announce it to you in writing, so that, knowing him to be excommunicated, you may avoid all communion with him.

We have further learned that the abbot of Saint Vito and Archdeacon Guy have, because of their attachment to Catholic unity, been deprived of both their dignities and their possessions. Therefore, if you have any obedience toward Blessed Peter and toward us, we command that they be restored to their positions and goods. But if you scorn to obey these present letters, we place your church under interdict from the divine offices. Those, however, who repent of the stain of this error shall be reconciled to Catholic unity by the counsel of our brother, the Archbishop of Trier, or of the aforesaid abbot. Know also that the aforementioned Guy has been ordained a deacon by us.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April.

CCLXXII. He exhorts the abbots and clerics of the archdeaconry of Guy to obey Guy, deposed by Richard, usurper of the Church of Verdun. (1109.)

[*Spicilegium*, ed. de La Barre, II, 248.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the abbots and other clerics, to Count RAINALD of Monzione, to RAINALD of Toul, and to the other clerics of [Col. 0254B] the archdeaconry of Guy: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have learned that, because of his attachment to Catholic unity, your archdeacon Guy has been despoiled of his goods by Richard, usurper of the Church of Verdun. Therefore we commend him to your charity by these present letters. We command that he be given the customary justice from the churches belonging to monasteries, and the obedience due to an archdeacon from clerics and laypeople. Otherwise, until they obey, let them be deprived of the divine offices and lose the tithes of their people.

But you, sons to whom God has given secular power and who uphold justice by arms, be his helpers for reverence toward Blessed Peter, and manfully restrain his adversaries. We command the same concerning the venerable man, the abbot of Saint Vito, both to you and to the rest of the regions of Verdun: because of that same attachment to Catholic unity, he has been deprived of his position and goods. Know also that the aforesaid Guy has been ordained a deacon by us.

CCLXXIII. Bull of protection and confirmation of the goods of the monastery of Calmosiacum. (1109, 21 March.)

[MARTENE, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, 1194.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SEHERUS, abbot of the monastery of Calmosiacum, and to his successors to be appointed in perpetuity.

Thus a [pious] petition of the will ought to be brought to completion by the ensuing effect [Col. 0254D], so that both the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire strength. Since, therefore, your belovedness, fleeing to the haven of the Apostolic See, has with due devotion sought its protection, we graciously assent to your petition and receive under the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of the Lord Savior and of the Blessed Mary his Mother, over which, by God’s providence, you preside, together with all that belongs to it. For we confirm, by the authority of this present privilege, the order of canonical life which you have professed, and decree that both you and [Col. 0255A] your successors who remain in the same religious observance shall possess in perpetuity all those things which you appear at present to hold for the support of the common livelihood: namely, the very freehold on which your church is situated, given by the knight Theodoric and his wife Hadelwide, with all its appurtenances; part of the freehold of Bulzei, given by Helvide of Calvomonte and her sons; part of the freehold of Igniaci, given by Widric of Walcourt and his wife Adelaide; part of the freeholds of Hamoniscurtis, Lihirici, and Lamerici, given by Bencelin of Casteneio and his wife Leucard in those same places; of these freeholds, another part given by Leucard of Villa, wife of Theodoric; part of the freehold of Darnole, given by the same Leucard at her death; the part which Bencelin held at Darnole, [Col. 0255B] given by Cunegund, wife of the knight Rofrid, through an exchange for Basonis-mons; part of the freehold of Truillaris, given by Mascelin of Domnus Martinus and his wife Hersind, together with the freehold of Maltucurt; the freehold of Janancurt, given by Robald of Domnus-Martinus, together with the part of the freehold which he held at Hulieni-villa; part of the freehold of Petri-villa, given by Lietard and his wife Elizabeth, together with a quarter of land at Darnole; the freeholds given by Berta, now a widow, and by her son Galfrid, which they held at Ruvirum, Masnila, Duvencurt, Unocurt, and Lifoi, with all their appurtenances; the freehold of Hudini-villa, given by Amalric and his wife Oda in exchange for the freehold which he held at Bagnoli; a quarter of land given by Beatrice, wife of Ganoli Darnoli; a quarter [Col. 0255C] of land given by Haduide of Fagnei-villa at Basolivilla; a quarter of land given by Stephen of Villa-Viriaco; the freehold given by Albric of Novo-castrum, his wife, and his sons at Unacurt, where a mill was built. Whatever also, in the future, you may be able to acquire by grant of pontiffs, liberality of princes, or offering of the faithful, lawfully and canonically, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Moreover, we decree that the brethren of your house shall not be compelled to render tithes or first-fruits from their ploughlands, labors, livestock, or mills, nor from the parish church of Saint Mary situated on the same estate of Calmosiacum, nor from anything else whatsoever. [Col. 0255D] Nor shall it be lawful for any person at all rashly to disturb that church, or to take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but let all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amendment by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the [Col. 0256A] last judgment let him lie under strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice toward that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional scriniary and notary of the Sacred Palace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April, in the second indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

### CCLXXIV. He takes the monastery of Saint Lambert under protection and confirms its possessions.

*(A.D. 1109, 25 March.)*

[It exists in the Imperial Vienna cartulary, according to JAFFÉ, *Regesta Pontificum Romanorum*, p. 498, who gives the foregoing title with this note: “From Pertz’s papers.”]

[Col. 0256B]

### CCLXXV. Privilege for the church of Saint Deodatus.

*(A.D. 1109, 10 April.)*

[SOMMIER, *History of the Church of Saint-Dié*, p. 162.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son REMBALD and the other brethren serving God in the church of Saint Deodatus: greeting and apostolic blessing.

A pious petition of will ought to be fulfilled by the ensuing effect, so that the sincerity of devotion [Col. 0256C] may laudably increase and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire strength. Since, therefore, your belovedness, fleeing to the haven of the Apostolic See, has sought protection with due devotion, we graciously assent to your petition and, by the authority of the Apostolic See, strengthen the church of Blessed Deodatus, situated in the valley of Galilee, where you have assembled to serve the Lord.

For we decree that whatever estates and possessions it possesses today, or may in the future, by God’s gift, possess through grants of pontiffs, royal munificence, princely liberality, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. The offerings which people coming there shall give to the altar for the remedy of their souls [Col. 0256D] shall be distributed for the common uses of the brethren.

No one shall be installed there as provost by any craft of deception or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall have elected in the fear of God. In accordance with the concession of Leo IX, Roman pontiff of holy memory, you may receive the consecration of altars and the ordinations of brethren to be promoted to sacred orders from whichever Catholic bishop you choose, provided that he freely grants what you request and lays aside every evil exaction. Indeed, for the correction of the brethren, whenever it is necessary, no persons shall be sent except those whom the provost, having consulted the sounder part of the brethren, summons as suitable for that very purpose.

Furthermore, whatever dignity the same church has obtained down to [Col. 0257A] our times, we also grant that it shall continue to possess hereafter, for the reverence of Blessed Deodatus and the salvation of many. If, indeed, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our grant, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amendment by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him lie under strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice toward that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and [Col. 0257B] before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

Written by the hand of John, regional scriniary and notary of the Sacred Palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of April, second indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

### CCLXXVI. He takes the monastery of Weissenau under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, imposing upon the monks an annual payment of one Byzantine.

*(A.D. 1109, 14 April.—See USSERMAN, in the *Bishopric of Bamberg*, Evidence no. 62.)*

[Col. 0257C]

### CCLXXVII. To Hugh, bishop of Grenoble.—Concerning the non-alienation of the possessions of the Church of Grenoble.

*(A.D. 1109, 18 April.)*

[PETIT, *The Penitential of Theodore*, vol. II, p. 419.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HUGH, bishop of Grenoble: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Accordingly, most reverend brother, we benignly assent to your wishes and, by the authority of this decree, strengthen the Church of Grenoble over which, by God’s providence, you preside. We decree and, by apostolic authority, forbid any of your successors [Col. 0257D] under any pretext to presume to give away, sell, or alienate lands, possessions, churches, tithes, or church revenues, and the other things which your brotherhood possesses, whether acquired by your predecessors or through your own diligence, or which you and your successors shall hereafter, by the Lord’s gift, acquire for the Church. If anyone receives them, whether sold or given away, he shall be subject to excommunication until he restores them.

We likewise forbid anyone, after your death or that of your successors, openly or secretly to dare to remove those goods until, by God’s grace, a pastor is appointed to the Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s [Col. 0258A] Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal, pope.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed, etc.

### CCLXXVIII. Bull for Saint Martin of Amiens.

*(A.D. 1109, 11 May.)*

[*Gallia Christiana*, X, Documents 302.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ARNULF, provost of the church of Saint Martin situated at the gate of Amiens, and to his brethren professing the regular life, present and future, forever.

A desire shown to concern religious purpose and the salvation of souls ought, by God’s agency [Col. 0258B], to be fulfilled without delay. Since, therefore, O sons, inspired by divine grace, you have resolved, according to the arrangement of our brother Godfrey, bishop of your city, to restrain your conduct under the discipline of the regular life and to serve almighty God in common according to the institutions of the holy Fathers, we also, in accordance with that bishop’s prayers, grant our assent to your devotion.

For we confirm by the authority of this present privilege the order of canonical life which you have professed, and decree that you and your successors who remain in the same religious observance shall possess in perpetuity all those things which you appear at present to hold for the support of the common livelihood: namely, all tithes from every newly cultivated land and episcopal crop [Col. 0258C] adjoining the city of Amiens, as has been granted to your church by predecessor bishops, except the tithes of lands from which the mother church or other churches of the city receive tithes; likewise, the tithes of the wool of all episcopal livestock; the altar of Saint Peter beyond the bridge and everything belonging to it; also the church of Saints Lupus, Walaricus, and Desiderius; the altar of Estombli and the land of its endowment; the altar of Warlus and Selincurte, free from every payment and service due to the bishop and his officials; their churchyards and guests, and the household of Saint Aper; likewise the altars of Donfront and Hargiscurte with their appurtenances; and also the prebend of each canon [lacuna] for one year after [Col. 0258D] his death, so that throughout that year you may offer the daily Mass for his soul; the brewery, guests, arable lands, and all the goods of the abbey of Saint Martin; and everything which your church formerly possessed at Amelly and Pisoy; and, from the mill of Saint Maurice, each year a small amount of winter grain and twenty-four sextarii of barley.

Moreover, whatever you may hereafter be able to acquire justly and canonically shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. No one shall have authority rashly to disturb that church or, under any pretext, to take away whatever is or shall be its property. Let you retain the same liberty as the canons of the mother church, provided that your church remains under the authority of the dean and canons of the mother church in accordance with the arrangement of the aforesaid bishop. Henceforth no canon shall be ordained among [Col. 0259A] you unless he has professed that he will live canonically.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amendment by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of the Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him lie under strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice toward that church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. [Col. 0259B] Amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, notary of the Sacred Palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Rome, in the portico of Blessed Peter, through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

### CCLXXIX. Privilege for Marmoutier.

*(A.D. 1109, 14 May.)*

[DUPAZ, *Genealogical History of Several Illustrious Houses of Brittany*, Paris, 1619, folio, II, 118.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0259C] sons WILLIAM, abbot of Marmoutier, and the other brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the representations of your letters and messengers, we have learned that our brother Benedict, bishop of Alet, first transferred to your monastery a certain cell on the island of Aaron, consecrated in honor of Saint Malo, with its appurtenances; and afterward granted by full conveyance to your monastery the church situated in the castle of Dinan, consecrated under the name of the same Saint Malo, because it belonged to the aforesaid cell as a member to its head. Geoffrey, lord of Dinan, his sons, and certain other secular powers also restored to your monastery whatever exterior goods they held in any manner [Col. 0259D] that belonged to the same cell or church.

We therefore, in accordance with your petition, add the strength of our confirmation to this grant, and decree that the aforesaid cell on the island of Aaron and the aforementioned church of the castle of Dinan, with all estates and possessions belonging to it, shall always belong to the possession, administration, and right of your monastery of Marmoutier. We establish and forbid in every way that anyone henceforth may separate that cell, with all its appurtenances, from the unity of your monastery. If anyone should rashly [Col. 0260A] presume to contravene the tenor of this decree, then, after a second warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be punished by the vengeance of ecclesiastical severity and by the sword of the Holy Spirit.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon and librarian, on the second day before the Ides of May, in the third indiction [Note: [Col. 0259D] The chronological data are corrupt. JAFFÉ.], in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

### CCLXXX. To Pons, abbot of Cluny.—He confirms to him and his successors everything granted, conferred, and confirmed to the monastery of Cluny by his predecessors, the popes.

*(A.D. 1109, 2 June.)*

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 36.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PONS, abbot of the monastery of Cluny: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0260B] At the beginning of your advancement, dearest son, you resolved to test the kindness of the Apostolic See, whether it remains toward you as it is seen to have remained to the end toward your predecessor Hugh, a man of outstanding religious devotion and wisdom. For you requested that we ought also to grant you those things which were granted by our predecessors to that abbot or to his predecessors. The request is indeed great and less suited to the custom of the Apostolic See; for such things are not usually granted to persons who are absent or insufficiently known. And although you are already known to us in some measure, not yet has so shining a proof of prudence or religious devotion appeared in you.

Nevertheless, the outstanding prerogative of your aforesaid predecessor, the better hope which by God’s grace we entertain concerning your [Col. 0260C] character, and the petition of the brethren—men certainly religious and wise—who elected you as their father, joined to your own request, have so moved our benevolence toward you that we have resolved at present to deny nothing to your reasonable petition, even though you are absent. For we trust that you have been trained, by the Lord’s gift, in the practices of the aforesaid abbot, and that those same brethren will remain forever in his praiseworthy discipline; so that, as in time past, so also in the future, examples of holy religious life may spread from the monastery of Cluny.

Therefore, relying upon this hope and this confidence through God’s grace, we confer, [Col. 0260D] grant, and confirm to you, dearest son, and to your lawful successors, and through you to the monastery of Cluny, whatever is known to have been bestowed, granted, and confirmed by our predecessors, whether through privileges of the Apostolic See or through other authentic instruments. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amendment by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him lie under strict vengeance. Upon all, however, who preserve justice toward that monastery, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and [Col. 0261A] before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional scriniary of the Sacred Palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Rome, in the portico of Blessed Peter, through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of June, in the second indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

(Sealed with a pendant lead bull, on untwisted silk cords of red and saffron colors.)

### CCLXXXI. To the bishops of Anagni and Campania.—Concerning the canonization of Saint Peter, bishop of Anagni.

*(A.D. 1109, 2 June.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1001.]

[Col. 0261B]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren, the bishops of Anagni and others established throughout Campania: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Keeping before our eyes the Most High Lord, who is praised and blessed in his friends, and considering therefore the merits of the vigorous and proven life by which the holy man Peter, formerly bishop of Anagni, drawn from the monastic order, served God in the pastoral office with purity, simplicity, diligent vigilance, and example; and also admiring the remarkable miracles with which divine grace adorned its saint before and after his death, as is faithfully recorded by Bruno, bishop of Segni, and has not ceased to adorn him down to our times: by the authority of these presents, we will and command that you may fittingly celebrate on the third day before the Nones of August the heavenly birthday of this confessor and bishop, whose commemoration belongs in the catalogue of saints; so that, through his pious intercessions, we may deserve to obtain grace in the present and everlasting glory in the future, with the aid of divine clemency.

Given at Segni, on the second day before the Nones of June, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

### CCLXXXII. To Peter, priest.

*(A.D. 1109, 29 September.)*

[LAMI, *Delights of the Learned*, 1737, p. 204.]

[Col. 0261D]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, priest: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We graciously admit the petitions of your devotion and therefore grant you leave, with the consent of the bishop of the same city, to build a monastery in the borough of Siena, in a suitable place. We decree that, if it is built by the grace of God, it shall always remain quiet and free under the guardianship and rule of the congregation of Passignano and Vallombrosa. Therefore we decree that no one at all may rashly disturb the monastery built [Col. 0262A] in honor of God, Saint Benedict, and the other saints, or take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but all things offered, whether by you or by other faithful persons, from their own right, shall be kept unimpaired and whole. Whoever shall take care to support that monastery and those serving the Lord in it, and to honor them from his own goods, shall obtain the grace of almighty God and his apostles. But if anyone, which may it never be, should attempt to oppose this our decree, let him suffer the loss of his honor and office unless he corrects his presumption by worthy satisfaction.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Given at Castiglione through the hand of John, [Col. 0262B] deacon cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of October, third indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the tenth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

### CCLXXXIII. To Pons, abbot of Cluny.—He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Cluny.

*(A.D. 1100, 16 October.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1041.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PONS, abbot of the monastery of Cluny, and to his successors to be regularly appointed forever.

Both the religious life of the monastery of Cluny, over which, by God’s providence, you preside, and the sweet and reverent affection for your predecessor, Hugh, abbot of holy memory, compel us, dearest son in Christ, Abbot Pons, [Col. 0262C] to grant your requests. Accordingly, we decree that the abbeys and priories which remained under the administration of the aforesaid Abbot Hugh shall remain also under yours and your successors’ administration. *(They are enumerated. Then it continues:)*

In the places which appear to have been without their own abbot in the days of the lord and venerable Abbot Hugh, no one shall ever presume to appoint an abbot. We also decree that this liberty shall remain assured to the monastery of Cluny: that the monks of your monastery who are to be promoted to sacred orders may be promoted by whichever Catholic bishops they prefer. Should need require, you may have chrism consecrated in your monastery, or by whichever bishops you choose. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, etc., as in certain other letters.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Given at Castellium through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of November, third indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II.

### CCLXXXIV. Privilege to Pons, abbot of Cluny, to whom he sends a white pallium, so that he may make from it dalmatics for use in the church of Cluny; he grants him the use of pontifical insignia on the eight principal feasts of his monastery.

*(A.D. 1109, 17 October.)*

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, p. 36.]

[Col. 0263A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PONS, abbot of Cluny: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not in the least doubt that the desire of the brethren of Cluny was good and praiseworthy when they chose you as abbot for the safeguarding of their souls. Endeavor, therefore, by God’s grace, dearest son in Christ, as far as lies in you, to fulfill their good desire; so that you yourself may advance in religious life and may always keep those entrusted to you in the fear of God. From the benevolence of the Apostolic See and the grace of Blessed Peter, we send you a white pallium, from which you ought to prepare dalmatics for the use of your church. We grant you, by special affection, the use of dalmatics, sandals (*compagae*), gloves, and mitre on the eight principal feasts [Col. 0263B] of your monastery, as it was granted to your predecessor, Abbot Hugh of happy memory, by our predecessor. Take care, therefore, that as you hold his place and have attained his dignity, so you also maintain religious discipline and pursue diligence, so that by God’s grace both the welfare of the monastery may remain unshaken and the grace of the divine name may be exalted both in you and in them.

Given at Castellium, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of November.

(Sealed with a pendant lead bull, on a single twisted cord.)

### CCLXXXV. Privilege for the monastery of Siegburg.

*(A.D. 1109, 28 November.)*

[LACOMBLET, *Cartulary for the History of the Lower Rhine*, Düsseldorf, 1840, quarto, vol. I, p. 175.]

[Col. 0263C]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son CUNO, abbot of the venerable monastery situated on Mount Siegburg, and to his successors to be regularly appointed forever.

Just as no effect ought to be granted to those seeking unjust things, so the request of those desiring lawful things ought not to be delayed. Since, therefore, your belovedness, fleeing to the haven of the Apostolic See, has sought its protection with due [Col. 0263D] devotion, we graciously assent to your petition and strengthen by the authority of the Apostolic See the monastery of Blessed Michael, over which, by God’s providence, you preside.

We confirm to you and your successors all possessions, estates, and other goods whatsoever granted by Anno, archbishop of Cologne of happy memory, founder of that monastery: namely, the church at Bleisa with its endowed holding and tithe-right; the church at Hanafo with tithes and other appurtenances, which he received from the canons of Bonn by exchange, having given to their use and that of their church the custodianship at Bonn; likewise the village called Mendenen, which he received from the provost or canons of the principal church in exchange for the tithe-right at Bathalicha. We also confirm the other places [Col. 0264A] which he granted through the hands of advocates to the same monastery and to the servants of Christ dwelling there, for food and clothing: namely Acchera, again Acchera; Strala, Nistera, Beringerishuscim, Geistingen, Upper Bleisa, Lara, Menedon, Atemere, Antrefe, Gulusa, Legia; vineyards at Wintere, Bethendorf, and Mulendorf; at Rigemogon certain fields with vineyards; the church at Berchein with tithe-right; the church in Lower Bleisa with its endowed holding; the church at Hanafo with tithes; Sulse, Trutthesdorf, Menimdorf, Torendorf, Mulendorf, Irmenderoth, Chorincheid, Inere, Uneheim, Flatenen, Perne, Grecenich, Hofstedenen, Luvesberch, Flamersfets, Quintinachen. Furthermore, the village of Hircennowen, which King Henry IX transferred to the same monastery.

[Col. 0264B] We decree that whatever goods have been offered to that monastery from their own right by other faithful persons, or happen hereafter to be offered or acquired by other lawful means, shall remain quiet and whole to you and to your successors who live according to the rule. We forbid the advocates to whom the advocacy of the monastery may at any time be entrusted to appoint another advocate under themselves; nor may they demand more from goods granted for stipends, or from those things paid for legal dues, than was provided by the ordinance of the aforesaid Archbishop Anno.

Therefore we decree that no one at all may rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but let all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those [Col. 0264C] for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amendment by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him lie under strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice toward that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict [Col. 0264D] Judge, may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional scriniary and notary of the Sacred Palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of December, in the third indiction, in the year 1109 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

### CCLXXXVI. He commands Duke Theodoric and Riquin, bishop-elect of Toul, by secular and ecclesiastical censure to repel the adversaries of the monastery of Calmosiacum from oppressing the monks.

*(A.D. 1109. See Scher’s book, *On the Beginnings of the Monastery of Calmosiacum*, in MARTENE, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, vol. III, p. 1191.)*

### CCLXXXVII. To Henry, abbot of Saint Vaast.

*(A.D. 1109.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, Luc. ed., II, 150.]

[Col. 0265A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HENRY, abbot of Saint Vaast: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The report which we recently heard concerning you brought us no small joy. For we heard that, having taken brethren from the Cluniac congregation, you have now begun to reform the ways of your monastery and to cultivate religious observance. This greatly delights religious men who know you. We therefore admonish and entreat you to persist steadfastly in what you have begun and to labor with greater diligence to bring the pursuit of religious life to a good end. [Col. 0265B]

### CCLXXXVIII. To Gebhard, bishop of Constance.—Concerning those who communicate with excommunicated persons, and how heretics are to be received.

*(A.D. 1101–1110, 6 February.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1083.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BEARD [probably Gebhard], bishop of Constance: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that the obscurities of the questions which you sent us are not hidden from your own understanding. But because you seek more certain instruction from the Apostolic See concerning what sound doctrine holds on these matters, we reply.

It is in no way lawful to communicate with excommunicated persons in matters prohibited by the sacred canons. Those who communicate voluntarily, whether monks or others, are involved in the guilt of the same offense. But those who communicate either in ignorance or unwillingly through necessity, although in the eyes of men they are defiled by contagion, we do not judge them for this reason guilty in the sight of the eternal Judge. Furthermore, the bodies of excommunicated persons are to be cast out of the basilicas of the saints, because their stench rises to heaven, as the fourth book of the *Dialogues* of Blessed Gregory indicates and as we have learned by the revelation of the saints themselves. Therefore, while such bodies are kept there, we judge that divine offices ought to cease.

Reason dictates that chrism or oil prepared by heretics ought, for reverence for the divine invocation, to be burned within the Church. Those coming from the heretics themselves are to be received altogether in the manner in which the records of our holy predecessors Leo and Gregory declare that they were formerly to be received or were received.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Ides of February.

### CCLXXXIX. Privilege concerning the market and the meal given on the two feasts of Saint Remigius, likewise concerning the immunity of this church.

*(A.D. 1110, 3 January.)*

[VARIN, *Administrative Archives of the City of Reims*, vol. IV, p. 255.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ AZENARIUS, abbot of the venerable monastery [Col. 0266A] of Saint Remigius situated near the city of Reims, and to his successors to be regularly appointed, for perpetual remembrance.

“Just as no effect is to be granted to those seeking unjust things,” and the rest, which may be read word for word in the bull of the year 1107, above, col. 216; the notes appended to the earlier bull indicate the places in which it differs somewhat.

### CCXC. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Florence.

*(A.D. 1110, 9 January.)*

[LAMI, *Ecclesiastical Monuments of Florence*, II, 1182.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BENEDICT, abbot of the monastery of Saint Minias, and to his successors to be regularly appointed forever.

[Col. 0266B] A pious request ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding act, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the advantage sought may undoubtedly gain strength. Since, therefore, your belovedness has fled to the haven of the Apostolic See and has duly sought its protection with devotion, we mercifully assent to your petition and, by authority of the Apostolic See, protect the monastery of the blessed martyr Minias, over which, by God’s providence, you preside. In that monastery rest the bodies of that holy martyr Minias himself and of many other martyrs. We therefore confirm to you and to that monastery Mount of the King, upon which the church of the aforesaid martyr stands, with every appurtenance of that estate, and the Field of Mars; and Bisarno, from the River Arno as far as the public road; [Col. 0266C] the church of Saint Mary of Albuino, situated at Alberita, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Peter, situated at Camullia, together with its hospital and all its appurtenances; and the estate of Sicignano, which Hugh son of Gerard and his wife Mandolla gave to that monastery, and that which was donated to it by Gerard son of Aldeprand.

Likewise, we confirm all the other churches, castles, villages, and possessions which Hildebrand, Lambert, Attho, and Gerard, bishops of Florence, emperors, kings, Catholic princes, or other faithful persons conferred upon that monastery from their own right.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the said monastery, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that everything granted for the support and government of those for whom it was granted shall be preserved wholly intact, to serve their use in every respect—without prejudice to the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Florence. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, attempts to contravene this document of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to divine vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here [Col. 0267A] they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, scrivener and notary of the sacred palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of January, in the third indiction, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

CCXCI. At the request of Bishop Goffrid, he confirms the boundaries of the diocese of Sora and the possessions of its Church. (1110, February 9.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 1245.]

[Col. 0267B]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GOFFRID, bishop of Sora, and to his successors . . . the people.

Just as no effect is to be granted to those seeking unjust things . . . assenting to your petition, dearest brother in Christ, by the permanence of this present decree we establish for the perpetual peace and stability of the holy Church of Sora that all the boundaries of the parish, which have hitherto been possessed by the parishioners with their rights, shall be preserved entirely and intact forever both to you and to your successors. These boundaries extend toward the estate and crypt of the robber; thence to the boundary of Cetinina; thence inward, and thence . . . to Sora; thence to the Sangro; thence to the Royal Valley; [Col. 0267C] thence to Afedena; thence to Vestia; thence to Savira of the Anistri; thence to Petra Recta; thence to Coacia; thence to Sulfuratum; thence to Ponte Fracto; thence to Monte Corneto; thence to Campo Rontio; [lacuna] thence to Petra Mala; thence to the land of Piro; thence returning to the aforesaid hill.

Within these boundaries, in all towns, villages, monasteries, and churches, we establish episcopal jurisdiction for you and your successors . . . Since they are known to belong to the Church of Sora by proprietary right, we decree that they shall remain forever peaceful and intact for you and your successors . . . the castle of Insula with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Lawrence; and . . . the church of Saint Paul in the Field; at Arpino, the parish church of Saint Mary and the parish church of Saint Michael the Archangel; in the castle . . . the church [Col. 0267D] of Saint Mary; at Sora, the parish church of Saint Restituta; the church of Saint Lawrence; the church of Saint Lucy; the church of Saint Vitus at Carpello; the church of Saint Peter . . . two mills on the River Liri, and one at Carnello; in the valley of Sora, the church of Saint Peter; and Saint Donatus . . . the parish church of Saint Mary; the church of Saint Sabinus . . . the church of Saint Mary of the Field; Saint Urban; the church of Saint Mary of . . . the church of Saint Mary of Picenisti at Atino; the churches of Saint Mary, Saint Peter, Saint Silvester, Saint Maurus, and Saint Angel of . . . three mills on the River Melfa with their appurtenances. Likewise, outside Atino, the church of Saint Marcian.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to harass or disturb the same church, to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, [Col. 0268A] diminish them, or afflict it with reckless vexations; but that everything shall be preserved intact, etc.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of February, in the third indiction, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

CCXCII. Confirmation of the endowment and goods of the monastery of Saint Benignus of Fruttuaria. (1110, March 13.)

[GUICHENON, *Hist. génér. de la maison de Savoie*, II, 24.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ALMEUS, abbot of the monastery of Fruttuaria, and to the monks, [Col. 0268B] greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a speedy result. For Countess Agnes, daughter of Marquis Peter, who, abandoning the world, chose the peace of monastic life, conferred upon your monastery one half of Villanova, in its entirety and with the freedom in which she herself had held it. She asked that this grant be confirmed by our authority. Therefore, yielding to her prayers and yours through our brother Mainard, bishop of Turin, we establish by this present decree that the same half of Villanova shall remain forever in the possession of your monastery. We make the same provision concerning the village of Fala, one half of which, from the offering of Marquis Ardition—who by God’s grace became a convert in your [Col. 0268C] monastery—and the other half from the sale by his brother Marquis Mansfred, we have learned belongs by right to your monastery.

Therefore no one may withdraw either that half of Villanova or the whole of Fala from your monastery’s possession, or alienate either by any contrivance; but all, as delivered by the aforesaid persons to your community, shall remain forever peaceful, entire, and inviolate property in the use and government of you or your successors. But if anyone—which God forbid—knowingly attempts rashly to oppose this document of our decree, let him incur the loss of his rank and office or be punished by the penalty of excommunication, unless he corrects his presumption by fitting satisfaction.

[Col. 0268D] I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church. SS.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal, on the third day before the Ides of March, in the third indiction.

CCXCIII. At the request of Bishop Peter, he confirms the liberty, privileges, and possessions of the Church of Squillace. (1110, April 5.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IX, 429.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, bishop of Squillace, and to his successors canonically promoted forever.

The authority of the Apostolic See compels us to be concerned for the condition of the Churches, correcting what is wrong [Col. 0269A] and establishing what is right. It is clear, indeed, that the Church of Squillace, of which you are, by the Lord’s appointment and through our institution, pastor, remained in earlier times especially under the jurisdiction of the Apostolic See, as is shown to those diligently investigating the authentic writings of blessed Gregory. Therefore, since by God’s providence, through the labours and victories of our most valiant brothers Robert, duke of noble memory, and Count Roger, the tyrannical invasion of the Greeks has ceased both from that Church and from the other churches of Calabria, we follow in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Urban II. Cherishing the Church of Squillace under the special jurisdiction of the Holy Apostolic See, we establish and decree to be observed in perpetuity that, as you, so also your successors henceforth, shall always be consecrated by the hand [Col. 0269B] of the Roman pontiffs.

Furthermore, within the circuit bounded by the rivers—as the torrents flow from the upper mountains into the rivers Crocchia and Alarum, and those rivers flow into the Adriatic Sea—we confirm those things which, in the presence of our brothers all the bishops of Sicily and some of Calabria, before the aforesaid Count Roger, and upon the testimony of elders and witnesses of many years, were proved to have belonged from ancient times to the Church of Squillace in accordance with the command of our same predecessor Urban II; and likewise those things which blessed Gregory is recorded to have granted to the Church of Squillace. Let these remain forever firm and whole in the possession of you, your successors, and that Church itself.

Moreover, we confirm to that Church, by proprietary right, the tenants and estates of Palaeopolis or Roccella, which Countess Adelaide, with her son [Col. 0269C] Roger, gave to the Church of Squillace for the redemption of the soul of the aforesaid Count Roger, together with the oratory of Saint Mary situated there. Further, whatever it may hereafter be able justly and canonically to acquire through the generosity of princes or the offerings of the faithful shall be preserved to it unimpaired by perpetual stability.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the same Church, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that everything granted for the support and governance of those for whom it was granted shall be preserved wholly intact, to serve their use in every respect. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, [Col. 0269D] attempts rashly to contravene this document of our constitution and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make full amendment by satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that Church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruits of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.
