Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of April, in the third indiction, [Col. 0270A] in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

CCXCIV. Privilege for the church of Saint Christopher of Phalempin. (1110, April 9.)

[MIRAEUS, *Opp. Diplom.*, III, 317.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved in Christ LAMBERT, abbot, and to his brethren professing the canonical life in the church of Saint Christopher of Phalempin, and to their successors forever.

We have learned of your devotion from the report of our venerable brothers John, bishop of Thérouanne, and Baldric, bishop of Noyon, [Col. 0270B] namely that, by the Lord’s bounty, you have been enkindled in the church of Phalempin for the observance of regular discipline. We have also learned the desire of the religious spouses Roger and Ogiva, who, making your place free from the yoke of their own lordship, wished canons to be established there according to the Rule of blessed Augustine. Therefore, assenting both to their wish and to the petitions of our aforesaid brother bishops, we establish by the force of apostolic authority that the order of canonical life which you have professed shall be preserved in that place forever.

For this reason, we decree that whatever lands or goods have been offered from their own right to that church by the founders of the church itself, by the aforesaid spouses, or by any faithful persons of God, or shall happen to be offered in the future, [Col. 0270C] shall remain perpetually firm and undisturbed for you and your successors.

Accordingly, we command and strictly forbid that any burden be imposed upon you by the dean or other clerics of the mother church concerning chrism or oil for catechumens or confirmation candidates.

We also grant you authority to appoint in the church of your parish a priest to govern the parish, without prejudice, however, to the reverence due to the bishop of Tournai, etc.

Given at the Lateran, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third indiction, on the fifth day before the Ides of April, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

CCXCV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Peter of Melk. (1110, April 16.)

[HUEBER, *Austria ex archivis Mellicensibus illustrata*. Leipzig, 1722, folio, p. 3.]

[Col. 0270D]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SIGIBOLD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter of Melk, and to his successors regularly appointed forever.

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a speedy result. Marquis Leopold offered to blessed Peter and to the Holy Roman Church the church and monastery of blessed Peter, built by his parents at the place called Melk, in the diocese of Passau and held under his right of [Col. 0271A] patronage, to be cherished forever under its protection. Therefore, assenting to his religious desires at the request of our brother Udalric, bishop of Passau, we receive that monastery under the protection of the Apostolic See and fortify it by the authority of this present decree.

We further decree that all lands, possessions, and churches with offerings of tithes which the aforesaid princes Leopold and his father Leopold and their other relatives, or other faithful persons, have conferred upon that monastery from their own right, or which may in the future be offered by grant of pontiffs, generosity of princes, or offerings of the faithful, or acquired by other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. [Col. 0271B] Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any trick of usurpation or by force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall elect in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict, to be consecrated by the Roman pontiff.

Nor shall you be compelled to submit to the judgment of neighbouring abbots, unless ecclesiastical necessity should require it in the case of those who belong to the proprietary jurisdiction of the Apostolic See. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of monks to be promoted to sacred orders from the bishop of Passau, provided that he enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide these freely [Col. 0271C] and without impropriety. Otherwise, you may approach whatever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration; supported by the authority of the Apostolic See, he shall grant what is requested.

No opposition from any bishop or provost shall prevent you from receiving for conversion laypersons or clerics living in the secular state. We also decree that the burial place of the same monastery shall be wholly free, and no one, unless they are excommunicated, shall obstruct the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there. Marquis Leopold, or whichever heir shall thereafter hold the march, shall remain advocate of that place. Yet neither they nor any person whatsoever may rashly claim anything for themselves in [Col. 0271D] the same monastery or in its goods, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations. Rather, everything granted for the support and government of those for whom it was granted shall be preserved intact, to serve their use in every respect.

Moreover, as a token of the exemption received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one gold piece annually to the Lateran palace. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts to contravene this document of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most holy [Col. 0272A] body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

CCXCVI. At the request of Bishop Didacus, he confirms the possessions of the Church of Saint James of Compostela. (1110, April 21.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 85.]

[Col. 0272B]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother DIDACUS, bishop of the Church of Compostela, and to his successors canonically promoted forever.

Just as no effect is to be granted to those seeking unjust things, so the petition of those desiring lawful things is not to be delayed. Therefore, assenting to your petitions, dearest brother in Christ, which you submitted through the faithful sons of your Church, Geoffrey, archdeacon of your Church, and Peter, priest and chaplain, we establish by the permanence of this present decree, for the perpetual peace and stability of the holy Church of Compostela and in reverence for blessed James the apostle, that [Col. 0272C] all things which belong by proprietary right within your parish to the church of blessed James itself, in which his body is indeed believed to rest, as we have learned from the report of the aforesaid brethren, shall be preserved wholly peaceful and intact forever for you and your successors: namely, the land of Superato, Dormiana, Bavegium, Coronatum, Mercia, the archpresbyterate of Saint Pelagius of Circitello, Mons Sacer, Taberiolus, the land of the Mountains as far as Avium, Morracium, Salniense, the land of the Baths, the land of Arches, Iriense, Pistomarcus, Amahea and the other mountains, Prucios, Trasancos, Lovacencos, Arros, Nemitos, Bisancos, the land of Faro, Coporos, Celticos, and Brecantinos. In the mountain districts, the two archpresbyterates [Col. 0272D] of Dubria and Barcala, Salagia, Gentines, and the rest as far as the Ocean, as they are contained in the writings of that church.

We also confirm to you those things which were offered to blessed James and his church by the late noble King Alfonso and his sisters, namely Geloyra and Urraca, and by the aforesaid king’s son-in-law Count Raymond and his wife Urraca, daughter of that king, by lawful charters or testaments: namely, the mint of the city of Compostela, the monasteries of Piloño and Branderiz, the church of Saint Mammes with all their appurtenances, and houses in the city of Compostela. We also confirm to you the towns and estates given by earlier kings of Spain, namely Honestum, Faro, the castle of Saint Mary of Lanciata with their appurtenances, the churches [Col. 0273A] of Saints Victor and Fructuosus, and the village of Corneliana in the district of Portugal with its appurtenances.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb that church, take away or diminish its possessions, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that everything granted for the government and support of those for whom it was granted shall be preserved intact, to serve their use in every respect. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts to contravene this document of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God [Col. 0273B] and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

CCXCVII. He writes to Bishop D[idacus] of Compostela that he grieves over the hardships of the Spanish Churches. (1110, April.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 86.]

[Col. 0273C]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother D., bishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The oppressions and hardships which the Church suffers in your regions afflict our heart with grievous sorrow. Therefore we pray Almighty God to deign to assist you, and we urge you yourselves to take care to raise up vigorous men for the defence of the Church. The petition which, both on your behalf and on behalf of the clergy and people, the sons of your Church—G., the archdeacon, and Peter the chaplain—who were sent to us, presented, we cannot at present fulfil, as those same messengers will be able to explain to you orally. Yet we wish you to know without doubt that we rejoice in the exaltation [Col. 0273D] of your Church. For we desire suitably to honour it on account of the merits of blessed James.

CCXCVIII. To Bishop D[idacus] of Compostela.—Concerning restoration of the church of Saint Michael to P[eter] the chaplain. (1110, April.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 87.]

P., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother D., bishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our son P., chaplain of your Church, complains against Suarius that, employing secular powers, he violently took from him the church of Saint Michael situated in your city. Therefore your brotherhood is not ignorant of what the canons prescribe. [Col. 0274A] Accordingly, we command your belovedness to summon him, so that he may restore the aforesaid church to P. and permit him to hold it undisturbed; otherwise let him be struck by canonical sentence and let the church itself be placed under interdict.

CCXCIX. To Godfrey, abbot of Saint-Maixent.—He receives his monastery into the protection of the Holy See. (1110, April 27.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XX, 1035.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved in Christ Lord GOFRID, abbot of the venerable monastery of Saint Maxentius the Helper, and to his successors regularly promoted forever.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding act, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably [Col. 0274B] and the advantage sought may undoubtedly gain [added: strength]. Since, therefore, your belovedness has fled to the haven of the Apostolic See and has duly sought its protection with devotion, we mercifully assent to your petition and receive under the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of blessed Maxentius, over which, by God’s providence, you preside, together with the adjacent village and all else belonging to it.

Accordingly, by the document of this present privilege we establish by apostolic authority that whatever lands and possessions that monastery now lawfully possesses in this third indiction, or may hereafter justly and canonically acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of princes, or offerings of the faithful, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among them the following were considered to require annotation under their proper names, etc. From these lands, indeed, you shall pay five *solidi* of Poitiers annually to the Lateran palace.

Therefore no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations. Rather, everything granted for the support and governance of those for whom it was granted shall be preserved intact, to serve their use in every respect. Nor shall the monastery itself be subjected to interdict or excommunication, unless perhaps on account of the wealthier persons, cubi . . . [lacuna], whom either the abbot or the monks have neglected to correct. Yet they themselves shall not admit persons excommunicated or under interdict to the divine office; nor, under a general interdict of the parish, [Col. 0274D] shall bells be rung.

Upon the death of you, abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one whatsoever shall be set over it through crafty usurpation or force, except one whom the brethren by their consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel—whether from their own community or, if necessary, from another—shall elect in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict. If henceforth any archbishop or bishop, emperor or king, prince or duke, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly [acts] against this document of our constitution, etc., as in certain other letters.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, regional scrivener of the sacred palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

[Col. 0275A] Given at Rome in the portico of blessed Peter, through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

CCC. To Peter, bishop of Poitiers.—He is to warn Hugh of Lusignan not to delay making reparation for injuries inflicted upon the monastery of Saint-Maixent. (1110.)

[Dom BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 46.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother P[ETER], bishop of Poitiers, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Because we know Hugh of Lusignan to be a faithful man of blessed Peter, we love him especially; but neither does Saint Peter accept loyalty that conflicts with loyalty toward the churches committed to him, [Col. 0275B] nor can we show affection in opposition to God. Therefore warn him earnestly not to delay correcting and making reparation for the injuries which he inflicts upon the monastery of Saint Maxentius, lest by a small occasion he destroy the labours of many years which he is believed to have performed for God.

> [Note: [Col. 0275D] William of Malmesbury relates that Hugh of Lusignan set out for Palestine in 1101 with Count William of Poitiers, in our volume XIII—that is, in Dom Bouquet—p. 8.]

Otherwise, within two months after you receive this letter, we command that he be restrained by canonical judgment.

CCCI. To Peter, bishop of Poitiers.—He entrusts to his judgment several disputes concerning the monastery of Saint-Maixent, and commends to him lands owing a census to the Roman Church. (1110.)

[Dom BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 46.]

[Col. 0275C] PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother P[ETER], bishop of Poitiers, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The bearer of this letter, G[offrid], [Note: [Col. 0275D] Goffrid, who in 1110 brought back from Rome the bull published by Besly in the *History of the Counts of Poitou*, [Col. 0276D] p. 431, and by Labbe, vol. X of the *Councils*, col. 679 (it is our letter 299 above): “Given at Rome in the portico of blessed Peter, through the hand of John, deacon cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.”] abbot of Saint Maxentius, complains that many things are being taken from his monastery by Hugh of Lusignan. They also say that they have a dispute with the abbot of La Chaise-Dieu concerning the churches of Gozenogili (Gazeneuil), and with the abbot of Saint-Severin concerning the churches of Lesaii or Berlaum. He also complains that his monastery is burdened by Mostarolo, by Simon of Werruca, by Thebaud Meschin, and by several others. Therefore we command your brotherhood to render him effective justice both concerning these matters and concerning the other complaints of the monastery. We especially commend to your protection the land of Pampro and Rigaudam, and of Saint Germerius, from which an annual census is paid to the Roman Church.

CCCII. Bull addressed to Saint Raymond, bishop of Barbastro. (1110, May 2.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XLVI, 329.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant, etc., to RAYMOND, bishop of Barbastro, and to his successors canonically appointed forever.

[Col. 0276A] Taught by the Spirit of the Lord, we have learned that the Lord transfers kingdoms and changes times. Formerly, in Spain, according to his good pleasure, he enlarged the kingdoms of the Christians; and again, through the tyranny of the Saracens or Moabites, he visited the sins of the Christians according to his judgments. Hence it came about that the episcopal see which had been at Lleida was transferred into the mountains, namely to the town called Roda. Then, when the power of the Moabites had again diminished, it was transferred nearer to Lleida, to the town of Barbastro. In our own time, through God’s grace, the Christians have gained firmer hope that, by the Lord’s working, they will recover the city of Lleida.

Therefore, following the judgments of the Lord our God, we decree by this present enactment that the episcopal see hitherto held at Roda or Barbastro shall in the future be transferred to [Col. 0276B] the city of Lleida when Almighty God has restored it to Christian rule. The mountain boundaries, however, shall be retained as held and possessed by you or your predecessors at Roda and Barbastro, together with the valleys of Bielsa and Gistaín, the abbey of Alao, and the monastery of Saint Martin of Cavallera, as they have been obtained from kings as the allodial property of the Church of Roda. Concerning the other monasteries situated within the same parish, due reverence shall be paid to you and your successors, as it has hitherto been paid to your predecessors.

We therefore confirm to you the churches of Balaguer and Tamarite and the lands already brought under Christian rule; and, when restored, the churches in Fraga, Zaidín, and Ontiñena. We likewise confirm all tithes and other [Col. 0276C] matters of ecclesiastical right belonging to the environs of Lleida. All the boundaries of the same diocese which have been or shall be brought under Christian power, we command, as established in former times by the privilege of our predecessor of apostolic memory, [Urban] II, and by our own privilege, to be subject to the jurisdiction of you and your successors, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See.

We therefore decree that no person may rashly disturb your Church, take away its possessions, retain abbeys, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations; rather, all shall be preserved intact for the use of you, your successors, the clerics, and the poor. If any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly presumes to contravene this document of our enactment [Col. 0276D] and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all others preserving the rights of that Church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that [Col. 0277A] here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Written by the hand of John, regional scrivener and notary of the sacred palace.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church. SS. BE. V.

Given at Rome in the portico of blessed Peter, through the hand of John, deacon cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Nones of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1110 of the Incarnation, and in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II.

CCCIII. He receives the monastery of Saint Vincent of Cupersano under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (1110, July 15.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, VII, 703.]

[Col. 0277B]

PASCHAL, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son VINCENT, abbot of the venerable monastery of Saint Benedict, situated in the city of Cupersano, and to his successors regularly succeeding forever.

A devout petition should be fulfilled with the affection that attends goodwill, so that both the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested benefit may undoubtedly gain strength. Since, fleeing to the haven of the Apostolic See, your belovedness has duly sought its protection, we graciously assent to your petition and receive under the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Saint Benedict at Cupersanum, over which, by God’s favor, you preside. Therefore, by the authority of the Apostolic See, we establish through this page of the present privilege [Col. 0277C] that everything which that monastery lawfully possesses in the present third indiction, or may hereafter be able justly and canonically to acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the same church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose support or governance they were granted, being of use to them in every respect. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any craft of intrigue or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall elect, whether from their own community or, if necessary, from another [Col. 0277D] community, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of monks who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from the bishop in whose diocese you are, provided that he possesses the favor and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide these things freely and without impropriety. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer [Col. 0278A] and receive consecration and the sacraments from him, provided that, supported by the authority of the Apostolic See, he grants what is requested. Moreover, neither the bishop nor the bishop’s officials shall have authority to impose any new exactions upon that place, inflict any burden upon it, or lay a hand of deposition upon the abbot of the place without the judgment of the Apostolic See. As the token of the protection received from the Roman Church, you shall pay yearly one half-ounce of gold to the Lateran Palace.

If, therefore, in future any archbishop or bishop, emperor or king, prince or duke, count, viscount, military governor (*stratigo*), judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of his power and rank; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who observe what is just toward the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Benevento through the hand of John, cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of July, in the second indiction, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eleventh year of the pontificate [Col. 0278C] of Lord Paschal II.

### CCCIV. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the Church of Sonnebecq.  
*(Year 1110, October 16.)*

[MIRAEUS, *Opera diplomatica*, II, 1152.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ LAMBERT, provost of the Church of Sonnebecq, greetings and apostolic blessing.

From the writing of Drogo, formerly venerable bishop of the Morini, we have learned that Fulpodus of good memory, together with his wife Ramburga, your grandmother, and after them your father Theobald, bestowed upon the holy Church at Sonnebecq in the village various estates belonging to them by right [Col. 0278D], from which provision might be made for seven canons.

[Note: [Col. 0277D] Drogo, sent from the monastery of Saint-Bertin to restore the abbey of Saint Winoc at Bergues; afterward elected bishop of Thérouanne in 1030, he died near Jubilanus in 1078.]

[Note: [Col. 0277D] Sonnebeck: an abbey of regular canons of the Order of Saint Augustine, two miles from Ypres; it was formerly subject to the congregation of Arrouaise.]

We decree that the properties therefore given to the same Church by your aforesaid parents, together also with the altars bestowed upon that place by Radbod, bishop of Noyon, of good memory—namely those of Roeselare, Nieuwkerke, and Bevenslaer—and whatever has been offered, or may hereafter happen to be offered [Col. 0279A], to that church from their own lawful property by any of the faithful, shall remain always firm and undisturbed for the use of those same canons.

[Note: [Col. 0277D] Roeselare, now called in Latin *Rollarium*, commonly Rousselaere. The abbot of Sonnebecq is in fact patron and schoolmaster of this place; nevertheless, he does not exercise pastoral care there through his religious. That pastoral care was granted to them in this bull.]

[Note: [Col. 0278D] Nieuwkerke, commonly Nieuwekercke, is an appendage of the altar of Rousselaere; in that place a priest is appointed from among the religious of Sonnebecq.]

[Note: [Col. 0278D] Bevenslaer, commonly Becclaere. The aforesaid prelate of that place is patron, but does not appoint a religious as priest.]

Whatever further fortification or liberty our aforesaid brother Drogo bestowed upon that place, we ratify by the authority of the present decree, prohibiting anyone from presuming to diminish, withdraw, or alienate it in any manner. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted, being useful to them in every respect.

If anyone—God forbid—shall rashly attempt to oppose this our decree, let him incur the loss of his honor and office, or be punished by the penalty of excommunication, unless he corrects his presumption by worthy satisfaction [Col. 0279B].

Thus it is subscribed.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, deacon-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

### CCCV. He confirms the possessions of the Church of Saint Donatian at Bruges.  
*(Year 1110, October 16.)*

[MIRAEUS, cited above, p. 26.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ BERTULF, provost of Saint Donatian’s at Bruges, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to be concerned for the condition of churches and to establish firmly what has been rightly instituted. Therefore we graciously assent to your petitions and decree that the things bestowed in our time for the support of your congregation, and also those known to have been granted before our time by our fellow bishops, shall remain undisturbed for you and your successors: namely, the altar of Holy Cross; the altar of Saint Michael; and the altars of Orscamp, Rhidervorde, Wara, Ema, Dicasnuda, Clare, Widescate, Kemla, Dudezela, Utkerka, Clemskerka [Col. 0279D], Artrika, and Lophem.

We decree accordingly that no one may diminish, withdraw, or alienate in any way either these things or others which, by God’s grace, have been or shall be given for the use of your congregation. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, being useful for every purpose. But if anyone—God forbid—shall rashly attempt to oppose this decree of ours, let him incur the loss of his honor and office [Col. 0280A], unless he corrects his presumption by worthy satisfaction.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1110 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, pope.

### CCCVI. To Leodegarius, bishop of Viviers.—He rebukes him because he allows the church of Saint Andeolus, which he had granted to the canons of Saint-Ruf, to be taken away from them by his clerics.  
*(Year 1110, October 18.)*

[BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 47.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the bishop of Viviers, greetings and apostolic [Col. 0280B] blessing.

It is not episcopal constancy to break just vows and reduce right ordinances to nothing. You had granted the church of Blessed Andeolus to the brethren of Saint-Ruf for almsgiving and religious purposes, and had confirmed this by the consent of your clerics, as we have learned from the brethren themselves and as we have known by reading your letters. But now you appear to connive with your clerics, since you allow them to take that church away from the aforesaid brethren. We indeed canonically confirm the grant which was made; but we strongly rebuke you, because in this matter you have shown yourself a violator of faith.

By these writings, therefore, we command your prudence to preserve your ordinance whole and valid. If, however, your clerics, as transgressors of a just vow [Col. 0280C], presumptuously persist in opposition, you must correct them by the right of a master and endeavor to reform them with fitting severity; otherwise the justice of the Apostolic See will be directed against you.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of November.

### CCCVII. To Diego, bishop of Compostela.—He urges him to ensure that Queen Urraca, daughter of the king of Castile, desists, under penalty of deprivation of the kingdom, from the incest she contracted by marrying Alfonso, king of Aragon, who was related to her in the third degree of consanguinity.  
*(About the year 1110.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1006.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother DIDACUS, bishop of Compostela, greetings [Col. 0280D] and apostolic blessing.

Almighty God has established you to preside over His people so that you may correct their sins and proclaim the Lord’s will. And further on: “Therefore endeavor, according to the authority divinely granted to you, to correct by due punishment so great a crime of incest, committed by the king’s daughter, so that she may either desist from so great a presumption or be deprived of communion with the Church and of secular power,” etc.

[Note: [Col. 0279D] We have found copied from Pope Paschal’s letters only these words. But when they had not obeyed the apostolic commands, they experienced God as avenger. For Urraca, having burst open through the middle, died a sudden death; and Alfonso was slain in war against the Saracens, as both Roderics affirm. SEV. BIN.]

### CCCVIII. To Pons, abbot, and the monks of Cluny.—He reproves them for having caused chrism to be consecrated in their monastery.  
*(About the year 1110.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1043, from Severus’s *Chronology*.]

[Col. 0281A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PONS, abbot, and the monks of the monastery of Cluny, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Our fellow bishop Berard of Mâcon, partly at our request and partly through his own uprightness, behaved kindly toward your predecessor, the venerable Abbot Hugh. When he departed intending to go to Jerusalem, all matters between you and him were quiet and peaceful. But after his departure [Col. 0281B] you greatly disturbed the rights of the Church of Mâcon, because you caused chrism to be consecrated in your monastery—something that has not hitherto been done. For this is supplied to the Church through the person of the bishop.

We therefore ask your belovedness to correct this in complete charity, and likewise to conduct yourselves toward him in other matters so that the bond of your former peace may be more closely drawn between you. For he loves you most fully, and ought to be loved most fully by you. Therefore we command that such things not be done hereafter. We have not forgotten with what zeal and earnestness we labored that firm and stable concord might remain between you. We desire and command that this be kept secure, so that the Church may suffer no further injury. May divine mercy preserve you [Col. 0281C] for us as we pray.

### CCCIX. To the canons of the Church of Lucca.  
*(Between the years 1103–1111, November 4.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, Lucca edition, IV, 586.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, the canons of the Church of Lucca, greetings and apostolic blessing.

You ought to rejoice greatly in the Lord because in your time the first beginnings of apostolic life have flourished anew in your parish—namely, in the church of Blessed Fridianus. You should therefore love that congregation more earnestly and, according to the measure of your resources, foster and honor it. By these present letters we stir up your belovedness, warning [Col. 0281D] and commanding you to embrace the canons of Blessed Fridianus more dearly in the Lord’s love; neither cause them any molestation yourselves nor allow others to inflict it upon them.

For whatever proof and hardship, honor and reverence, you bestow upon them, we count as bestowed upon ourselves. We are indeed astonished at what your fellow brother, the archpriest, is said to have done against them. For a certain convert, who, after promising obedience, returned to the vanities of the world, was excommunicated for this reason by the aforesaid prior. Enticed by a simulated absolution, he remained in apostasy; indeed, when he believed himself absolved, he became more firmly bound [Col. 0282A].

Therefore we forbid any further presumption of this sort. Do not excommunicate their parishioners or admit them to penance without their consent. Conduct yourselves toward them in all things in such a way that suitable peace may remain for them and full charity between you may endure by God’s grace.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Nones of November.

### CCCX. To the parishioners of the Church of Saint Fridianus at Lucca.  
*(Between the years 1103–1111, November 4.)*

[BALUZE, cited above.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the parishioners of the Church of Saint Fridianus, greetings and apostolic blessing.

We have long learned, from the report of many persons, of the devotion which you bear toward the church of Blessed Fridianus [Col. 0282B]. Therefore, rejoicing with due affection, we give thanks to God and pray that by His grace He may deign to preserve His love in your hearts. Visiting you by these present letters as beloved sons in Christ, we exhort you henceforth to remain steadfast, with God’s help, in that devotion and good purpose; and by God’s grace so to offer that place the assistance of your counsel and aid that those serving the Lord there may have support, and that you may deserve to obtain forgiveness of your sins.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Nones of November.

### CCCXI. To the clergy and people of Arles.—That they should elect another in place of their bishop Gibelin, who had been transferred to Jerusalem.  
*(Year 1111, January 2.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1003.]

[Note: [Col. 0281D] In the charter of Baldwin, king of Jerusalem, in William of Tyre, book XI, chapter 12, issued in 1110, Gibelin is described as “elected patriarch” [Col. 0282D]. G. Robert of Monte, *Patrologia* CLX, under this year. JAFFÉ.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the clergy and people of Arles, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Because of the affairs and disturbances which existed in the Church of Jerusalem, we sent our venerable brother Gibelin, formerly bishop of your church, to those regions with our legation. His person pleased everyone so greatly that the clergy and people of that church elected him, by unanimous vote and common desire, to be their father and shepherd. Since they had long been deprived of episcopal government [Col. 0282D], we confirmed the election by our approval.

We therefore warn and exhort your belovedness in the Lord by these present letters that you too should hasten to elect a canonical shepherd for yourselves, and not regard the matter as especially burdensome and harsh. For the Church of Jerusalem has received him with such ardor that, even if we desired it altogether, we could in no way restore him to you.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of January.

### CCCXII. To King Henry.—He congratulates him because he “abhors his father’s wickedness.” He affirms that, if Henry “shows to himself and to his lawful successors, with full devotion of mind, the obedience which kings or emperors have shown to their Catholic predecessors,” he will certainly regard him as a Catholic emperor. He wishes envoys to be sent to him.

*(Year 1111.—See PETER’S Chronicle of the Monastery of Cassino, p. 779.)*

### CCCXIII. He invites the Normans and Lombards to the service of the Roman Church.

*(Year 1111, February.—See cited work.)*

### CCCXIV–CCCXV. He commands King Henry that the regalian rights be restored by bishops and abbots.  
*(Year 1111, February.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 42.]

[Col. 0283B] PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HENRY, king, and to his successors.

Both the ordinance of divine law has decreed and the sacred canons have forbidden that priests should be occupied with secular cares, or should attend a court except to rescue condemned persons or others suffering injury. The Apostle Paul also says: “If you have secular lawsuits, appoint as judges those who are of least account among you.” Yet in the regions of your kingdom bishops and abbots are so occupied with secular wealth that they are compelled constantly to attend court and to perform military service. Such things are indeed rarely, or never, carried out without robberies, sacrileges, burnings, or killings.

The ministers of the altar have become ministers of the court, since they have received from kings cities, duchies, marches, mints, estates, and other things. Now too an intolerable custom has become established in the Church: bishops-elect are in no way to receive consecration unless first invested by the royal hand. As a result, the depravity of the Simoniacal heresy and ambition have sometimes prevailed so greatly that episcopal sees were seized without any election having preceded; at times persons were invested even while bishops were still living.

Moved by these and many other evils which had commonly arisen through investiture, our predecessors, the popes Gregory VII and Urban II of happy memory, frequently assembled episcopal councils and condemned those investitures by a lay hand. They decreed that clerics who had obtained churches through them should be deposed, and that those who conferred them should be deprived of communion, in accordance with the chapter of the Apostolic Canons which reads thus: “If any bishop, having employed secular powers, has or obtains a church through them, let him be deposed and separated, together with everyone who communicates with him.”

Moreover, we expressly decree that churches, with the offerings and hereditary possessions which manifestly did not belong to the kingdom, are free, just as on the day of your coronation you promised Almighty God in the presence of the whole Church. Bishops, freed from secular concerns, ought to care for their peoples and not be absent from their churches for long. According to the Apostle Paul, they keep watch as those who will render an account for their souls. Following in their footsteps [Col. 0284A], we too confirm their decision by an episcopal council.

Therefore, dearest son King Henry—now, through our office and by God’s grace, emperor of the Romans—we command you and the kingdom to relinquish those regalian rights which in the time of Charles, Louis, Henry, and your other predecessors manifestly belonged to the kingdom. We prohibit and, under the strictness of anathema, forbid any present or future bishop or abbot to seize those same regalian rights: cities, duchies, marches, counties, mints, tolls, markets, royal advocacies, the rights of centurions, and estates which manifestly belonged to the kingdom, with their appurtenances; the military service and castles of the kingdom. Nor shall they henceforth concern themselves with those regalian rights except by the king’s favor [Col. 0284B]. Nor shall it be lawful for our successors who succeed us in the Apostolic See to trouble either you or the kingdom concerning this matter.

### CCCXVI. A privilege concerning investitures, extorted by force.  
*(Year 1111, April 12.)*

[PERTZ, *Monumenta Germaniae Historica, Leges*, II, 72.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ H., glorious king of the Germans and, by the grace of Almighty God, august emperor of the Romans, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Divine providence has ordained that your kingdom should be especially joined to the Holy Roman Church [Col. 0284C]. Your predecessors obtained the crown and empire of the city of Rome through the abundant merit of their uprightness and prudence. To the dignity of that crown and empire, divine majesty has likewise advanced your person, dearest son H., through the ministry of our priesthood.

Therefore, the prerogative of dignity which our predecessors granted to your predecessors, the Catholic emperors, and confirmed in charters of privilege, we likewise grant to your belovedness and confirm by this page of the present privilege: namely, that you may confer investiture by staff and ring upon bishops or abbots of your kingdom freely elected without simony or violence. After investiture, however, let them receive canonical consecration from the bishop to whom they belong. If anyone has been elected by clergy and people without your consent, let him be consecrated by no one unless he is invested by you [Col. 0284D]. Bishops and archbishops shall indeed have the liberty canonically to consecrate bishops or abbots invested by you.

For your predecessors enlarged the churches of their kingdom with such great benefactions from their regalian rights that the kingdom itself must chiefly be fortified by the support of bishops and abbots, and popular dissensions, which often occur in elections, must be restrained by royal majesty. For this reason, the concern of your prudence and power ought diligently to ensure that, by the Lord’s aid, the greatness of the Roman Church and the welfare of the other churches are preserved through more ample benefactions.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our grant [Col. 0285A], let that person, unless he repents, be bound by the bond of anathema and incur the loss of honor and dignity. May divine mercy protect those who observe it, and grant that your person and power may rule prosperously to His honor and glory. Amen.

### CCCXVII. He grants Otto, bishop of Bamberg, and his successors the use of the pallium and the privilege of having the cross borne before them.  
*(Year 1111, April 15.)*

[LUDEWIG, *Scriptores rerum Germanicarum*, I, 413.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother OTTO, bishop of Bamberg, greetings and apostolic blessing.

It is characteristic of charity to rejoice in the good progress [Col. 0285B] of others; for “charity does not seek its own things” (1 Corinthians 13). Hence also the Apostle says: “Then we live, if you stand firm in the Lord” (1 Thessalonians 3). And again: “For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of glory? Is it not you before our Lord Jesus Christ?” (1 Thessalonians 2).

Moved by this obligation of charity and compelled by the authority of the Apostolic See, we are bound on this account to render what is due to our brethren and to impart, according to each church’s appropriate measure, the dignity of the Holy Roman Church to the other churches. Therefore, venerable brother Otto, bishop of Bamberg, we grant your belovedness the pallium for celebrating the solemnities of the sacred Masses. Your fraternity shall know that it may be used only within the church and only on the days contained in this present document: namely, on the holy day of the Lord’s Resurrection [Col. 0285C] and Pentecost; likewise the Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ; the feast day of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul; the feast of Saint Dionysius the martyr; the anniversary day of your consecration; and dedications of churches. We wish you to uphold in every respect the grace of this pallium, whose honor consists in humility and justice.

Therefore, with your whole mind, let your fraternity hasten to show yourself humble in prosperity and, should adversities ever come, upright with justice; friendly to the good and opposed to the wicked; never accepting anyone’s person against truth, never oppressing anyone speaking for truth; being devoted to works of mercy according to the truth of your means, yet desiring to devote yourself even beyond your means [Col. 0285D]; showing compassion to the weak, rejoicing with those in health; counting another’s interests as your own, and exulting in others’ joys as in your own; being mercifully stern in correcting vices, and soothing the minds of hearers in fostering virtues; maintaining judgment without anger in anger, yet not abandoning the censure of just severity in tranquillity.

This, therefore, dearest brother, is the dignity of the pallium received; if you preserve it diligently, you will possess inwardly what you are shown to have received outwardly. Moreover, we grant that the banner of the cross may be borne before you within the parish of the Church of Bamberg, with the reverence due to the metropolitan see of Mainz preserved. Thus endowed with a special dignity of the Roman Church, you may devote yourself especially to obedience and service to it. May heavenly favor preserve your fraternity unharmed for long years [Col. 0286A]. Amen.

Written through the hand of John, regional scriniarius and notary of the Sacred Palace.

### CCCXVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Hersfeld.  
*(Year 1111, April 15.)*

[WENCK, *Hessian State History*, II, 58.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ REGINHARD, abbot of the monastery of Hersfeld, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Just as no effect should be granted to those who seek unjust things, so the petition of those who desire lawful things should not be delayed. Accordingly, dearest son in Christ Reginhard [Col. 0286B], assenting to your petitions, we confirm through this page of the present privilege for your venerable monastery of Hersfeld whatever is known to belong to it through lawful donations of the faithful. Among these things, we particularly decree that the testament of the devout emperor Charles, which he assigned to your monastery, shall remain valid.

We likewise grant, by the authority of the present decree, the tithes which the same monastery has possessed from ancient times and which were granted to your predecessors by privileges of our predecessors, the pontiffs of the Apostolic See. Whatever it may hereafter be able justly and canonically to acquire by grant of pontiffs, generosity of princes, or offering of the faithful shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors [Col. 0286C].

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the same monastery, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it by reckless vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted, being of use to them in every respect. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any craft of intrigue or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or the sounder part of the brethren, elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict, whether from their own community or, if necessary, from another.

If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution [Col. 0286D], and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person lose the dignity of honor and power; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just toward that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and finally find, before the strict Judge, eternal rewards.

I, Paschal, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

[Col. 0287A] Given at Rome, on the island of Lycaonia, through the hand of John, deacon-cardinal and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, acting in place of Deacon Frederick, archchancellor and archbishop of Cologne, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1111 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Paschal II, and in the first year of the empire of Emperor Henry IV.

### CCCXIX. To Emperor Henry.  
*(Year 1111.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1094.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved son HENRY, august emperor of the Romans, greetings and apostolic blessing.

After a short interval, we have heard something unfavorable concerning you [Col. 0287B], which greatly troubles us. It has reached us that, to disturb the peace of the Church, you intend to release H. at Aricia, so that he may retain the possessions taken from the Church and not cease to trouble the remainder. We had thought that those who remain in our fidelity remained with us on the shore; but, as a true report has revealed, our brother of Arezzo is still tossed amid storms and sees the harbor from afar.

We therefore ask and admonish your belovedness by these present letters, as we trust in you, to restore your favor to our aforesaid brother and restore the possessions of the Church. Also command his faithful men no longer to withdraw themselves from his service. For they cannot persecute the members and be cut off without injury to the head, and insult to the sons pertains to injury to the father. Love, therefore, those whom we love, so that we may hate those whom you hate and love those whom you love. Henceforth may Almighty God, in His mercy, guard and preserve you.

### CCCXX. To the people of Arezzo.  
*(Year 1111.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1092.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the clergy and citizens of Arezzo, greetings and apostolic blessing.

By the authority of our office we are compelled to bear concern for all churches [Col. 0287D]; therefore we have decided to send you this present letter on behalf of our venerable brother, your bishop. We have heard that you neither treat him with due reverence nor render him due obedience. This certainly wholly contradicts the divine ordinance.

For when the Lord Jesus Christ redeemed the holy Church by the shedding of His precious blood, He appointed in it shepherds to administer saving things to His people in His stead. Hence those who inflict injuries upon them and despise their commands are known to inflict injury upon and despise the Lord Himself, as He says: “He who touches you touches the pupil of my eye; and he who despises you despises me.”

We therefore command all of you to return, by the coming Nativity of the Lord, to obedience to the aforesaid brother, your bishop [Col. 0288A], and to love him with due affection as father, teacher, and God’s vicar, and venerate him with due reverence. Otherwise, from the authority which we bear by divine ordering through our ministry, we lay upon you a temporal interdict, and prohibit the very spiritual sustenance—the divine offices—until you repent. It is fitting that you who despise God in His ministry should likewise lack God’s benefit and the ministry of His vicar.

### CCCXXI. To Emperor Henry, ordained by him.  
*(Year 1111, May 3.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1093.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ HENRY, august emperor of the Romans, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Since your presence departed from us, no report concerning the soundness of your condition has reached our hearing. Nevertheless, because it is our wish gladly to learn of your prosperity and to communicate ours to you in return, we inform your excellency of our own circumstances through the account of these present letters. By God’s grace, we are well, although some have still refused to obey your command in matters which you ordered restored to Blessed Peter—namely, the inhabitants of the city of Castellana, the castle of Corcolo, Monte Alto, Monte Acuto, and the people of Narni. Yet through the force of your command we trust to obtain these places, and also the county of Perugia, that of Gubbio, that of Todi, Bagnoregio [Col. 0288C], the castle of Felicitas, the duchy of Spoleto, the March of Fermo, and the other possessions of Blessed Peter.

As we have heard, the son of our faithful Count Rusticellus is being detained by some of your people. We ask your belovedness, therefore, to have him restored to us, because he too is a faithful man of Blessed Peter and resides on his estate. We most earnestly exhort your serenity always to love justice and embrace it with all your strength and endeavor, so that He who is the true king, emperor, and judge may grant you a crown and glory in the perpetuity of His kingdom and empire.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Nones of May.

### CCCXXII. He asks Emperor Henry to order the return of goods taken from the Church of Rimini.  
*(Year 1111.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 1094.]

[Col. 0288D]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his son in Christ HENRY, august emperor of the Romans, greetings and apostolic blessing.

The bishopric of Rimini is manifestly among the special rights of blessed Peter; yet, because of sins, it has been stripped of almost all its goods and reduced to the smallest remnants. We therefore ask your affection that, for love of blessed Peter, your kindness order its goods restored to it, and that, once restored, it may, by the Lord’s grant, obtain peace.

### CCCXXIII. To Baldwin, King of Jerusalem.—He decrees that, in order to enlarge the bounds of the diocese of Jerusalem, all cities which he subdues shall be subject to Jerusalem as their metropolitan. (A.D. 1111, June 8.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1005.]

[Col. 0289A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the glorious BALDWIN, king of Jerusalem, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

The long possession of unbelievers and tyrants has thrown into confusion the boundaries and possessions of the churches which were or are in your regions. Since, therefore, we cannot by deliberation assign its certain boundaries, we have rightly judged that your request should be granted: because you have devoted yourself to expose your person to the utmost dangers for the exaltation of the Church of Jerusalem, whatever cities of the unbelievers you have captured or shall capture shall be subject to the governance and dignity of that same Church. Moreover, the bishops of those cities shall endeavor to render obedience to the patriarch as to their own metropolitan; so that, supported by their assistance, and they in turn strengthened by the help of his unity, they may so advance in the exaltation of the Church of Jerusalem that almighty God may be glorified in their progress.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of June.

### CCCXXIV. To Gibelin, Patriarch of Jerusalem.—On the same subject. (A.D. 1111.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 0289C]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most reverend brother GIBELIN, patriarch of Jerusalem, and to his successors canonically promoted in perpetuity, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

According to changes of times, the kingdoms of the earth are also transferred. Hence it is fitting that the boundaries of ecclesiastical dioceses likewise be altered and transferred in many provinces. The boundaries of the Asian churches had indeed been apportioned by ancient determinations; but the incursions of diverse peoples of diverse faith have thrown those distributions into confusion. Thanks be to God, however, that in our times the cities of Antioch and Jerusalem, [Col. 0289D] together with their surrounding districts and adjacent provinces, have been brought under the power of Christian princes. It is therefore fitting for us to put our hand to this divine change and transfer, and, according to the time, to order what must be ordered: so that we may grant to the Church of Jerusalem those cities and provinces which have been acquired, through God’s grace, by the blood of the glorious King Baldwin and the army following him.

Therefore, by the authority of this present decree, we ordain that all the cities and provinces which divine grace has already restored, or shall in the future deign to restore, to the dominion of the aforesaid king be governed and administered by you, dearest brother and fellow bishop Gibelin, and by your successors, and through you by the holy Church of Jerusalem, under patriarchal or metropolitan right. [Col. 0290A] For it is fitting that the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre, in accordance with the desires of Christ’s faithful soldiers, receive due honor and, freed from the yoke of Turks or Saracens, be more abundantly exalted in Christian hands.

### CCCXXV. He thanks Emperor Henry for ordering the restoration of goods lost by the clergy of Padua and by Judge H. (A.D. 1111.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1094.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his son in Christ HENRY, august emperor, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

We give thanks to your affection on behalf of the clergy of Padua and Judge H., because you restored to them your favor and ordered their goods, which they had lost, to be restored. We ask further on behalf of the laymen that you receive them into your favor and cause their goods to be restored to them, so that henceforth, under the protection of your safeguard and with God’s help, they may be able to remain in peace.

### CCCXXVI. To Emperor Henry. (A.D. 1111, about June.)

Udalric of Bamberg, codex no. 267, in ECCARD, *Corpus Historiae*, II, 275.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ HENRY, august emperor of the Romans, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0290C] We always wish to hear good things concerning your magnificence, as concerning a son of the Church whom divine Providence has established as prince and defender of the Church. We therefore admonish your affection, and in admonishing ask, that you consider the gifts of divine dispensation which you have received, and that, both in the fear of the Lord and in reverence for the Church and defense of justice, you may advance, as you ought and as you are able, with that same Lord granting it. Indeed, we pray almighty God for this: that not only we, but the whole Catholic Church as well, may glory in your advancement.

We sent our legate after you; but, having come as far as Ravenna, he feared to proceed farther because of the disturbances of the roads that occur after the army’s passage. When almighty God has brought us [Col. 0290D] to a suitable time, we shall, through his grace, arrange the sending of a legate as may be expedient.

### CCCXXVII. To John of Tusculum and Leo, bishops of Vercelli and cardinals.—He promises to annul and invalidate the concession of investitures made to the emperor. (A.D. 1111, July 5.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1008.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers JOHN of Tusculum and LEO of Vercelli, bishops and cardinals assembled together, fellowship and peace in Christ.

What you did against our person—or rather against your father—apart from the judgment and presence of this Church, although it may have seemed to you to arise from zeal for God, nevertheless, as it seems to me, you did not proceed by a canonical path; for it is clear that not charity but rivalry dictated it. Yet, however it was done, trusting in divine mercy and considering the salvation of our soul, we shall take care to amend what we did for our brothers and sons, because of the destruction of the City and the whole province, so that what earthly men have corrected in me may also be shown corrected by the Church. But do you act for the Church within the Church, so that the Church itself may experience that zeal for the Church of God which you have and show that you have. Farewell in the Lord.

Given at Terracina, on the third day before the Nones of July.

### CCCXXVIII. *To Bruno, bishop of Segni and abbot of Monte Cassino: he writes that “a bishop ought not at the same time to be an abbot.” He orders him to relinquish the abbacy.*

[Col. 0291B]

(A.D. 1111.—See the *Chronicle of the Monastery of Monte Cassino*, pp. 783–784.)

### CCCXXIX. *He releases the monks of Monte Cassino from obedience to Bruno and orders a successor to be substituted for him; unless they do so, he declares that he will place separate abbots over all the cells of the monastery.*

(A.D. 1111.—See Peter’s *Chronicle of the Monastery of Monte Cassino*, p. 783, and the *Life of St. Bruno*, *Acta Sanctorum*, July, IV, 484.)

### CCCXXX. *He urges the people of Segni to take another bishop for themselves in Bruno’s place.*

[Col. 0291C]

(A.D. 1111.—*Life of St. Bruno*, *Acta Sanctorum*, July, vol. IV, 484.)

### CCCXXXI. To Emperor Henry. (A.D. 1111, October 26.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1094.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his son in Christ HENRY, august emperor, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

From the letters which we received from your affection, we learned that you had long been gravely ill; but as the report of your illness had afflicted us, so the news of your recovery has in turn made us glad. We give thanks to God for the prosperity which you have reported to us, for he orders all things by an inestimable providence.

What you complain of concerning the bishops [Col. 0291D] greatly distresses our heart. For since we made with you that agreement which you know, not only those far away, but even those who are about us, have raised their necks against us; they tear our vitals apart with internal wars and cover our face with great shame. Since we cannot obtain judgment concerning them, we leave them to judgment, lest we more grievously disturb God’s Church.

Moreover, although we endure such great and such grievous things, we are surprised that your N. brings oppressions upon all the churches which he occupies and ravages in hostile fashion, and, forgetful of the mutual agreement, claims for his own usurpation things which belong to our right. We are likewise surprised that the hostages given by us [Col. 0292A] are, as we have heard, harshly, shamefully, and tyrannically treated; matters which assuredly bear no little upon injury to your highness. Yet amid all these things we admonish you, the foremost son of the Church, always to fear God’s judgments, remembering that time which you described in your letters, saying: “In the very time of our most grievous illness, when our life was in doubt, when only the expectation of our dissolution was entertained”; and strive so to please him that he may order for you his favor and an earthly kingdom, and bring you to eternal kingdoms.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Kalends of November.

### CCCXXXII. To Guy, Archbishop of Vienne.—Investiture of clerics is to be taken from kings. (A.D. 1111.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XX, 1008.]

[Col. 0292B]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GUY, archbishop of Vienne and legate of the apostolic see, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

If that savage barbarity tries to bend your constancy by threats, blandishments, or other means, let your prudence remain immovable. For if this was done to the green wood, what shall be done to the others? If this was perpetrated in the head, what shall be done in the members? Therefore, dearest brother, remain steadfastly and manfully, with God’s help, in your good undertaking. Let threats, [Col. 0292C] blandishments, or other modes of persuasion or dissuasion not move your foresight; but, with the Lord’s help, endure in such a way that your constancy may be an example to others of saving perseverance.

What you asked to be informed of is this: the documents made in the tents in which I was held under guard with a multitude of clerics and citizens of the City and of the whole province, for the liberty of the Church, for the release of all captives, and because destruction seemed to threaten the Church, the City, and the whole province, with the sword hanging over them on every side—namely, the documents concerning election and the investiture of persons, providing that, after a free election without force or simony, and with the king’s consent, the king should have the power to invest with staff and ring, [Col. 0292D] and that a person elected by clergy and people should not be consecrated unless invested by the king—I judge wholly void and invalid by canonical sentence, and decree that they remain under perpetual condemnation, so that they may never possess any authority or any good repute.

But those things which the sacred canons of the apostles, the Council of Antioch, the universal councils, and our predecessors—and especially the lords Gregory and Urban of happy memory—have concerning these matters forbidden, condemned, established, and confirmed, I forbid, condemn, establish, and confirm; and I profess that I shall observe their enactments.

### CCCXXXIII. *To Ivo, bishop of Chartres, concerning church investitures, he writes that “he did what he did under compulsion, and still forbids what he forbade, although he permitted certain abominable things to be written by certain abominable persons.”*

[Col. 0293A]

(A.D. 1111.—See Ivo’s letters 233 and 236.)

### CCCXXXIV. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Corvey (diocese of Paderborn).

(See the *Annals of Corvey* for A.D. 1111, in PERTZ, *Monumenta Germaniae Historica, Scriptores* III, 7.)

### CCCXXXV. To Ralph, Archbishop of Tours, and fellow bishops, on behalf of the abbot of Saint-Albinus. (A.D. 1112, February 15.)

[MABILLON, *Annals of the Benedictines*, Appendix, 67.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable [Col. 0293B] brothers and fellow bishops R. [RALPH] of Tours, I. [HILDEBERT] of Le Mans, and M. [MARBOD] of Rennes, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

The holy Roman Church, as she is mother of all, so embraces all with maternal charity and strives to assist all who seek her mercy. The bearer of the present letters, P. [Paganus] Alerici, lodged his complaint with us: although the brothers of the monastery of Saint-Albinus had placed him in the office and authority of abbot, our brother R., bishop of Angers, expelled him from that seat and authority under an interdict of anathema without hearing or judgment, and, after an appeal to the apostolic see, restored A. [Archembald], who had renounced that same abbacy.

He also complained that the brothers who had elected him were forbidden to give him help or counsel, and that those who had appealed with him or on his behalf were afterwards deprived of their offices and obediences. [Col. 0293C] He made another complaint: that, for the prosecution of his appeal and cause, he had requested common expenses from those who appeared to govern the aforesaid abbey, but could by no means obtain them. In these matters, certainly, if they are true, no small injury has been inflicted not only upon the appellant, but also upon the apostolic see to which the appeal was made.

We therefore command your experience, within forty days after receiving this letter, to take care to assemble in the chapter-house of Saint-Albinus at Angers, with our brothers G., abbot of Vendôme, G., abbot of Saint-Florent, G., abbot of Saint-Serge, and R. of Arbrissel, and, with the Lord’s help, to settle this cause in canonical order. If one of you is prevented by an urgent necessity from being present, let the others carry out the matter; and we command that the monks who elected the aforesaid brother P. Alerici be present for this business, liberty being granted them to defend his cause.

Meanwhile, let what P. spent on his dispute be restored to him by the readers of that monastery, and henceforth, until the conclusion of the case, let what is necessary be supplied to him and his followers. Moreover, let his brothers have restored to them in full their offices and obediences of which they were deprived after the appeal to the apostolic see. [Col. 0294A] We have also heard that this same brother P. Alerici is exposed to plundering by laymen. We therefore admonish your brotherhood to enjoin, on our behalf, our beloved son F., count of the Angevins, to protect him and all his people by the safeguard of his office.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March.

### CCCXXXVI. To Lambert, Bishop of Arras. (A.D. 1112, March 27.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, Lucchesi edition, II, 1557.]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0294B] When the abbot of Saint-Vaast came to us, we retained him with us for several days at the request of your letters. But since, during so long a period, none of your clergy arrived in our presence, it seemed expedient that he should be dismissed with the attestation of our letters. We therefore approve that the case pending between him and your clergy be decided in your hearing, in the presence of our fellow brothers, the bishops of Thérouanne and Amiens, so that long possession, lawfully proved according to your judgment, may obtain peace. We also ask that you administer justice to that same abbot concerning the altar of Hénin.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of April.

### CCCXXXVII. To the Same. (A.D. 1111, April 9.)

[BALUZE, *ibid.*]

[Col. 0294C]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

You are to know that the complaints of your clergy against the monks of Saint-Vaast, and likewise those of the monks of Saint-Vaast against your clergy, have been decided as follows. Having heard the arguments of both parties, it was judged by the common deliberation of the brethren that both chapels—namely, Holy Cross and Saint Maurice—shall remain with the monks as is contained in the written instrument of Gerard, bishop of Cambrai [Note: [Col. 0293] It is extant in Locher’s *Chronicle of Belgium*, p. 226.], who was then visitor of Arras.

Moreover, from the new borough of the mother church, the clergy shall receive first-fruits, tithes, and three annual solemn offerings: namely, those of Easter, Pentecost, and the Nativity of the Lord. But the voluntary offerings and one half of the alms which, from that borough or by the disposition of dying persons, are assigned to the churches, or are divided through the agency of trustees, shall, whenever they happen to be offered, be received peacefully and freely by that monastery without any opposition from the clergy; provided, however, that the other half is not withdrawn from the mother church. The priests serving as chaplains shall render the bishop the customary obedience.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of April.

### CCCXXXVIII. He confirms that the monastery of Monte Cassino is to be preferred to other monasteries throughout the West, free from every jurisdiction and subject to the holy Roman Church alone; and decrees under anathema that its abbot, in every assembly of bishops and princes, shall hold a place above all other abbots and shall speak first among all members of his order. (A.D. 1112, February 4.)

[MARGARINI, *Bullarium of Monte Cassino*, II, 129.]

[Col. 0295A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most reverend and most dear brother GERARD, consecrated by our hands, through God’s grace, as abbot of the monastery of Monte Cassino, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 0295B] It is written: “The gifts and calling of God are without repentance.” Therefore no repentance can oppose that gift which divine grace bestowed upon our most blessed father Benedict, author of the monastic rule; and he himself, the father of all monks, together with his monastery of Monte Cassino, in which he both lived and died, shall forever be regarded as the head of all monasteries throughout the West. Accordingly, pursuing the purpose of the divine ordinance, we embrace that monastery with special affection and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, decree that it is to be preferred to the other monasteries throughout the West and remain forever under the right and protection of the apostolic see alone.

And we decree that both you and your successors shall sit above all abbots in every assembly [Col. 0295C] of bishops or princes, and in judicial proceedings shall pronounce an opinion before the other men of your order. If, in the future, any archbishop or bishop, emperor or king, prince or duke, count, viscount, judge, or ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, attempts to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes suitable satisfaction and amendment, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for that monastery, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

Written by the hand of Rainerius, scrivener and notary of the sacred palace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of John, cardinal-deacon and librarian of the holy Roman Church, on the day before the Nones of February, in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1113 [1112], and in the thirteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Paschal II.

### CCCXXXIX. Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud. (A.D. 1112, April 5.)

[PAVILLON, *Life of Blessed Robert of Arbrissel*, Proofs, p. 607.]

[Col. 0296A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sisters in Christ, nuns serving almighty God in the monastery of Fontevraud, both present and future, in perpetuity.

Since, by the authority and benevolence of the apostolic see, we stand indebted to all the children of the holy Church, it is fitting that we attend with a more earnest zeal of charity to those places and persons which adhere more specially and intimately to the Roman Church and which stand out through a more abundant grace of religious life. Therefore, moved by the more ardent efforts of your religious observance and inclined by the prayers of the venerable man Robert of Arbrissel, we have undertaken to cherish under the special protection of the apostolic see your monastery, built by the aforesaid Robert and, by the Lord’s gift, to be consecrated in honor of the Blessed Mary ever Virgin.
