Otherwise, for receiving those [Col. 1207A] sacraments, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer. Moreover, we forbid anyone to seize the advocacy of your house, whether an heir of the founders or any other person, without the consent of the provost and brethren. No person whatsoever may therefore rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain or diminish possessions taken away, or harass it through rash vexations; rather, let them be preserved intact, wholly beneficial for the use of those for whose support and governance they were granted. As a token of the liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one gold coin annually to the Lateran palace. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our enactment, etc.

[Col. 1207B]

I, Calixtus, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh Ides of May, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1122, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus II.

### CXXXIII. To Franco, abbot of Tournus.—A privilege of immunity. (1121, May 18.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 205.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son FRANCO, abbot of Tournus, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 1207C]

It befits us to assist and foster venerable places dedicated to God with the greater zeal because, by divine ordering, their care and protection are known to rest more particularly upon us. Therefore, dearest son in Christ, Abbot Franco, we incline our ears to your petition with the affection of due kindness. And because the monastery of Tournus belongs in a special manner to the protection of Blessed Peter, whose right it is, and because the church now standing there was consecrated by our hands through God’s grace, we strengthen that place by the singular protection of the Apostolic See.

By the authority of this present decree, therefore, we establish that henceforth no bishop may inflict any burden concerning altars and churches, tithes, or anything rightly belonging to them, which you were known to possess before the interdiction of our predecessor Pope Urban of holy memory, or which you acquired afterward by concession of bishops. Rather, as you held some things partly and others wholly by their permission, so you shall hold them perpetually in the future. You may lawfully possess for your own support and that of the poor the tithes of the churches you now hold which are possessed by laymen, if reverence for your religious house can withdraw them from lay control. [Col. 1207D]

Moreover, whatever you may hereafter, through the Lord’s bounty, be able justly to acquire shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We further add that the same place, where rest the bodies of Blessed Valerian the martyr and St. Philibert the confessor, [Col. 1208A] shall henceforth be preserved free from every yoke of secular authority. No bishop of any diocese may disturb that place under pretext of excommunication, absolution, or any other administrative act, or impose crosses or any new exactions upon the borough or the other possessions of the monastery.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our enactment, should rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amends through fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and rank, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be separated from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and [Col. 1208B] be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Calixtus, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Given at Alba through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1122, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus.

### CXXXIV. To the same.—Another privilege. (1121, May 18.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1208C]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son FRANCO, abbot of Tournus, and to his successors regularly appointed.

It befits us to assist and foster venerable places dedicated to God with the greater zeal because, by divine ordering, their care and protection are known to rest more particularly upon us. Therefore, dearest son in Christ, Abbot Franco, we incline our ears to your petition with the affection of due kindness. And because the monastery of Tournus belongs in a special manner to the protection of Blessed Peter, whose right it is, and because the church now standing there was consecrated by our hands [Col. 1208D] through God’s grace, we strengthen that place by the singular protection of the Apostolic See.

By the authority of this present decree, therefore, we establish that the cemetery which we have blessed beside the same monastery shall always remain peaceful and free. Further, the boundaries of safety and security, marked by crosses placed around the extensive circuit of the monastery, shall be preserved wholly firm and inviolable, so that no one at all may make depredations or assaults within them, or rashly inflict grave injuries upon anyone.

We also confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See the settlement made at Tours by our predecessor Pope Urban, of holy memory, between your monastery and that of Blessed Florentius concerning the churches of Holy Cross and St. Nicholas. [Col. 1209A] In addition, by the text of this present document, we confirm forever to you and your successors everything which your monastery lawfully possesses at present in the fourteenth indiction, or may hereafter, by God’s bounty, be able justly and canonically to acquire. Among these we have thought fit to name the following: namely, in the bishopric, etc. It enumerates the possessions of that church. Then:

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your monastery, take away its possessions, retain or diminish possessions taken away, or harass it through rash vexations; rather, let all things be preserved intact, wholly beneficial for the use of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text [Col. 1209B] of our confirmation, should rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amends through fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and rank, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be separated from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment.

But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Calixtus, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

[Col. 1209C]

Given at Alba through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal deacon and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1122, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus II.

### CXXXV. He again urges Galter, bishop of Maguelonne—already admonished by letter “in the previous August”—to judge between the brethren of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem and the monks of Aniane, who were disputing over the church of the Saviour at Rubus. (1121, May 29.)

[ROZIÈRE, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre*, 73.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G[ALTER], bishop of Maguelonne, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1209D]

Concerning the church of the Saviour at Rubus, belonging to the Sepulchre of Jerusalem, we addressed our letters to your brotherhood in the previous August, commanding you, as justice required, to ensure that the Jerusalem brethren possessed it peacefully. But, as we have learned, because the name St. Mary of Rubus had through ignorance been included in those letters, the brethren were unable to obtain justice from you on that account. Therefore, by these present letters we command your brotherhood diligently to hear the case of the same brethren and the monks of Aniane, and, with the Lord’s help, determine it, so that each party may obtain its due right. For we do not wish the Church of Jerusalem to suffer any loss in its right because of an error in a name.

[Col. 1210A]

Given at the Castle of Arenarium, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June.

### CXXXVI. He confirms the rights and goods of the canons of Verona. (1121, June 14.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 772.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons THEOBALD, archpriest, and the other canons of the Church of Verona, present and future, in perpetuity.

Just as [we deny effect] to those who request unjust things, etc., and [let them] remain unimpaired. Among them we have thought fit to record by their proper names: namely, the churches of St. George, St. John the Baptist, St. Andrew, St. Clement, St. Cecilia, St. Faustinus, St. Firmus with its chapel, and St. Paul; in the borough, the churches of St. John the Baptist, St. Peter in [Col. 1210B] Carnario, and St. John in Quintiano; the castle of Bruno with its chapels and remaining appurtenances; the castles of Gratiana, Martiana, Puliano, Biunde, Porcile, and Calmasino, with their chapels and other appurtenances; the village of Quinto and the place called Villa, with their chapels.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain or diminish possessions taken away, or harass it through rash vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved entire, wholly beneficial for the use of those for whose support they were granted. We further decree that no one may impede, disturb, or claim for himself the distribution of the benefices of your canonry; rather, as it was established in former times and strengthened by the privileges of our predecessors, so, with God’s help, may it remain firm and inviolable in the future. Nor may any one of you receive from another’s hand benefices customarily distributed by the gift of the chapter; rather, the former custom concerning them shall be preserved in future times. [Col. 1210C]

By this present decree we further establish that, if suitable persons are found in your church, no one from another church shall be preferred as archpriest or archdeacon. If it happens that the archpriest or archdeacon dies at the same time, then until others are appointed, their duties concerning the distribution of benefices shall be supplied by the provost, as is also contained in the privileges of our predecessors granted to your church. If, therefore, in future, etc.

I, Calixtus, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given in the territory of Palestrina, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1122, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus II, through the hand of Chrysogonus, deacon and chancellor of the Holy Apostolic See.

### CXXXVII. To D[idacus], archbishop of Compostela.—Concerning bishops suspended because they had not attended the council, and the archbishop of Braga deprived of his legation. (1121, June 21.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 336.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother D., archbishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1211A]

We have granted dignity and honour to you and to the Church of Compostela for its good and advantage; we are aggrieved if those brethren will not obey your commands. You have indeed already administered justice against them in part; nevertheless, we urge your brotherhood diligently once more to admonish the bishops of Coimbra, Lugo, and Mondoñedo, and the others, to strive humbly to obey you. If they do not do this within forty days after your admonition, then, by the Lord’s authority, we confirm from that time the sentence pronounced by you against them, until they make satisfaction.

Concerning Braga, we reply to your charity as follows. As report has it in our parts, and as you showed in letters sent to us through P., a canon and chaplain of your church, you desire excessively to oppress the Church of Braga and to claim its dignity for yourself. Therefore we tolerate, in this respect, the disobedience of that brother, until either you yourselves, with God’s help, come into our presence, or send suitable envoys to represent you in this case. We have appointed as the deadline for this appearance the Nativity of Blessed John the Baptist in the following year. [Col. 1211B]

We commend to your affection the aforesaid envoy of yours, who [variants: *quem*, “whom,” or *quia*, “because”] we have learned has laboured faithfully for you, asking that henceforth, for love of us, you hold him especially dear.

[Col. 1211C]

Given in the territory of Tivoli, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of July.

### CXXXVIII. He writes to D[idacus], archbishop of Compostela, that the marriage of Gerald, who married a kinswoman of his former wife, must be dissolved. (1121, June 21.)

[FLOREZ, as above, p. 381.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother D., archbishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

This brother, Gerald, whom you sent to us, stated to us orally that he had long maintained a relationship with a certain woman. After some time, however, he took a wife, who was found to be related to the former woman in the third degree [Col. 1211D]. If the case is so, it has seemed good to our brethren that he ought altogether to dismiss that wife. For, since he contracted an altogether unlawful marriage, it does not appear that he could subsequently attain a lawful marriage.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, 21 June.

### CXXXIX. To Atto of Arles, Fulco of Aix, archbishops, and the other bishops throughout Provence.—That they are to excommunicate Count Ildefonsus and his associates unless they make satisfaction to the monastery of Saint-Gilles within forty days. (1121, 21 June.)

[MINARD, *History of Nîmes*, vol. I, preliminary matter, p. 30.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren and fellow bishops ATTO of Arles, FULCO of Aix, BERENGER of Narbonne, and WALTER of Maguelonne [Col. 1212A], greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the complaint of the abbot (Hugh) and brethren of Saint-Gilles: that Count Ildefonsus, with the counsel and assistance of your parishioners Raymond of Baux, Elzéar of Castries, William Rainald of Merenas, invaded by armed force the church and borough of Saint-Gilles; committed arson and homicide there; and compelled the burgesses to perjury against their fidelity to the monastery. We therefore ask and admonish your brotherhood that, on our behalf, you carefully admonish the count and the others, so that they may leave the monastery and borough free and undisturbed to the abbot and brethren; that the count demolish the castle newly built for its destruction; and that, by your judgment, he make satisfaction to the same monastery for property taken and injuries inflicted. If he does not fulfil this within forty days after receiving our letter, we pronounce against them a sentence of excommunication until they make satisfaction. In their territories we prohibit every divine office and burial, except the baptism of infants and the penances of the dying; and we also command that all places to which they go shall be entirely free of divine offices for as long as they remain in them.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, 21 June.

### CXL. To the bishops of Uzès, Toulouse, and Nîmes.—That they are to declare Count Ildefonsus excommunicated unless he restores what he took from the monastery of Saint-Gilles. (1121, 22 June.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 239.]

[Col. 1212C]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren RAYMOND, bishop of Uzès, [AMELIUS], bishop of Toulouse, and JOHN, bishop of Nîmes, greeting and apostolic blessing.

How many evils, disturbances, and injuries Count Ildefonsus has brought upon the monastery and brethren of Saint-Gilles, you know all the better because you live nearer. We have therefore taken care to admonish him by our letters to restore what he has taken, leave the monastery [Col. 1212D], together with the borough and other appurtenances, free and undisturbed to the abbot and brethren, and demolish the castle which he has built for the destruction of that village. If he takes care to accomplish this within forty days after receiving those letters, let us give thanks to God. Otherwise, from that time, with the Lord’s help, we pronounce a sentence of excommunication against his person and counsellors; and in their territories we prohibit every divine office and burial, except the baptism of infants and the penances of the dying. We also command that every place to which they come shall be wholly free of divine offices for as long as they remain in it. We therefore command your brotherhood both to announce this sentence issued by us and to ensure that it is observed throughout all your dioceses [Col. 1213A] until the count makes satisfaction.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, 22 June.

### CXLI. To Raymond of Baux, William of Sabran, Elzéar of Castries, Raino of Castlar, and William Rainoard.—He threatens to excommunicate them, as counsellors and helpers of Count Ildefonsus, unless within forty days they cease from harassing the monastery of Saint-Gilles. (1121, 22 June.)

[D. BOUQUET, *ibid.*, p. 240.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the noblemen Raymond of BAUX, William of SABRAN, Elzéar of CASTRIES, Raino of CASTLAR, and William RAINOARD, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1213B] It has been reported to us that Count Ildefonsus, at your instigation and with your assistance, invaded by armed force the church and borough of Saint-Gilles, committed arson and homicide there, and compelled the burgesses to perjury against their fidelity to the monastery. All these things, indeed, bring great peril upon your souls. Therefore, by this present writing, we command you under injunction to admonish the same count diligently, so that within forty days after receiving our letter he may leave the church and borough of Saint-Gilles wholly free and undisturbed to the abbot and brethren. But if the count and you scorn to obey this command of ours, with the Lord as author we pronounce against him and against you a sentence of excommunication, and in your territories [Col. 1213C] a sentence of interdict.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, 22 June.

### CXLII. To the burgesses of the monastery of Saint-Gilles.—He absolves them from the oath of fidelity rendered to Count Ildefonsus, who had compelled them to perjury. (1121, 22 June.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 240.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, the greater and lesser burgesses of the monastery of Saint-Gilles, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that none of you is unaware that the monastery of Saint Giles, together with all that pertains to it [Col. 1213D], belongs by right to the Roman Church and stands under the guardianship and protection of blessed Peter and the Apostolic See. Therefore whoever wrongs you and that place utterly wrongs us, and your injury is known to redound to the Apostolic See. We have learned, indeed, that Count Ildefonsus compelled you by force to an oath contrary to the firmness of faith and contrary to fidelity to the monastery. We therefore, providing with due concern both for the salvation of your souls and for the welfare of the monastery, absolve you from the obligation of that oath [Col. 1214A]. Moreover, we command you inviolably to observe the oath which you had previously made to the abbot and monastery.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, 22 June.

### CXLIII. To Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse.—He orders him, under penalty of excommunication, to repair the damages inflicted upon the monastery of Saint-Gilles. (1121, 22 June.)

[D. BOUQUET, *ibid.*, p. 239.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ILDEFONSUS, illustrious count, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Raymond,

> **Note:** [Col. 1213D] Raymond Berengar—Count, as it appears to us, of Barcelona, and likewise Count of Provence or Arles—was then waging war with Ildefonsus, likewise a lord of Provence, to determine the boundaries of each man’s dominion. Since the men of Saint-Gilles supported the Count of Barcelona in these conflicts, they provoked Ildefonsus against themselves; he had not forgotten that the valley of Flavianus—that is, the territory of Saint-Gilles—had been granted to them by his father not long before. [Col. 1214D]

our son, Hugh the abbot, and the brethren [Col. 1214B] of the monastery of Saint-Gilles, which belongs by right to blessed Peter, complain strongly against you: that you have invaded by armed force the church and borough of Saint-Gilles, committed arson and homicide there, and compelled the burgesses to perjury against their fidelity to the monastery. They also complain that, beside the boundaries established by our predecessors and confirmed by us, you have built a certain castle for the destruction of the village. We are greatly astonished and grieved by all this, since that place, together with all its appurtenances, is known to pertain solely to the Apostolic See, and since we had confidence in your good character. We therefore admonish and command your nobility that within forty days after you receive this letter you leave the church and borough of Saint-Gilles [Col. 1214C] wholly undisturbed to its abbot and brethren, demolish that castle, and make satisfaction for the property taken and the sacrilege committed, according to the judgment of our brethren and fellow bishops Atto of Arles, Berenger of Narbonne, and Walter of Maguelonne. If you prove contemptuous, we shall by no means tolerate injury to a monastery of the Roman Church. From that time we pronounce against your person and against those by whose counsel these evils were done a sentence of excommunication; and by the authority of the Holy Spirit we prohibit divine offices and burial throughout all your territory, except the baptism of infants and the penances of the dying.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, 22 June.

### CXLIV. He commands Pelagius, Archbishop of Braga, “to restore the honour of Saint James in Portugal, which his predecessor [Maurice], Archbishop of Braga, had held in *praestimonium* from the Archbishop of Compostela and which he himself violently retains.” 1121.

[See the *History of Compostela* in FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 340.]

[Col. 1214D]

### CXLV. He rebukes *[Alpherada]*, abbess of the nunnery of Saint Mary at Capua, because, “after the second appointed terms had passed,” she did not appear for judgment. He threatens, unless she comes or sends envoys, to restore the church of Cingla to the monastery of Monte Cassino. (1121.)

[See PETER’s *Chronicle of the Monastery of Monte Cassino*, I, IV, ch. 70.]

[Col. 1215A]

### CXLVI. To D[idacus], Archbishop of Compostela.—He commends Guy, a knight journeying to Saint James. (1121, 5 July.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 339.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother D., Archbishop of Compostela [Col. 1215B], greeting and apostolic blessing.

This knight Guy, our faithful man, has undertaken a vow to visit the church of the most blessed apostle James. We therefore ask your affection to hold him commended to you for our sake as long as he remains there. If you wish to convey anything to us, you may faithfully entrust it to him.

Given at Lateran, 5 July.

### CXLVII. Concerning the confirmation of the Regular Canons of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem and their possessions. (1121, 6 July.)

[ROZIÈRE, *Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre*, p. 15.]

[Col. 1215C] CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, GERARD, prior, and his brethren professing the regular life in the church of the Holy Sepulchre, present and future alike, for ever.

We have the Lord’s command: “Enter through the narrow gate,” for narrow is the way that leads to life. Since therefore you, most beloved sons in Christ, inspired by divine grace, have resolved to restrain your conduct under the discipline of the regular life and, that you may be able to enter through the narrow gate, to serve Almighty God in common according to the institution of the holy Fathers, we rejoice in your vows with fatherly affection. Hence, granting your petition our due favour, we establish your purpose of religious life by the authority of this present privilege [Col. 1215D]. We decree that no person whatsoever may alter in your church the order of canonical life which you have professed; rather, by God’s authority, it shall remain firm and inviolable in future times.

Moreover, by the permanence of this present decree, we ordain that you and your successors who remain in the same religious life shall possess in perpetuity all things which you are at present seen to hold for the support of your common sustenance, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means: namely, half of all offerings made at the Lord’s Sepulchre; likewise, the offerings of the Cross; the tithes of the city of Jerusalem and adjacent places, except the tithes of the *funda*; and half [Col. 1216A] of the benefice granted by the king in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem, as all these are set out in the charter of grant and confirmation of Patriarch Arnulf, of good memory; likewise, by grant of that same patriarch, the church of Saint Peter at Joppa, with the full integrity of its honour and dignity, and the church of Saint Lazarus with its appurtenances. In addition, whatever you may hereafter, by God’s bounty, acquire justly and canonically, shall remain undisturbed and whole to you and your successors.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations; rather, all shall be preserved intact for the use and complete benefit of those for whose support and governance they were granted [Col. 1216B]. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this charter of our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make fitting amends, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let that person know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the wrongdoing committed; let that person be separated from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to strict vengeance. But may all who preserve justice for that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 1216C] Written by the hand of Gervasius, regional scriniary and notary of the sacred palace.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Grisogonus, cardinal deacon and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on 6 July, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1122, and in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Calixtus II.

Given at the Lateran, 14 April.

### CXLVIII. To the Archbishop of Caesarea and the other bishops, abbots, etc., established throughout the province of Jerusalem, to King B[aldwin], etc.—He announces that he has sent the pallium to Patriarch Guarmund. (1121, 6 July.)

[ROZIÈRE, *ibid.*, p. 14.]

[Col. 1216D] CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brethren and sons in Christ: the Archbishop of Caesarea and the other bishops, abbots, and priors established throughout the province of Jerusalem; and also to our illustrious and most beloved son and kinsman, King B[ALDWIN], to the princes, barons, clergy, and people of Jerusalem, [greeting] and apostolic blessing.

After the death of our venerable brother Ar[nulf], patriarch of good memory, we have learned, both from letters sent by you and from the reliable account of our wise and religious envoys, and have rejoiced, that you unanimously agreed in the election of our fellow brother Guar[mund]. We have therefore willingly assented to your request; and, although this appeared contrary to the custom of the Roman Church, and although we had entrusted execution of this matter to our legate, our venerable brother P[eter], Bishop of Porto, nevertheless, out of reverence for the Lord’s Sepulchre and love for you, we did not delay sending the pallium through those envoys [Col. 1217A]. In it we grant that aforesaid brother of ours the fullness of the pontifical or patriarchal office, confirming by apostolic authority the integrity of his dignity and power, and that of the Church of Jerusalem entrusted to him, so that henceforth he may have authority, with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, to hold councils and episcopal consecrations.

Addressing these present letters to you, we ask and, in asking, admonish all of you to remain firm and steadfast in the unity and obedience of your mother, the Roman Church. For she, by God’s grace, liberated your Church with the blood of many of her sons, and she labours daily on your behalf in regions beyond and on this side of the mountains. Take care, moreover, to love, honour, and revere with due humility and obedience the aforesaid brother of ours, your patriarch [Col. 1217B], so that by his care and concern the mercy of Almighty God may work salvation in you; and so that you may deserve to rejoice in him, and he in you to receive a crown at the judgment of the eternal Judge. May our Lord Jesus Christ, who in our days deigned to glorify the place of his feet, keep you under his protection through the prayers of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant you victory over his enemies [Col. 1217C], loose you from the bonds of sins, and lead you to life and everlasting glory.

Given at the Lateran, 6 July.

### CXLIX. To Guarmund, Patriarch of Jerusalem. (1121, 6 July.)

[ROZIÈRE, *ibid.*, p. 72.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GUAR[MUND], Patriarch of Jerusalem, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have heard that a certain dissension has arisen in the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre: on its account the cantor and subcantor, living in their own houses almost as secular persons, preside over the choir of the regular brethren and at their own pleasure direct, through whatever person they wish, the celebration of divine offices [Col. 1217D]. Your prudence can easily perceive how unseemly, absurd, and contrary to the propriety and peace of the regular brethren this is. We therefore charge your diligence carefully to admonish them either to dwell with the brethren in the cloister and honourably discharge their ministries in person, as is fitting, or to free the religious brethren from the burden of this office. Otherwise, we shall not be able to endure this impropriety any longer without expelling it altogether from that venerable house of God. For it may sufficiently satisfy the cantor and subcantor, if, while they remain in secular life, the benefice of the cantorship is left to them and the religious brethren freely arrange, among themselves, in the due unanimity of charity, for the celebration of divine offices [Col. 1218A].

Given at the Lateran, 6 July.

### CL. To Mark, a Venetian cleric.—He writes that he has learned from the letters of P[eter], Bishop of Porto, his legate, that Mark offered his possessions to blessed Peter “under an annual rent of one Byzantine.” He praises Mark’s piety and sends him the first stone for laying the foundations of a church. (1121, 24 July.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 1238.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son MARK, cleric, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1218B] Our most distinguished and venerable brother and legate, P., Bishop of Porto, has informed us by letter that through his hands you have offered your possessions to blessed Peter and his Roman Church, under an annual payment of one Byzantine. You desire to build there a church in which regular canons may live under the right and lordship of blessed Peter. We therefore approve your devotion and desire, receive that offering, and pray Almighty God for you, that he may enable you to complete, to his honour and to your salvation, the good work you have begun. Accordingly, we send the stone which you are to place in the foundation of that church, granting you in it our consent and favour.

> **Note:** [Col. 1217D] Elsewhere we read of the custom of Roman pontiffs of sending the first stone for the construction of new churches, especially when those churches were placed under the protection of blessed Peter and the Roman See. [Col. 1218D]

Given at Aversa, 25 July.

### CLI. To Berenger, Archbishop of Narbonne, and his suffragans.—They are to admonish Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse to permit the Abbot of Saint-Gilles, whom he had expelled, to return to the monastery; otherwise, they are to punish him by excommunication and interdict. (1121, 4 October.)

[BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 236.]

[Col. 1218C]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren BERENGER, Archbishop of Narbonne, and his suffragans, JOHN, Bishop of Nîmes, and WALTER, Bishop of Maguelonne, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that Count Ildefonsus seized our son Hugh, Abbot of Saint-Gilles, from the monastery [Col. 1218D], had him violently taken to the castle of Belcayra, and forced him, by extortion of an oath, to go to Cluny, on the condition that the abbot should not thereafter return to the monastery of Saint Giles except with the count’s permission. Your prudence can easily perceive how grave this is; and indeed, if so great a crime is left unpunished, still more serious dangers may arise in future even among persons of higher rank. We therefore command your brotherhood to admonish the same count to absolve the abbot altogether from that oath, permit him to return to the monastery without molestation, and leave the aforesaid monastery of Saint-Gilles, which belongs by right to the Roman Church, wholly free and undisturbed together with [Col. 1219A] all its possessions. If the count maintains a claim against the abbot or the place itself, we shall willingly render him justice at the proper time. But if he proves contemptuous, act in our stead: separate him from the thresholds of the churches, and prohibit every divine office throughout his territory, in cities and castles, except the baptism of infants and the penances of the dying.

Given at Melfi, 4 October.

### CLII. He commands B[oso], legate of the Apostolic See, to exhort Queen Urraca, daughter of King Ildefonsus, to release Archbishop Didacus of Compostela from imprisonment and restore the castles taken from him; and he orders that, unless she obeys within forty days, she be excommunicated and all her land subjected to interdict after the bishops have been summoned. (1121, 7 October.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 341.]

[Col. 1219B]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable and beloved son in Christ B., cardinal priest and legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We remember having often written to you that it is the wish of our brethren that you return to them as quickly as possible. Yet, because urgent affairs constrain us, we still impose upon you certain duties appropriate to the present time, through which you must remain longer. We have been informed that Queen Urraca, daughter of King Ildefonsus of noble memory, seized by some deceit and treachery our most beloved brother Didacus, Archbishop of the Church of Compostela [Col. 1219C] and likewise our legate in certain provinces; compelled him to place the castles and honours of the Church in her power; and nevertheless did not release him from captivity. Such a crime is in no way to be tolerated by the Church of God. For you know what the Lord said concerning priests: “Whoever despises you despises me”; and, “Whoever touches you touches the apple of my eye.” We therefore command your affection by this present letter to admonish the same queen without delay to set our aforesaid brother entirely free, restore in their full integrity the castles and honours of the Church, and make satisfaction to God and his Church for so great an outrage. If she does not do this within forty days after your admonition [Col. 1219D], let your diligence, having summoned the other brethren and bishops, pronounce a sentence of excommunication against her and her supporters, and prohibit throughout all her territory every divine office except the baptism of infants and the penance of the dying, until what has been done so wickedly is fully corrected by the judgment of the Church.

Given at Melfi, 7 October.

### CLIII. To the Archbishop of Toledo concerning the same matter. (1121, 7 October.)

[FLOREZ, *ibid.*, p. 342.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother B[ERNARD], Archbishop of Toledo [Col. 1220A], legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have heard, and have been deeply grieved, that Queen Urraca, daughter of King Ildefonsus of distinguished memory, has stretched forth her hands to a new and most wicked crime. For we have been informed that she seized by some deceit and treachery our most beloved brother Didacus, Archbishop of the Church of Compostela and likewise our legate in certain provinces; compelled him to place the castles and honours of the Church in her power; and nevertheless did not release him from imprisonment. Such a crime is in no way to be tolerated by the Church of God. For you know what the Lord said concerning priests: “Whoever despises you despises me,” and “Whoever touches you touches the apple [Col. 1220B] of my eye.” Therefore, by this present letter we command your brotherhood to admonish the same queen without delay to set our aforesaid brother wholly free, restore the castles and honours of the Church in their full integrity, and make satisfaction to God and his Church for so great an outrage. If she does not do this within forty days after your admonition, let your brotherhood, having summoned the other brethren and fellow bishops, pronounce a sentence of excommunication against her and her supporters, and prohibit throughout all her territory every divine office except the baptism of infants and the penances of the dying, until what has been done so wickedly is fully corrected by the judgment of the Church.

Given at Melfi, 7 October.

### CLIV. He informs the archbishops and bishops of Spain of the foregoing letters to Cardinal Boso and Bernard, Archbishop of Toledo. (1121, 7 October.)

[FLOREZ, *ibid.*, p. 343.]

[Col. 1220C]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren, archbishops and bishops throughout Spain, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever new evils, intolerable to Catholic men, arise through the wickedness of any person, they must be rooted out with a swift hand, lest—God forbid!—they gain strength hereafter. We must be especially vigilant in such matters, because, although unworthy, we hold in the Church the place of God and of his Christ [Col. 1220D]. For we have been informed that Queen Urraca seized by some deceit and treachery our most beloved brother Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela and likewise our legate in certain provinces; compelled him to hand over the castles and honours of the Church into her power; and nevertheless did not release him from captivity. Such a crime is in no way to be tolerated by the Church of God. We therefore command you by these present letters: whenever you are summoned either by our brother Bernard, Archbishop of Toledo, or by our son Boso, cardinal priest, to whom we have committed this case, take care to meet together without delay and, acting upon their counsel, pronounce a sentence of excommunication against that queen and her supporters [Col. 1221A], and prohibit throughout all her territory every divine office except the baptism of infants and the penances of the dying, until she entirely releases our aforesaid brother, restores the castles and honours of the Church, and makes satisfaction to God and his Church for so great an outrage.

Given at Melfi, 7 October.

### CLV. To the queen concerning the same matter. (1121, 7 October.)

[FLOREZ, *ibid.*, p. 344.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the illustrious Queen URRACA, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Unless you take care, with the greatest haste, to correct your most grave presumption [Col. 1221B], you must greatly fear that you will be most severely struck by God’s judgment. For you are said to have stretched forth your hands against the vicar of God and of his Christ, our venerable brother Didacus, Archbishop of the Church of Compostela and our legate in certain provinces, to whom you had also promised friendship and security. For it is written through the prophet concerning priests: “Do not touch my anointed ones, and do no evil to my prophets.” And again the Lord himself says: “Whoever touches you touches the apple of my eye.” From our own experience we can judge how greatly this wickedness must displease Almighty God, since we cannot endure even any injury to the pupils of our eyes without grave [Col. 1221C] distress. Therefore, lest you be struck by that dreadful sentence of divine judgment, we command you by the authority of this present letter, without delay, entirely to release our aforesaid brother, restore the castles of the Church with the honours which you have taken away, and humbly make satisfaction to God and his Church for so great a crime. Otherwise, know certainly that he who has made his priest the pupil of his eye will take severe vengeance upon you; and we ourselves, and through our brethren—with his help—will do such justice concerning your person, those who committed these acts, and your whole territory that others hereafter will not presume to do such things by your example.

Given at Melfi, 7 October.

### CLVI. To King Ildefonsus concerning the same matter. (1121, 7 October.)

[FLOREZ, *ibid.*, p. 345.]

[Col. 1221D]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved nephew IL., vigorous and glorious king of the Spains, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We give thanks to Almighty God and our Lord Jesus Christ, who, while we suffered from a most grave illness, according to the multitude of his mercies restored us to our former health. We also give him thanks because, within and outside the City, and throughout all Italy, the faithful of the Church are so united to us that all humbly obey our will. Yet there is one matter over which we are most deeply grieved [Col. 1222A]: as we have heard, your mother Queen Urraca, fearing neither God nor showing reverence to his most blessed apostle James, in your presence presumptuously stretched forth sacrilegious hands against the vicar of God and of his Christ, our venerable brother Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela and likewise our legate in certain provinces. Your nobility ought not now to forget how lovingly that same brother of ours embraced you and with what affection he once raised you. You should also know that the Lord says in the Gospel: “I love those who love me, and I will honour those who honour me.” Therefore, if that aforesaid brother loved your person from childhood, raised it as far as he could, and suffered many grave things through you, you, most beloved son [Col. 1222B], should love and honour him, and, through yourself and your faithful men, take every care that he be entirely released from captivity. Thus, by this example, other persons may love you more, trust more strongly in your goodness, and more willingly wear themselves out in your service.

Moreover, we ask your affection frequently to make known to us by letter and messenger your condition and welfare; for, even if we cannot sufficiently assist you, we nevertheless rejoice in your success. We love you with true affection as a most beloved and special son of the Church and as our own flesh, and we shall most willingly give you our counsel and aid. May Almighty God, through the prayers of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul and also James, preserve your person and kingdom for his honour [Col. 1222C] and your salvation, and bring you to everlasting life.

Given at Melfi, 7 October.

Cause the other letter which we are sending to your mother to be presented to her by your messenger.

### CLVII. To Bernard, Primate of Toledo.—The rights of the primacy of Toledo. (1121, 3 November.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 215.]

CALIXTUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BERNARD, Primate of Toledo, and to his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

After the condescension of heavenly mercy had freed the illustrious city of Toledo—once renowned among the cities of Spain—by the zeal and labor of King Alfonso of glorious memory from the tyranny of the Saracens, our predecessors of holy memory, Urban and Paschal, pontiffs of the Roman Church, endeavored to restore the church of that city to its former dignity. Therefore, most reverend brother and fellow bishop Bernard, conferring upon you the pallium, that is, the fullness of the pontifical office, they established you by the enactments of their privileges as primate throughout all the kingdoms of Spain, just as your predecessors, the bishops of the aforesaid city, are known to have been in ancient times.

Following in the footsteps of these our Fathers, we have judged it proper to grant the requests both of you and of our most reverend nephew, King Alfonso; so that, with the Lord as author, we may confirm to you and your successors this same honor, and through you to the Church of Toledo. By apostolic authority, therefore, we decree that you shall hold the dignity of primacy throughout all the kingdoms of Spain. Yet, retaining your person in our hand with a more special favor, we determine that, should any case arise concerning you, it shall be decided by the judgment of the Roman pontiff alone. Thus all the bishops of Spain shall regard you as primate; and, if anything worthy of inquiry arises among them, they shall refer it to you—while in all things the authority of the Roman Church remains unimpaired, as do the privileges of each individual metropolitan.

Moreover, by the stability of this present privilege we fortify the Church of Toledo, confirming to it the territory of Complutum with its boundaries, and likewise all the churches and dioceses which it is known to have possessed of old by its own right. Furthermore, we decree that the episcopal sees of Oviedo, León, and Palencia shall be subject to the same Church of Toledo as to their metropolitan. But the remaining sees which in ancient times were subject to it, when Almighty God in the condescension of His mercy restores them to Christian power, we establish by the authority of this decree to be referred back to their own head.

Further, we subject to your jurisdiction, under this condition, the dioceses of those cities which, when the Saracens invaded, lost their own metropolitans: so long as they lack their own metropolitans, they must be subject to you as to their proper metropolitan, without prejudice to the tenor of the privilege which has been granted by us to the bishop of the Church of Compostela. But if any metropolitan sees are restored to their own former state, each diocese shall be restored to its own metropolitan, so that under the governance of its proper shepherd it may rejoice in the bestowal of the divine benefit. If, therefore, in future ages any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, etc.

Given at Mantua, through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal-deacon and librarian of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of November, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1122 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus II.

## CLVIII. To the same person.—On the same subject. (1121, November 3.)

[MANSI, *ibid.*, 216.]

[Col. 1223D]

On account of your goodness and the ancient nobility of the Church of Toledo, our lord predecessor, Pope Paschal of holy memory, bestowed spiritual honor upon both your person and the same church entrusted to you. Accordingly, he appointed you his vicar in the regions of Spain and honorably entrusted to you the legation of the apostolic see. We also, showing kindness and favor toward you, embrace you with equal affection and honor you with distinction, granting you, with the Lord’s cooperation, the whole of that same legation, excepting, however, the metropolitan sees of Braga and Mérida.

Following the example of that same our father, [Col. 1224A] we also grant and confirm to you all the churches, with their possessions and revenues, which that same lord and our father is known to have granted: saving nevertheless in all things the right and lordship of the Roman Church, and likewise the tribute to be paid to it each year. For henceforward it is yours, Brother Bernard, to love the aforesaid mother, the Roman Church, in such a manner, and to venerate her—even though situated in more distant regions—in such a manner, that you may always be deemed more worthy of her favor and magnificence.

Given at Mantua, on the third day before the Nones of November.

## CLIX. To the Bishops of Oviedo and León.—That they be subject to the Primate of Toledo. (1121, November 3.)

[MANSI, *ibid.*, 216.]

[Col. 1224B]

Our predecessor, Pope Urban of holy memory, recognizing the ancient nobility of the Church of Toledo and sympathizing with its poverty, granted the churches of Oviedo and León to the archbishop of Toledo and confirmed this by the authority of his writing. Following his example, we decree, with the Lord’s assistance, to provide for the aforesaid Church. We therefore admonish and command your brotherhood that you render reverence and obedience to the archbishop and primate of Toledo as to your own metropolitan.

Given at Mantua, on the third day before the Nones of November.

## CLX. To the bishops, abbots, and others in Spain.—That they obey Bernard, Primate of Toledo, as apostolic legate. (1121, November 3.)

[MANSI, *ibid.*]

[Col. 1224C]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the archbishops, bishops, abbots, provosts, and all others, clergy as well as laity, established throughout Spain: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that it has escaped your notice that our lords predecessors, Urban and Paschal of holy memory, pontiffs of the Roman Church, loved with special affection our venerable brother Bernard, Primate of Toledo, [Col. 1224D] and honored him as a special son. For, entrusting to him their authority in your regions, they appointed him legate of the apostolic see. We too, therefore, showing him the same affection and favor, have judged it proper to entrust to him our authority and likewise our legation.

We therefore ask, admonish, and command all of you to take care humbly to obey him as our legate, and, whenever the cause of ecclesiastical advantage requires it, to hold synodal assemblies with him at his summons, correcting with God’s aid what needs correction and, with common assistance, confirming what needs confirmation.

Given at Mantua, on the third day before the Nones of November.

## CLXI. At the request of Louis, King of the Franks, he confirms the union of the bishoprics of Noyon and Tournai. (1121, December 9.)

[MARLOT, *Metropolis Remensis*, II, 277.]

[Col. 1225A]

Calixtus, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, LOUIS, most illustrious and most glorious King of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Your fathers, the kings of the Franks of glorious memory, after they had received through the mercy of Almighty God the first principles of the Christian faith, cherished the Roman Church with special devotion. Nor did they think it enough to venerate their mother only in their own times; they also bequeathed to their descendants, by a kind of hereditary right, reverence, obedience, and affection toward her. Hence, through the grace of divine inspiration, it has come about that you too, descended from the same royal line and succeeding to the government of this kingdom, have likewise succeeded in excellence of character and remained a noble heir in devotion to your aforesaid mother.

We have experienced this in our own days, and nearly the whole Roman Church recognizes it. For this reason, dearest son, we have determined graciously to admit your petitions and, with God as author, to honor your person and kingdom in a special manner. You request that we confirm by the strength of our authority the ancient union of the dioceses of Noyon and Tournai. Indeed, great and extensive tracts of land lie between the two Churches, and each of them, as they assert, could have its own bishop; but since the abundance of your affection compels us, we readily grant this request.

We therefore confirm, by the page of this present decree, the union of the Churches and dioceses of Noyon and Tournai, preserved unbroken by our predecessors until these times; and we decree that it shall remain valid forever. By apostolic authority we establish that one bishop only shall preside over both Churches; nevertheless, in times to come Noyon shall be regarded as the head and seat of episcopal dignity. In all these matters we desire our brother Lambert, the bishop, to be more diligent, and through God’s grace so to provide for each Church that neither is deprived of the benefit of pastoral office and teaching.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our enactment, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not amend by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let such a person know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most holy Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to strict punishment. But may all who observe it have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 1226A] I, Calixtus, bishop of the catholic Church, approving, have signed.

Given at Neufchâteau, through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal-deacon and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of December, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1122 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus II.

## CLXII. At the request of Bishop Geoffrey, he confirms the privileges of the Church of Mileto. (1121, December 23.)

[CAPIALBI, *Memorie per servire alla storia della Chiesa Miletese*. Naples, 1835, 8vo, p. 145.]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable Father [read: Brother] GEOFFREY, bishop of Mileto, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 1226B]

The authority of our office exhorts us to be solicitous for the condition of churches and to establish what has been rightly ordered. Therefore, dearest brother in Christ, Bishop Geoffrey, granting your requests and confirming the enactments of our predecessors of holy memory, Gregory VII and Urban II, pontiffs of the Roman Church, we establish by the stability of this present privilege that the Church of Mileto shall remain specially under the jurisdiction of the apostolic see, and that all your successors, just as you and your predecessors, shall be consecrated by the hand of the Roman pontiff.

By apostolic authority we also confirm that the Church of Vibo, transferred to Mileto, shall remain forever as decreed in the privileges of our aforesaid predecessors. We further add that the Church of Tauriana, which has been desolated because of the sins of its inhabitants, shall pass into the diocese of Mileto and henceforth remain subject to the bishop of Mileto; thus the Church of both Vibo and Tauriana shall be regarded as one diocese and shall henceforth be called by the name of Mileto.

No person, therefore, may rashly disturb this same Church of Mileto, take away its possessions, retain what has been offered to it, diminish it, or harass it with presumptuous vexations. Rather, all things which it now possesses, or may in future acquire through the Lord’s bounty—whether by grants of pontiffs, the liberality of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means—shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors; especially those things which have rightly been deemed to belong, whether in possession or governance, to the Churches of Vibo and Tauriana.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not amend by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let such a person know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who observe the just commands of the Church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find [Col. 1227A] before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Calixtus, bishop of the catholic Church. **THE LORD IS THE SUPPORT OF THOSE WHO FEAR HIM.**

Given at the Lateran [Note: [Col. 1227D] Perhaps it should be read “at Benevento.” CAPIALBI.—Undoubtedly it should be read “at Catanzaro.” JAFFÉ, *Regesta R. P.*, p. 539.], through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal-deacon and librarian of the catholic Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of January, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1122 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of Lord Calixtus II’s pontificate [Note: [Col. 1227D] Two serious difficulties have been raised against the authenticity of this bull, since the other objection—the discrepancy of the date with the indiction and the year of the pontificate—disappears as soon as they are recorded as Ughelli transcribed them from the original. The first concerns the title “Father” which the pontiff gives Geoffrey in it. This, however, should not occasion surprise when one considers that such titles were often written with initials, which could easily have been confused by the copyist. The second seems to me more weighty. We know from Falco, Romuald, and other bulls published in the great collection of the Councils [Col. 1228D] that Pope Calixtus III spent the period from September 1121 almost until all of February 1122 in our provinces. Indeed, Falco states that on 23 February 1122 the complaints of Agnes, abbess of the monastery of St Peter, against Bethlehem, abbess of the monastery of St Mary, were presented to the pontiff in the palace at Benevento, and he continues:

> Then the Apostolic Lord, because he was seriously ill and could not hold court in his presence, commanded Dionysius, bishop of Tusculum, Chrysogonus the chancellor, Robert of Paris, and the other cardinals to act as judges in this matter.

The date of our bull should therefore rather read “at Benevento”; otherwise it must be judged spurious, unless it was misread.].

## CLXIII. To all the faithful. (1121, December 28.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IX, 367.]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all [Col. 1227B] faithful of the Church: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Let it be known to all faithful and orthodox members of holy mother Church who at any time see, read, or hear this present writing that we, in person, in the fourth year of our episcopate, in the year 1122 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the fifteenth indiction, came into the regions of Calabria for the restoration of peace between William, duke of Italy, and Roger, count of Sicily; that we remained at Neocastro for fifteen days on the aforesaid business; that we returned thence through Catanzaro; and that there, by God’s grace, with several of our bishops and cardinals, whose names are subscribed below, we personally dedicated a church in honor of holy Mary, Mother of the Lord, and of the chief apostles Peter and Paul.

We granted and confirmed to that church the headship and episcopal dignity of the whole district and dependency of Three Taverns. For that church, by the power and authority of God and of blessed Mary His Mother, and of the chief apostles Peter and Paul, with the assent and confirmation of the bishops and cardinals who were there with us, we bestowed and granted this gift of mercy and remission: that all whose bodies are buried by their own wish in the cemetery of the same church, unless they die under excommunication and without confession, shall at that very hour be absolved of all their sins, be delivered from the torments of hell and everlasting Gehenna, and be recognized as participants in the first resurrection.

[Col. 1228A] We further added, by God’s will and with the consent of the bishops and cardinals, and by the authority of apostolic dignity and ecclesiastical power, that all who should devoutly come to the annual festival of the dedication of the aforesaid church—which we have decreed shall be celebrated for eight days, namely from the feast of the Innocents until their octave—shall, if they have confessed or confess within the octave, obtain by the aforesaid authority remission of one year for mortal sins and one third for venial sins.

And all who have bestowed or shall bestow their alms upon the same church, who shall defend it, increase it, and not diminish it, we bless on behalf of God and by the authority of holy Mary, Mother of God, and of the chief apostles Peter and Paul; and we receive them into our prayers.

[Col. 1228B]

I, Calixtus, bishop of the catholic Church.

I, Lambert, bishop of Ostia.

I, Giles, bishop of Tusculum.

I, Crescentius, bishop of Sabina.

I, Peter, bishop of Porto.

I, Vitalis, bishop of Albano.

I, Archbishop of Bari.

I, Rodulf, archbishop of Reggio.

I, Gregory, archbishop of Santa Severina.

I, Fulco, archbishop of Acerenza.

I, Geoffrey, bishop of Messina.

I, Vellard, bishop of Agrigento.

I, Rainald, bishop of Mileto.

I, Angerius, bishop of Catanzaro.

I, Henry, bishop of Neocastro.

[Col. 1228C]

I, Peter, bishop of Squillace.

I, Radulf, bishop of Martirano.

I, Peter, bishop of Malvito.

I, John, bishop of Anglona.

I, Gerard, bishop of Potenza.

I, John, bishop of Catanzaro.

I, William, bishop of [Albertina?].

I, Policronius, bishop of Nicastro.

I, Gervasius, bishop of Umbriatico.

I, Gerontius, bishop of Gerace.

I, Nicholas, abbot of the Church of St Angelo at Mileto.

I, Hubert, abbot of St Euphemia.

I, Lambert, master of [Hierimit?].

I, Roger, abbot of St Julian.

[Col. 1228D]

I, Boniface, cardinal-priest of the title of St Mark.

I, Benedict, cardinal-priest of St Peter in Chains, of the title of Eudoxia.

[Col. 1229A]

I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of St Cecilia.

I, Divizzo, cardinal-priest of Saints Sylvester and Martin, of the title of Equitius.

I, Theobald, cardinal-priest of the title of Pammachius.

I, Crescentius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Marcellinus and Peter.

I, Desiderius, cardinal-priest of the title of St Praxedes.

I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of St Prisca.

I, Deusdedit, cardinal-priest of the title of St Lawrence in Damaso.

I, Gregory, cardinal-priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina.

I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of St Chrysogonus.

[Col. 1229B]

I, Amicus, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem.

I, Sigizzo, cardinal-priest of the title of St Sixtus.

I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of St Marcellus.

I, Robert, cardinal-priest of the title of St Sabina.

I, Romuald, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Via Lata.

I, Aldo, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian.

I, Romanus, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Portico.

I, Jonathan, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

I, Henry, cardinal-deacon of St Theodore.

[Col. 1229C]

Given at Catanzaro, through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal-deacon and librarian of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of January, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1122 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus II.

## CLXIV. To Alexander, King of Scotland.—That he and the bishops obey the Archbishop of York, their metropolitan. (1122, January 15.)

[WILKINS, *Concil. Brit.*, I, 481.]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to ALEXANDER, illustrious and glorious King of the Scots: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Concerning the presumption of the bishops who are in your kingdom and the case of our venerable brother Thurstan, [Col. 1229D] Archbishop of York, we have already sent you letters, but have not been heard. Therefore, admonishing your nobility in the Lord by the present letter of visitation, we command that you by no means permit the bishops of your kingdom to consecrate one another without their metropolitan’s permission. Whenever the needs of the churches require it, those elected shall reverently approach their metropolitan, namely the Archbishop of York, and receive consecration either by his hand or, if necessity arises, by his permission. By apostolic authority we command both them and yourself humbly to obey that archbishop as father and teacher.

Given at Taranto, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of February.

## CLXV. To J[ohn], Bishop of Glasgow. (1122, January 15.)

[*Monastic. Anglic.*, III, 147.]

[Col. 1230A]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother JOHN, bishop of Glasgow: greeting and apostolic blessing.

You were consecrated bishop at the request of the Church of York by our lord predecessor, Pope Paschal of holy memory. Although you ought certainly to have acknowledged that favor humbly, you have, as we are informed, been raised to such pride that you have refused to make profession even at our command to your metropolitan, the Archbishop of York. You should know for certain that we cannot endure longer the obstinacy of this contempt. Therefore, reiterating our command, we command you to acknowledge as your mother the Church of York, [Col. 1230B] in whose chapter you were elected as its suffragan, and not to behave as an ungrateful son; and to make profession to our venerable brother Thomas, your metropolitan. Otherwise, whatever sentence he pronounces against you according to canonical equity, we shall, with God as author, hold valid.

Given at Taranto, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of February.

## CLXVI. To the Bishops of Scotland.—That they obey their metropolitan, the Archbishop of York. (1122, January 15.)

[WILKINS, *Concil. Brit. Magnae*, vol. I, p. 481.]

[Col. 1230C]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brothers in Christ, all bishops throughout Scotland, suffragans of the Church of York: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We remember that in letters some time ago we admonished all of you to render reverence and obedience to our venerable brother Thurstan, Archbishop of York. Yet, as has been reported to us, you have until now neglected to do so. We therefore command you, by a reiterated injunction of the apostolic see, to lay aside every excuse and pretense, henceforth acknowledge the aforesaid brother as Archbishop of the Church of York and your metropolitan, and render him reverence and obedience.

Moreover, those elected to churches shall approach him as their metropolitan in order to receive consecration, and none of them shall presume to consecrate another without his permission. Such consecration will indeed be invalid, and we shall not be able to refrain from administering canonical justice in the matter, with the Lord’s help.

Given at Taranto, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of February.

## CLXVII. Privilege for the Abbey of St German of the Meadows. (1122, January 28.)

[BOUILLARD, *Hist. de Saint-Germain des Prés*, proofs, p. XXXV.]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HUGH, abbot of the monastery of St German of [Col. 1231A] the Meadows, situated near the city of Paris, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A pious request should be fulfilled with a corresponding result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the benefit sought may assuredly acquire force. Since, therefore, your belovedness has fled to the haven of the apostolic see and requested its protection with due devotion, we graciously grant your petition and receive the monastery of St German, over which you preside with God as author, together with all things belonging to it, under the guardianship and protection of blessed Peter.

Accordingly, by the page of this present privilege, we confirm in perpetuity to you and your successors every honor, every dignity, [Col. 1231B] and every liberty which has been conferred upon your monastery by authentic privileges of the apostolic see or by royal charters. We further establish that whatever goods or possessions belong to your church through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, and whatever you may in future acquire lawfully and canonically by God’s bounty, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors.

Among these, we have judged the following to be noted by their proper names: in the district of Poitou, the church of St German of Nentriac; in the district of Bourges, the church of Catherigiac, together with the other churches which your monastery possesses, etc.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain what has been offered to it, diminish it, or harass it with presumptuous vexations. Rather, everything shall be preserved intact and serve in every way the benefit of those for whose support and governance it was granted. Furthermore, by a decree to remain forever, we establish that in your grievances you may freely appeal to the apostolic see.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt to act against it and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not amend by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let such a person know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him or her be cut off from the most sacred Body and [Col. 1231D] Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let that person be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who observe what is just toward the same place [Col. 1232A] may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Calixtus, bishop of the catholic Church.

Given at Botenti, through the hand of Chrysogonus, cardinal-deacon and librarian of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of February, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1122 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Calixtus II.

## CLXVIII. To Emperor Henry V. (1122, February 19.)

[NEUGART, *Cod. diplom. Alem.* from manuscript codex 55 of the Library of St John at Schaffhausen.]

[Col. 1232B]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his kinsman, King H. [Note: [Col. 1231D] Henry V is indicated.]

We grieve greatly because we do not dare to visit you with the address of apostolic greeting, according to our heart’s desire. Nevertheless, we have judged it proper to send to your presence this letter and our venerable brother A., [Note: [Col. 1231D] At this time this was Azzo, bishop of Acqui in the marquisate of Montferrat, most devoted to Henry V’s party, as appears from his letter to the same emperor (*Eccard, Corp. hist. med. aevi*, vol. II, p. 266). Thus Calixtus II could employ his efforts with no slight hope of a successful outcome, especially because of the bond of kinship by which Azzo was bound to both men, and perhaps also because, before this pope’s pontificate, he had been drawn over to Caesar’s party.] bishop of Acqui, who is kinsman both to us and to you and loves us jointly with sincere affection, in order that you may more fully recognize our will and, by God’s grace, recover from excessive hardness.

For both you are far more indebted to us, and we to you, than our predecessors were to one another. Besides the common duty of fatherhood by which we are bound through the administration of the apostolic see, and besides that dignity of the empire which German kings obtain through the ministry of the Roman pontiff alone, the close kinship of the flesh [Col. 1232C] [Note: [Col. 1231D] The origin of the kinship must be sought in Empress Agnes, grandmother of Henry V. She was the daughter of William III, surnamed the Great, duke of Poitou and Aquitaine, by Agnes, daughter of Otto-William, count of Burgundy, and sister of Renaud I, count of Burgundy, Henry III’s opponent in his acquisition of the kingdom of Burgundy. Agnes, the wife of Henry III and grandmother of Henry V, was therefore this man’s niece through his sister. The son and successor of this same Count Renaud, William I the Great, was father of Guy, archbishop of Vienne and later pope, the author of this letter. See *Dictionnaire de l’Art de vérifier les dates*, col. 503, Migne edition. Whether Bishop Azzo also sprang from this lineage is unclear. Certainly his name assigns him Lombardy as his homeland, where the aforesaid Otto-William, son of Adalbert, king of Italy, defeated and captured by Emperor Otto I in 964, perhaps first saw the light.] compels us to hear and love one another. For no one has ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it.

Therefore, as our kinsman—whom we desire to love with a twofold love in Christ, honor, and exalt above all—we admonish you not to refuse any longer peace with the Church; do not permit the suggestions of the wicked, who glory in pleasing themselves in our affairs, to rise to your heart; and do not choose to be the servant of all, when you ought to rule over all.

Henry, the Church seeks to claim nothing of your right for itself; as your mother, it freely administers all things to everyone. We do not aspire to the glory either of kingdom or empire, but desire only to serve God in the justice of His Church. Return therefore to yourself; return, and consider carefully what and who you have become. Do not trust in the pride of the wicked, because God resists the proud. You have soldiers as your helpers; the Church has as her defender the King of all kings, who purchased her with His own blood. She also has the holy apostles Peter and Paul as her lords and patrons.

Give up what does not belong to your office, so that you may worthily perform what is yours. Let the Church possess what belongs to Christ; let the emperor have what belongs to him. Let each side be content with its own office, and let neither side through any ambition arrogate anything to itself from the other, since both ought to observe justice toward all. If you are willing to hear us and obey our admonitions and the counsel of religious and wise persons, you will give great joy both to God and to the world, and together with the height of temporal kingdom and empire you will attain also the glory of the eternal kingdom.

Furthermore, you will bind us and the whole Church to yourself in such bonds of affection that, by the grace of Almighty God, you will truly be seen as prince, truly as king, and truly as emperor. But if you rashly adhere to the flatteries of fools who wish to rule you and to their wicked suggestions, and fail to render the honor due to God and the Church, through religious and wise men we shall take care to provide for the Church of God, not without injury to you; for we are unable to endure this condition any longer.

Given on the eleventh day before the Kalends of March. “Leguntii episcopus” [reading uncertain].

## CLXIX. Privilege for the Monastery of St Peter at Melk. (1122, March 10.)

[HUEBER, *Austria illustrata*, p. 7.]

[Col. 1233C]

Calixtus, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ERKENFRID, abbot of the monastery of St Peter at Medelikeh, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of our office urges us to concern ourselves with the condition of churches and to confirm what has been rightly established. Therefore, beloved son in Christ, Abbot Erkinfrid, we graciously grant your petition and, at the request of our fellow-brother Reginmar, bishop of the Church of Passau, place under the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Saint Peter over which, by God’s ordinance, you preside, following the example of our predecessor of holy memory, Pope Paschal. [Col. 1233D] Moreover, Margrave Liupold offered to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, to be fostered forever under its protection, that same place, built by his parents at Medlikch in the parish of Passau and possessed under the right of patronage.

By the present page of privilege, therefore, we establish by apostolic authority that whatever estates, possessions, or churches with offerings of tithes the aforesaid princes Liupold and his father Liupold, and their other kinsmen, or other faithful persons, have bestowed from their own right upon that monastery, or whatever may hereafter be offered through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, [Col. 1234A] the offerings of the faithful, or acquired by other means, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.
