CXXXIII.---To Manasses, Archbishop of Reims.---On ten churches to be restored to Lambert. 141

CXXXIV.---To Lambert, Bishop of Arras.---On certain clerics absolved from excommunication. 141

CXXXV.---To B[ernard, Archbishop of Toledo], D[iego] of Compostela, D. (?) of Mondoñedo, P[eter] of Lucca, bishops.---On the abbot of Cines. 142

CXXXVI.---He confirms the immunity of the Church of Affligem. 142

CXXXVII.---To Stephen, Abbot of Bèze.---He confirms the possessions and rights of the monastery of Bèze. 142

CXXXVIII.---He urges King Henry to reconcile Saxony with the Roman Church. 144

CXXXIX.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Monte Cassino. 144

CXL.---He confirms the privileges of the monastery of St Peter in Ciel d’Oro at Pavia. 148

CXLI.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St Benedict at Polirone, imposing on the monks an annual tribute of two ounces of gold. 148

CXLII.---To Guido, Bishop of Pavia.---He confirms the privileges, possessions, and rights of the bishopric of Pavia. 151

CXLIII.---To Martin, Prior of Camaldoli.---He takes the monasteries subject to the Camaldolese hermitage under protection. 152

CXLIV.---To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.---That, at the Lateran Council, the supporters of investitures in England are excommunicated. 154

CXLV.---He threatens Robert, Count of Meulan, with God’s wrath if he continues to persuade the King of the English “to oppose the Roman Church in the matter of investitures.” 154

CXLVI.---He rebukes Gerard, Archbishop of York, because he “neither swore to assist” Anselm “nor opposed the king’s injustice.” 155

CXLVII.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Altdorf, imposing on the monks an annual payment of one Byzantine coin. 155

CXLVIII.---He confirms the privileges of Pons, Bishop of Le Puy. 155

CXLIX.---To the clergy of the Church of Paris.---He commends to them Galon, made Bishop of Paris and departing from him, and sends him with the fullest authority. He forbids senior prebendaries to receive homages from junior ones. He places the monastery of St Eligius, notorious for the laxity of its nuns, at Galon’s discretion. 157

[Col. 1488]

CL.---To Daimbert, Archbishop of Sens.---He commends to him the bishop of Paris, consecrated by himself. 158

CLI.---The establishment of the collegiate church of St Mary at Bruges is confirmed. 158

CLII.---Confirmation of goods belonging to the church of Ferrara, whose boundaries are assigned, and to which eleven lesser estates from the patrimony of the Roman Church are granted. 159

CLIII.---To Bernard, Archbishop of Toledo, and Diego, Bishop of Compostela. 161

CLIV.---Privilege for the monastery of Tournus. 161

CLV.---Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud. 164

CLVI.---He takes the monastery of St Michael (diocese of Verdun) under protection and confirms its possessions. 165

CLVII.---He confirms the ancient exemption of the See of Oviedo. 168

CLVIII.---To the Bishop of Beauvais concerning a certain land of St Bertin called Hubertinsin. 169

CLIX.---To Diego, Bishop of Compostela.---On the wearing of mitres. 170

CLX.---To G[undisalvus], Bishop of Mondoñedo.---He declares that he has learned that the archpresbyterates of Bisancos, Trasancos, and Salagia belong by right to the Church of Compostela. He commands him to claim them no longer. 170

CLXI.---He confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of Tulle. 171

CLXII.---He takes the monastery of St George in the Black Forest into the special protection of the Apostolic See. 172

CLXIII.---To Hugh, Abbot of Cluny. 173

CLXIV.---To Rothard, Archbishop of Mainz.---On bishops invested by kings; likewise on those consecrated during the time of schism. 174

CLXV.---At the request of Gertrude, Countess of Flanders, he confirms certain possessions of the Church of St Walburga at Veurne. 175

CLXVI.---Privilege for the bishopric of Pistoia. 175

CLXVII.---To Eustace, Abbot of St Nicholas.---Privilege of that abbey. 178

CLXVIII.---To the entire Gallican clergy.---He recounts Werner’s invasion of the Apostolic See. 179

CLXIX.---Paschal’s rescript to the letter of Otto, Bishop of Bamberg, in which he stated that he had received the bishopric from the emperor but was unwilling to remain in it unless he were invested and consecrated by the pope. 180

CLXX.---He entrusts the case of Odo, Abbot of St Quentin, to the Bishops of Chartres and Paris. 180

CLXXI.---He forbids A[dam], abbot, and the monks of St Denis “to approach bishops other than Galon, Bishop of Paris, for receiving the sacraments, without his permission.” 180

CLXXII.---Charter confirming the churches held by the canons of Langres. 181

CLXXIII.---Under penalty of excommunication he commands Gisela, Abbess of Remiremont, to desist from harassing the monks of Chaumousey. 182

CLXXIV.---Bull for the monastery of St Peter at Chartres. 183

CLXXV.---Bull for the monastery of St Walaricus. 184

CLXXVI.---To Bertram, Prior of St Faith at Sélestat.---He confirms the goods and privileges of that monastery. 185

CLXXVII.---To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.---He congratulates him upon the peace concluded with the king. 186

CLXXVIII.---To William, Bishop of Rouen.---William was suspended. The pope writes to him that, through the intercession of Anselm, he grants whatever Anselm may grant. 188

CLXXIX.---To William, Archbishop of Rouen. 188

CLXXX.---To B[uthard], Bishop of Mainz. 188

CLXXXI.---To Guido, Bishop of Ticino, and the clergy of Pavia. 189

CLXXXII.---Privilege for the monastery of St Saviour and St Julia at Brescia. 189

CLXXXIII.---To R[uthard], Archbishop of Mainz.---He commends Otto, Bishop of Bamberg, consecrated by himself. 191

CLXXXIV.---To the clergy and people of Bamberg.---He commends Bishop Otto to them. 192

CLXXXV.---He praises the parishioners of the Church of St Frigdianus at Lucca for obeying the canons. 192

[Col. 1489]

CLXXXVI.---He confirms the privileges of the Church of St Frigdianus at Lucca. 193

CLXXXVII.---To B[ernard], Archbishop of Toledo. 194

CLXXXVIII.---To Peter, Archbishop of Acerenza.---He confirms his election and the rights of the metropolitan see of Acerenza, and sends the pallium. 194

CLXXXIX.---Bull for Benedict, Abbot of the monastery of St Saviour at Moxi. 195

CXC.---To the bishops of Gaul.---Against the killers of the Abbot of Vézelay. 196

CXCI.---If Gisela, Abbess of Remiremont, has scorned to fulfil his command concerning the monks of Chaumousey “until the beginning of the next Lent, he forbids her entry into the church from that time onward.” 197

CXCII.---To Gebhard, Bishop of Constance, and Oderic, Bishop of Passau.---Not all excommunicated persons are to be avoided. 197

CXCIII.---He confirms to Hugh, Abbot of St Giles, the abbey of Seumich, founded by Ladislaus, King of the Hungarians. 198

CXCIV.---To Guido, Abbot of St Stephen at Laon.---Privilege of the monastery of St Stephen. 199

CXCV.---To the monks of St Peter and St Saviour at Pavia. 200

CXCVI.---To the canons of Augsburg. 200

CXCVII.---He commands Diego, Bishop of Compostela, together “with the bishops of the provincial sees—Peter of León, Pelagius of Asturias, and others—to determine, by the most certain investigation, the dispute between the clergy of the Churches of Osma and Burgos concerning the boundaries of their common parish.” 201

CXCVIII.---Privilege for the Church of Coimbra. 201

CXCIX.---To Hugh, Abbot of Cluny.---He forbids anyone to demand toll or anything else from those going to or leaving Cluny within the designated boundaries. 201

CC.---He confirms the rights and goods of the monastery of La Chaise-Dieu. 202

CCI.---To William of Sabran and the other associates of Bertrand, Count of Toulouse.---Under penalty of excommunication, he summons them to make satisfaction for damage inflicted upon the monastery of St Giles. 202

CCII.---To Richard, Archbishop of Narbonne, and the bishops of his province.---He recounts the adulteries of Bertrand, Count of Toulouse, and the damage inflicted upon the monastery of St Giles, and urges them to restrain others from assisting or associating with him and his companions. 203

CCIII.---To the clergy of Augsburg.---He rejoices that they have been reconciled with Bishop Hermann. 204

CCIV.---To Hugh, Abbot of Cluny.---He confirms the rights and possessions of the Cluniacs. 204

CCV.---Confirmation, made to Abbot Gauceran, of the churches and possessions of the monastery of Athanac. 205

CCVI.---He adjudicates the dispute between the nunnery of Remiremont and the canonry of Chaumousey. 206

CCVII.---To the monks and burgesses of St Giles.---He announces that Bertrand, Count of Toulouse, has been excommunicated by him, and commands them, under penalty of excommunication, to avoid him. 207

CCVIII.---Privilege for the monastery of St Germain-des-Prés. 207

CCIX.---He confirms the privileges of the monastery of St Laumer at Blois. 208

CCX.---He confirms the privileges of the monastery of St John at Chartres. 209

CCXI.---Privilege for the abbey of St Martin-des-Champs. 209

CCXII.---Privilege for the monastery of St Arnulf. 210

CCXIII.---He confirms the possessions of the abbey of Elnone, or St Amand, of the Order of St Benedict, and fortifies them with apostolic privileges. 211

CCXIV.---To Gebhard, Bishop of Constance.---He rebukes him because, having been invested, he attended the consecration of Henry, Archbishop of Magdeburg, and did not come when summoned to the council. 213

CCXV.---He does not grant the petition of Reinhard, Bishop of Halberstadt, because he “received the governance of the Church through the investiture of a lay hand.” He announces what was decreed at the Council of Troyes. 214

CCXVI.---To Rothard, Archbishop of Mainz.---He charges him with certain offences committed by him and, so that he may not err in future through ignorance, sends him excerpts from the sacred canons; at the request of certain prelates, he also graciously grants him indulgence. 214

CCXVII.---To Nicholas, abbot, and the monks of Corbie.---For the benefit of the school of Corbie, he confirms a gift made by King Philip, that merchants should have free passage to the market of Corbie. 215

CCXVIII.---He confirms certain privileges of the monastery of St Remigius at Reims. 216

[Col. 1490]

CCXIX.---At the request of Bishop Humbald, he confirms the goods of the Church of Auxerre. 217

CCXX.---Privilege for the monastery on the island of Agenes. 218

CCXXI.---To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.---He permits Anselm to promote the sons of priests to holy orders, admit Abbot Richard to communion with him, and dispense the remaining matters as circumstances may seem to require. 219

CCXXII.---Bull confirming the exemption, already granted by a bull of Pope Nicholas II, of the monastery of Corbigny from subjection to Flavigny. 220

CCXXIII.---To Hugh, Abbot of Cluny.---He awards to the Cluniacs the cell of St Denis at Nogent against William, Abbot of St Peter at Chartres. 220

CCXXIV.---He grants a bull to Hugh, Abbot of St Germanus at Auxerre. 221

CCXXV.---To Richard, Archbishop of Narbonne.---He confirms the possessions and rights of the Church of Narbonne. 222

CCXXVI.---To the abbots of St Pons and of Electum.---That they are not to receive persons excommunicated by the Bishop of Narbonne. 223

CCXXVII.---To the monks of St Giles.---He announces that he has absolved Count Bertrand, after he repaired the damage inflicted on the monastery of St Giles [printed: “St Aegyptus”]. 223

CCXXVIII.---Decree for the district of Salmoriac. 224

CCXXIX.---To Hugh, Abbot of Cluny.---He subjects the abbey of St Wilmar to him for correction. Its abbots are henceforth to be appointed by the abbots of Cluny. Any monk may transfer to the monastery of Cluny. 225

CCXXX.---He grants certain privileges to the monastery of St Benedict at Polirone. 226

CCXXXI.---At the request of Bishop Rangerius, he confirms the privileges of the Church of Lucca. 226

CCXXXII.---He confirms certain privileges of Gregory, archdeacon; Hubert, archpriest; Rainerius, primicerius; Guido, cantor; and the brothers of the Church of Lucca. 227

CCXXXIII.---To John, Abbot of Florence.---Privilege of the Florentine monastery. 227

CCXXXIV.---Bull of Pope Paschal II.---Privilege for the nunnery of St Peter of Lucca. 228

CCXXXV.---To Daimbert, Archbishop of Sens.---He entrusts to him the adjudication of the case of two abbots. 229

CCXXXVI.---To the clergy of the Church of Jerusalem, the king [Baldwin], and the people. 230

CCXXXVII.---He subjects certain monasteries to the monastery of La Chaise-Dieu. 232

CCXXXVIII.---He commands Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, to judge the marriage case of Robert, count, imprisoned by the King of England. 232

CCXXXIX.---Privilege for the church of St Martin. 232

CCXL.---To Adelgot, Archbishop of Magdeburg.---He summons him to the Apostolic See to render an account of the offence committed. 233

CCXLI.---To Bruno, Archbishop of Trier.---He entrusts to him the absolution from excommunication of the Bishop of Liège. 234

CCXLII.---To Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg.---He consoles him because he had suffered much from his own people; likewise concerning certain persons interdicted by him and concerning the Guibertines. 234

CCXLIII.---He assigns the monastery of St Germanus at Auxerre to Hugh, Abbot of Cluny. 235

CCXLIV.---He commends the canons of St Frigdianus to R[angerius], Bishop of Lucca. 235

CCXLV.---He rebukes R[angerius], Bishop of Lucca, because he allows the canons of St Frigdianus to suffer injuries. 236

CCXLVI.---To R[otho], provost of St Frigdianus. 236

CCXLVII.---To R[angerius], bishop, and the canons of the Church of Lucca.---Concerning the canons of St Frigdianus. 236

CCXLVIII.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St Michael at Siegburg. 237

CCXLIX.---He commands Lambert of Arras and John of Thérouanne to judge between the canons of Tournai and the monks of St Martin. 237

CCL.---Privilege for the church of St Evasius. 237

CCLI.---He confirms to Otto, Bishop of Bamberg, the town of Albegerinstein, granted by King Henry. 238

CCLII.---He writes to P[eter] of León, D[iego] of Compostela, R. of Palencia, P. of Nazareth, and P[elagius] of Asturias, bishops, concerning the boundaries of the Church of Burgos, which are not to be diminished. 238

[Col. 1491]

CCLIII.---At the request of Bishop Garcia, he confirms the boundaries of the diocese of Burgos. 239

CCLIV.---To several bishops and abbots of Gaul.---On the legation of the Apostolic See entrusted to Girard, Bishop of Angoulême. 240

CCLV.---Privilege for the church of St Mary of Vasert. 241

CCLVI.---He informs Lawrence, Abbot of St Vitonus, that Richard, Bishop of Verdun, has not been received into communion by him. 242

CCLVII.---To Eustace, Bishop of Valence, and Leodegarius, Bishop of Viviers.---That they should restrain Bertrand, Count of Toulouse, who, though absolved from the bond of excommunication at their prayers, was again despoiling the monastery of St Giles. 242

CCLVIII.---To Berengar, Bishop of Fréjus, and Leodegarius, Bishop of Apt.---That they should cease, together with the Count of Toulouse, from attacking the monastery of St Giles. 243

CCLIX.---He confirms the liberty, privileges, and possessions of the monastery of St Bertin at Sithiu. 243

CCLX.---To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.---He promises to provide for the privilege of the holy Church of Canterbury. 243

CCLXI.---Privilege for the monastery of Selbald. 246

CCLXII.---To D[iego], Bishop of Compostela.---That no one may celebrate Mass on the altar of Blessed James except the bishop or the seven cardinals. 247

CCLXIII.---He confirms the exemption of the Church of Burgos and the boundaries established for it in a council. 248

CCLXIII bis.---He confirms the boundaries and liberty of the Church of Burgos. 248

CCLXIV.---To Henry, King of the English. On the same subject. The king’s letter to which he replies has been lost. 249

CCLXV.---To Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury.---He grants what Anselm had requested. 250

CCLXVI.---He exhorts Ildefonsus, King of the Spains, not to permit the parishes of churches, confirmed by Roman pontiffs, to be confused. 251

CCLXVII.---He commands the Bishop of Huesca to make satisfaction to the Bishop of Barbastro for injuries inflicted. 251

CCLXVIII.---To Baldwin, Archbishop of Dol.---Privilege of Baldwin, Archbishop of Dol, concerning the pallium. 251

CCLXIX.---To the suffragans, clergy, and people of Dol.---He grants the pallium to Baldwin, Archbishop of Dol. 252

CCLXX.---He confirms the possessions and rights of the Church of St Frigdianus at Lucca. 253

CCLXXI.---He commands the Catholic brethren of the Church of Verdun to avoid Bishop Richard, who is excommunicated, etc. 253

CCLXXII.---He exhorts the abbots and clerics of Guido’s archdeaconry to obey Guido, who had been deposed by Richard, invader of the Church of Verdun. 254

CCLXXIII.---Bull of protection and confirmation of the goods of the monastery of Chaumousey. 254

CCLXXIV.---He takes the monastery of St Lambert under protection and confirms its possessions. 256

CCLXXV.---Privilege for the church of St Deodatus. 256

CCLXXVI.---He takes the monastery of Weissenau under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, imposing on the monks an annual payment of one Byzantine coin. 257

CCLXXVII.---To Hugh, Bishop of Grenoble.---On the possessions of the Church of Grenoble, which are not to be alienated. 257

CCLXXVIII.---Bull for St Martin at Amiens. 258

CCLXXIX.---Privilege for Marmoutier. 259

CCLXXX.---To Pons, Abbot of Cluny.---He confirms for him and his successors all things by his predecessor popes.
monastery of Cluny, granted, conferred, and confirmed. 260  
CCLXXXI.—To the bishops of Anagni and Campania.—On the canonization of Saint Peter, bishop of Anagni. 261  
CCLXXXII.—To Peter, priest. 261  
CCLXXXIII.—To Pontius, abbot of Cluny.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Cluny. 262  
CCLXXXIV.—Privilege addressed to Pontius, abbot of Cluny, to whom he sends a white pallium, so that he may make from it dalmatics for use in the church of Cluny; granting him the use of pontifical insignia on the eight principal feasts of his monastery. 262  
CCLXXXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Siegburg. 263  
CCLXXXVI.—Commands Duke Theodoric and Richwin, bishop-elect of Toul [Col. 1492], to repel, by secular and ecclesiastical censure, the opponents of the monastery of Caimocias from oppressing the monks. 264  
CCLXXXVII.—To Henry, abbot of Saint Vaast. 265  
CCLXXXVIII.—To Gebhard, bishop of Constance.—On those communicating with excommunicated persons, and on how heretics are to be received. 265  
CCLXXXIX.—Privilege concerning the market and the meal given on the two feasts of Saint Remigius, likewise concerning the immunity of that church. 265  
CCXC.—Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary at Florence. 266  
CCXCI.—At the request of Bishop Geoffrey, confirms the boundaries of the diocese of Sora and the possessions of its church. 267  
CCXCII.—Confirmation of the endowment and property of the monastery of Saint Benignus at Fruttuaria. 268  
CCXCIII.—At the request of Bishop Peter, confirms the liberty, privileges, and possessions of the church of Squillace. 268  
CCXCIV.—Privilege for the church of Saint Christopher of Phalempin. 270  
CCXCV.—Privilege for the monastery of Saint Peter of Melk. 270  
CCXCVI.—At the request of Bishop Diego, confirms the possessions of the church of Saint James of Compostela. 272  
CCXCVII.—Writes to D[idacus/Diego], bishop of Compostela, that he grieves over the hardships of the Spanish churches. 273  
CCXCVIII.—To D[idacus/Diego], bishop of Compostela.—Concerning the restoration of the church of Saint Michael to P[eter], chaplain. 273  
CCXCIX.—To Geoffrey, abbot of Saint-Maixent.—Receives his monastery into the protection of the Holy See. 274  
CCC.—To Peter, bishop of Poitiers.—He is to admonish Hugh of Lusignan not to delay in making amends for the injuries inflicted upon the monastery of Saint-Maixent. 275  
CCCI.—To Peter, bishop of Poitiers.—Entrusts to his judgment several causes of the monastery of Saint-Maixent for settlement, and commits to him lands held under rent from the Roman Church. 275  
CCCII.—Bull addressed to Saint Raymond, bishop of Barbastro. 275  
CCCIII.—Receives the monastery of Saint Vincent at Capersano under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 277  
CCCIV.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the church of Sonnebecq. 278  
CCCV.—Confirms the possessions of the church of Saint Donatian at Bruges. 279  
CCCVI.—To Leodegar, bishop of Viviers.—Rebukes him because he permits the church of Saint Andeolus, which he had handed over to the canons of Saint-Ruf, to be taken from them by his clerics. 280  
CCCVII.—To Diego, bishop of Compostela.—Admonishes him to ensure that Queen Urraca, daughter of the king of Castile, under penalty of deprivation of her kingdom, desist from the incest which she incurred by marrying Alfonso, king of Aragon, who was related to her in the third degree of consanguinity. 280  
CCCVIII.—To Pontius, abbot, and the monks of Cluny.—Rebukes them because they caused chrism to be consecrated in their monastery. 281  
CCCIX.—To the canons of the church of Lucca. 281  
CCCX.—To the parishioners of the church of Saint Frigdianus at Lucca. 282  
CCCXI.—To the clergy and people of Arles.—That they should elect another in the place of their bishop Gibelin, who had been transferred to Jerusalem. 282  
CCCXII.—Congratulates King Henry because he “abhors the wickedness of his father.” He affirms that, if Henry “with full devotion of mind shows to him and to his legitimate successors the obedience which kings or emperors have shown to his Catholic predecessors,” he will indeed regard him as a Catholic emperor. He wishes envoys to be sent to him. 283  
CCCXIII.—Invites the Normans and Lombards to the service of the Roman Church. 283  
CCCXIV.—CCCXV.—Orders that the regalian rights be restored to King Henry by bishops and abbots. 283  
CCCXVI.—Privilege concerning investitures extorted by force. 284  
CCCXVII.—Grants to Otto, bishop of Bamberg, and his successors the use of the pallium and the right to have the cross borne before them. 285  
CCCXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Hersfeld. 286  
CCCXIX.—To Emperor Henry. 287  
CCCXX.—To the people of Arezzo. 287  
CCCXXI.—To Emperor Henry, ordained by him. 288  
CCCXXII.—Asks Emperor Henry to order property taken from the church of Rimini to be restored. 288  
[Col. 1493]  
CCCXXIII.—To Baldwin, king of Jerusalem.—Decrees that, in order to enlarge the boundaries of the diocese of Jerusalem, all cities which he subdues shall be subject to Jerusalem as their metropolitan see. 289  
CCCXXIV.—To Gibelin, patriarch of Jerusalem.—On the same matter. 289  
CCCXXV.—Thanks Emperor Henry because he ordered property lost by the clerics of Passau and by H., the judge, to be restored. 290  
CCCXXVI.—To Emperor Henry. 290  
CCCXXVII.—To John, bishop of Tusculum, and Leo, bishop of Vercelli and cardinals.—Promises that he will annul and invalidate the concession of investitures made to the emperor. 290  
CCCXXVIII.—Writes to Bruno, bishop of Segni and abbot of Monte Cassino, that “a bishop ought not at the same time to be an abbot.” He commands him to relinquish the abbacy. 291  
CCCXXIX.—Releases the monks of Monte Cassino from obedience to Bruno and commands that a successor be appointed in his place; unless they do so, he declares that he will place separate abbots over all the cells of the monastery. 291  
CCCXXX.—Urges the people of Segni to choose another bishop for themselves in Bruno’s place. 291  
CCCXXXI.—To Emperor Henry. 291  
CCCXXXII.—To Guy, bishop of Vienne.—The investiture of clerics by kings is to be wondered at [reading uncertain]. 292  
CCCXXXIII.—Writes to Ivo, bishop of Chartres, concerning investitures of churches, that “he did what he did under compulsion, and still forbids what he has forbidden, although he allowed certain unspeakable things to be written by certain unspeakable persons.” 292  
CCCXXXIV.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Corbie (diocese of Paderborn). 293  
CCCXXXV.—To Ralph, archbishop of Tours, and his fellow bishops, on behalf of the abbot of Saint-Albinus. 293  
CCCXXXVI.—To Lambert, bishop of Arras. 294  
CCCXXXVII.—To the same. 294  
CCCXXXVIII.—Confirms that the monastery of Monte Cassino is to be preferred to other monasteries throughout the West, free from every jurisdiction and subject only to the holy Roman Church; and decrees under anathema that its abbot shall hold, in every assembly of bishops and princes, a place superior to other abbots and shall give his opinion before all others of his order. 295  
CCCXXXIX.—Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud. 296  
CCCXL.—To Ralph, archbishop of Reims.—Confirms the privileges granted to the bishop of Arras. 297  
CCCXLI.—To the clergy and people of Arras.—Forbids the church of Arras to be made subject to Cambrai. 297  
CCCXLII.—Urges Baldwin, count of Flanders, and his mother Clementia to support the liberty of the church of Arras and defend its possessions. 298  
CCCXLIII.—For the monastery of Saint Martin of the Valley, to which he grants the safeguard of apostolic protection, specifies its churches and enumerates its privileges (80). 298  
CCCXLIV.—Receives the monastery of Saint-Bertin at Sithiu under protection and confirms its property. 301  
CCCXLV.—Secures for the monastery of Anchin the church of Saint George near Hesdin, given by John, bishop of Thérouanne. 303  
CCCXLVI.—To Bernard, patriarch of Antioch.—States that, by granting the aforementioned privilege, he did not intend to diminish the dignity of the patriarchal church of Antioch. 303  
CCCXLVII.—Confirms the liberty of the church of Orange, separated from that of Tricastin. 304  
CCCXLVIII.—Confirms the decrees of the council held at Vienne by Guy of Vienne and other archbishops, bishops, and abbots. 305  
CCCXLIX.—Calls the bishops of Spain to a synod to be held “at the forthcoming feast of Blessed Mary” (2 February 1113, at Benevento), “so that in his presence they may deliberate concerning the affair of the king of Aragon and Queen Urraca, and concerning a conference on peace and concord.” 305  
CCCL.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Nonantola. 306  
CCCLI.—Privilege for the monastery of Arêval. 308  
CCCLII.—To the bishops established throughout Denmark, among other things: “Concerning also the tribute which your predecessors established annually for Blessed Peter, we wish your brotherhood, together with our same brother the archbishop of Lund, to be diligent, lest the Roman Church suffer further fraud in this matter; rather, let your prudence wisely undertake in full this obligation of charity.” 310  
CCCLIII.—To Baldric, bishop of Noyon and Tournai.—That he should not permit the brethren of the monastery of Saint Martin to be harassed by the clerics of Tournai. 310  
[Col. 1494]  
CCCLIV.—To Galon, bishop of Paris, and the chapter of the church of Paris.—That servants of the church of Paris may be admitted to give testimony in civil suits. 311  
CCCLV.—To Emperor Henry. 312  
CCCLVI.—Judgment on the controversy between the abbot of Monte Cassino and that of the monastery of Terra Maggiore concerning the church of Saint Mary of Casale Plano, which is awarded to Monte Cassino. 312  
CCCLVII.—Bull by which he grants the protection of the Apostolic See to the hospice of Saint John of Jerusalem. 314  
CCCLVIII.—Grants Lanuin, prior of the Tower, authority to teach and bless hermits. 316  
CCCLIX.—To Bernard, patriarch of Antioch.—States that he did not grant the privilege of the church of Jerusalem to the prejudice of Antioch. 316  
CCCLX.—To Baldwin, king of Jerusalem.—On the same matter. 316  
CCCLXI.—Privilege for the monastery of Saint Nicasius at Reims. 317  
CCCLXII.—General privilege for the monastery of Saint Nicasius. 318  
CCCLXIII.—Assigns the cell of Gordana to the monastery of Aniane. 320  
CCCLXIV.—Urges the bishops and princes of Spain to put an end to the overthrow of churches, killings, plundering, and burnings. 321  
CCCLXV.—Privilege concerning the borough of Saint Remigius and the agreement between the said abbey of Saint Remigius and the abbey of Saint-Vaast. 322  
CCCLXVI.—Confirms the possessions of the monastery of Saint Victor at Marseille. 327  
CCCLXVII.—Bull enumerating the Camaldolese monasteries and receiving them under apostolic protection. 330  
CCCLXVIII.—To the clerics of the church of Tournai.—Grants them the right to have their own bishop, the yoke of the church of Noyon having been cast off. 332  
CCCLXIX.—To Bishop Lambert and the canons of Arras. 333  
CCCLXX.—To Lambert, bishop of Arras. 333  
CCCLXXI.—Defends the liberty of the monastery of Saint-Bertin at Sithiu against Pontius, abbot of Cluny. 334  
CCCLXXII.—To William, archbishop of Besançon. 334

CCCLXXIV.—To Lambert, bishop of Arras.—Writes to the arbitrators selected by him to settle the dispute between the canons and monks of Arras. 336  
CCCLXXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Saint-Ruf at Avignon. 336  
CCCLXXVI.—Privilege for the church of Apt under Bishop Langerius. 337

CCCLXXXII.—Confirms all possessions and privileges of the monastery of Subiaco. 345

CCCLXXXV.—Confirms the possessions of the church of Farinate, founded by the counts of Bergamo and conferred upon Blessed Peter, on condition that twelve coins of Milanese currency be paid annually to the Lateran Palace. 349  
CCCLXXXVI.—Privilege for the church of Blessed Lawrence at Florence. 349

[Col. 1495]  
CCCXCI.—Privilege for the church of Lescar. 354  
CCCXCII.—To Lawrence, abbot of Saint Vito.—That he should render neither obedience nor communion to the clerics of Verdun. 355  
CCCXCIII.—Urges Diego, bishop of Compostela, to labor for the restoration of peace. 356  
CCCXCIV.—Confirms the possessions and rights of the church of Blessed Mary in the port of Ravenna. 356

CCCXCVI.—To the canons of the church of Chartres.—Confirms Bishop Ivo’s decree by which he converted the provostships and the other benefices called precariae into common uses. 357  
CCCXCVII.—To Pontius, abbot of Cluny.—Confirms possessions acquired by him. 358  
CCCXCVIII.—To Pontius, abbot of Cluny.—Grants pontifical ornaments. 359

CDI.—At the request of Archbishop Maurice, confirms the boundaries of the diocese of Braga. 361

CDXXIV.—To Arnold, bishop of Carcassonne. 377  
CDXXV.—To King Henry and the bishops of England.—Rebukes them because, without consulting the pope, they do many things improperly. 378

[Col. 1496]

CDXLV.—To the canons and lay parishioners of the church of Saint Frigdianus at Lucca. 391

CDLII.—To Lanuin, prior of the Tower. 395  
CDLIII.—To Otbert, bishop of Liège.—Concerning the complaint of Ralph, archbishop of Reims. 395

CDLV.—To Adelgot, archbishop of Magdeburg. 396

CDLVII.—To Vitalis, abbot of Savigny.—Permits the brethren of Savigny to celebrate the divine offices during an interdict. 397  
CDLVIII.—Exempts the monastery of Pfäfers from the authority of the bishop of Basel and confirms its possessions. 397

CDLXII.—Privilege for the church of Saint Pancras at Hadmersleben. 399  
CDLXIII.—Grants Dominic, abbot of the monastery of Saint Facundus at Sahagún, the power of binding and loosing over the burgesses of Saint Facundus. 400

CDLXV.—Confirms certain possessions and privileges of the monastery of Saint Facundus at Sahagún, imposing upon the monks an annual payment of two solidi. 402  
CDLXVI.—Orders, in accordance with the judgment of a synod, that the episcopal see of Besançon [Col. 1497] remain in the church of Blessed Stephen. 402

CDLXIX.—Releases Oldegarius, abbot of Saint-Ruf and bishop-elect of Barcelona, from the government of the monastery, and commands him to accept the bishopric. He sends Boso, cardinal-priest, as legate to Spain. 405  
CDLXX.—To Raymond, marquis of Barcelona.—Congratulates him on his victory over his enemies and receives him and his people under his protection. 407  
CDLXXI.—To the archbishops, bishops, and clergy of England.—Announces that he is sending Anselm, abbot of Saint Sabas, as legate to England to hold synodal assemblies. 407  
CDLXXII.—Informs Henry, king of England, that he has conferred apostolic authority upon Anselm, abbot of Saint Sabas, for administration in England. 408  
CDLXXIII.—To B[ernard], archbishop of Toledo, M[aurice], archbishop of Braga, Al[fonso], bishop of Tui, Ie[ronymus], bishop of Salamanca, Queen T., and her barons P. Gonçalves, E. Muñiz, and E. Gusendiz: announces that he has assigned to Bishop Hugh of Portugal the church of Lamego, which had been adjudged to Bishop Gonsalvo of Coimbra. 408

CDLXXIX.—Privilege confirming all the property of the monastery of Saint Bartholomew, addressed to Abbot John. 412

CDLXXXI.—Privilege for the church of Blessed Mary in the Port. 414

CDLXXXV.—To the monks of Saint Giles. 416  
CDLXXXVI.—To Herman, bishop of Augsburg. 417  
CDLXXXVII.—Privilege for the canons of Saint Fidelis. 417

CDXC.—To the canons of the church of Augsburg.—On the case of their bishop. 418

D.—Confirms certain possessions of the monastery of Subiaco. [Col. 1498] 424

DVIII.—To the canons of Saint Frigdianus at Lucca. 430

DXVII.—Privilege for the church of Belley. 435

DXX.—Whether clerics owe tithes to clerics. 437  
DXXI.—Those who do not allow the Church of God to be regularly ordered are to be judged sacrilegious. 437  
DXXII.—He sells the Holy Spirit who gives tithes for money. 437  
DXXIII.—No one who refuses to be subject to any bishop may administer episcopal rites to abbots. 437

DXXV.—Whoever obtains churches through laymen is to be excommunicated. 438  
DXXVI.—On the same subject. 438  
DXXVII.—On the same subject. 438  
DXXVIII.—To Lanuin, prior of the Tower. 438  
DXXIX.—To the same. 439

## Letters and Privileges of Calixtus II
I.—To Adalbert, Archbishop of Mainz.—Concerning his own elevation. 1093

VII.—To the Abbot of Tournus in the kingdom of the Franks.—Privilege for Tournus. 1096  
VIII.—Privilege for the monastery of La Vallée. 1098

XIV.—For the same monastery. 1105

XX.—Bull concerning the gift of the church of St. Liberata, made by Hildebert, Bishop of Agen, to Stephen, Abbot of Chaise-Dieu. 1110

XXII.—To B., provost, clergy, and people of Hildesheim. 1113  
XXIII.—Grants to Berengar, Abbot of the monastery of Crassus in Septimania, and to his successors, the church of St. Peter of Valeriis, subject to an annual payment of two gold pieces. 1114  
XXIV.—To the noblewoman Jussolina and her sons, on the same subject as the preceding. 1114  
XXV.—Bull for Gerald, prior of the church of Blessed Stephen the Protomartyr at Cahors. 1115  
XXVI.—To Henry, King of the English, for settling the controversy concerning the primacy of the Church of York. 1117  
XXVII.—To Hervé, Abbot of the monastery of Redon.—Let him restore the money taken from the men of Quimperlé from Belle-Île, or appear to render an account at the Council of Reims. 1117  
XXVIII.—Bull for Guy, Abbot of Turturiacum. 1117  
XXIX.—Extract from a bull of Pope Calixtus II for Holy Trinity, Poitiers. 1119  
XXX.—Bull for the abbey of St. Vincent at Senlis. 1119  
XXXI.—To Turgid, Bishop of Avranches, and Hildebert, Bishop of Le Mans, etc.—Commends to them the monastery of Savigny. 1120  
XXXII.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the convent of St. Mary of Fontevraud. 1121  
XXXIII.—Confirms the possessions of the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul and St. Ghislain at Celles. 1124  

[Col. 1509]

XXXIV.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Vendôme. 1125  
XXXV.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Denis near Paris. 1126  
XXXVI.—Enumerates and confirms the possessions of the abbey of Bourbourg, a convent of noble Benedictine nuns recently founded by his sister Clementia, Duchess of Burgundy. 1127  
XXXVII.—To Godebald, Bishop of Utrecht.—Grants him the episcopal mitre. 1130  
XXXVIII.—Receives the monastery of Marbach under protection and confirms its privileges. 1130  
XXXIX.—Confirms the privileges of the church of St. Martin at Tours. 1131  
XL.—Confirms the liberty and privilege of the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu. 1133  
XLI.—Confirms the privileges of the church of Cambrai. 1134  
XLII.—To the clergy and people of Hildesheim. 1134  
XLIII.—Commands Gilbert, Archbishop of Tours, to carry the following letter to Henry, King of the English, and, together with Geoffrey, Archbishop of Rouen, diligently to commend Thomas, Archbishop of York, to the king. 1135  
XLIV.—To Henry, King of the English. 1135  
XLV.—Bull concerning the privileges of the monastery of St. Mary of Jehoshaphat, in the diocese of Chartres. 1136  
XLVI.—Confirms the decree issued by Geoffrey, Bishop of Chartres, against simony. 1137  
XLVII.—Confirms the monastery of Springiersbach and its discipline. 1138  
XLVIII.—To Morvan, Bishop of Vannes, and Brice, Bishop of Nantes.—That they compel the Abbot of Redon by canonical coercion to repay the money owed to the Abbot of Quimperlé. 1138  
XLIX.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of St. Remigius at Reims. 1138  
L.—Grants to the abbey of St. Amand, or Elnone, of the Order of St. Benedict, privileges of liberty and immunity. 1139  
LI.—Exhorts Ralph of Durham, Ralph of Orkney, John of Glasgow, and all bishops throughout Scotland, suffragans of the Church of York, to obey Thurstan, Archbishop of York, who had been consecrated by him. 1141  
LII.—Letters delivered to the kings of Norway for the admission of Ralph, Bishop of Orkney. 1142  
LIII.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the Parisian monastery of St. Martin-des-Champs. 1142  
LIV.—Bull for Pacanus, abbot, and the monks of Blessed Mary of Étampes. 1145  
LV.—To Josceran, Bishop of Langres.—Appoints him judge in the dispute between the Abbot of Saint-Pierre-le-Vif at Sens and the Abbot of Molesme. 1146  
LVI.—To the monks of St. Viventius at Vergy.—Orders, under penalties of interdict, that they receive a prior from the monastery of Cluny. 1146  
LVII.—Asks Benedict, Bishop of Lucca, to protect securely those travelling to him or returning from him. He commends to him A., prior, and the church of St. Frigdianus. 1146  
LVIII.—To Stephen, Abbot of Cîteaux.—Confirms the statutes of the monastery of Cîteaux. 1147  
LIX.—Declares Bruno, Archbishop of Trier, free from every authority of a legate unless a legate be sent *a latere* (“from the pope’s side”). 1148  
LX.—Confirms for Archbishop Bruno metropolitan right and other ancient insignia. 1148  
LXI.—Orders that the hospital founded at Koblenz before the church of St. Florin by Bruno, Archbishop of Trier, be maintained. 1149  
LXII.—To Ulrich, Bishop of Constance.—That he restore to the people of Schaffhausen an estate taken by force. 1149  
LXIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Saviour of Schaffhausen. 1150  
LXIV.—To Hugh, Bishop of Auxerre.—Grants him authority to confer upon churches of canons and monks those churches which laymen had held. 1152  
LXV.—Privilege of Pope Calixtus by which is confirmed the decree of the Council of Beauvais concerning the dispute between William, Bishop of Châlons, and the canons of Cheminon, to whom Richard, Bishop of Albano, had granted excessive immunity. 1152  
LXVI.—Confirms the immunity and possessions of the monastery of Vézelay. 1155  
LXVII.—To Berard, Bishop of Mâcon, and Walter, Bishop of Chalon.—Informs them that he has consecrated the altars of the monastery of Tournus and blessed its cemetery. 1155  

[Col. 1510]

LXVIII.—To the canons of Mâcon.—Against the devastators of the estate of Montgoudin. 1153  
LXIX.—Informs Adalbert, Abbot of Schaffhausen, that he has undertaken protection of the monastery. 1156  
LXX.—Confirms the privileges of the convent of Beaulieu. 1156  
LXXI.—To Marbod, Bishop of Rennes.—Concerning the sentence of excommunication pronounced against the abbot and monks of St. Melaine. 1157  
LXXII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Bonneval. 1157  
LXXIII.—To Humbald, Archbishop of Lyons.—Against the devastators of the estate of Montgoudin. 1158  
LXXIV.—Bull for the monastery of St. Cucuphas in the district of Vaux. 1159  
LXXV.—Confirms the property and privileges of the canons of the church of St. John at Besançon. 1162  
LXXVI.—To the Archbishops of Arles, Aix, and Embrun, and the other bishops throughout the province. 1164  
LXXVII.—Privilege for the monastery of Cluny. 1164  
LXXVIII.—To the canons of Vienne.—Confirms the ancient privileges of the Church of Vienne. 1167  
LXXIX.—Transfers to the Church of Compostela the metropolitan dignity of the Church of Mérida. 1168  
LXXX.—Informs bishops, abbots, clerics, etc., established throughout the provinces of Mérida and Braga, that he has entrusted his vicariate in those regions to Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela. 1170  
LXXXI.—Special letters to the Archbishop of Compostela. 1170  
LXXXII.—Orders Gonzalo, Bishop of Coimbra, and Jerome, Bishop of Salamanca, to obey their metropolitan Didacus. 1170  
LXXXIII.—Receives the Church of Portugal under protection and confirms its possessions. 1171  
LXXXIV.—To bishops, princes, counts, knights, and the other faithful throughout Spain. 1171  
LXXXV.—To Pelagius, Bishop of Braga. 1172  
LXXXVI.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary Magdalene at Besançon. 1172  
LXXXVII.—Confirms the discipline, possessions, and privileges of the canonical church of the people of the martyrs (at Oulx). 1173  
LXXXVIII.—To Amadeus, Bishop of Maurienne.—Commands him to restore the church of St. Mary at Susa to Arbert, provost of Oulx, within forty days. 1173  
LXXXIX.—Confirms the possessions of the church of St. John at Monza. 1173  
XC.—Confirms all the property and rights of the monastery of St. Saviour at Pavia. 1174  
XCI.—Receives the monastery of St. Paul of Argon under patronage and confirms its property and privileges. 1176  
XCII.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the church of St. Evasius at Casale. 1176  
XCIII.—Grants to Oberto, Bishop of Cremona, and his successors the right of consecrating the abbots of the monastery of St. Peter. 1177  
XCIV.—Confirms the possessions of the monastery of St. Saturninus at Cagliari. 1178  
XCV.—Dedicates the cathedral church at Volterra. 1178  
XCVI.—To John, Prior of Camaldoli.—Privilege for the monastery of Sesto. 1178  
XCVII.—Bull for the monastery of St. Mary of Morrona and its abbot Gerard. 1179  
XCVIII.—To Stephen, chamberlain and his legate residing at Trier.—Concerning his arrival in Rome. 1180  
XCIX.—C.—Confirms all donations made to the monastery of Monte Cassino by Gunnarius and his wife, with the addition of an annual payment to the Lateran palace to be rendered by the monks. 1181  
CI.—To the nobleman Gunnarius. 1182  
CII.—Commands Roger, Bishop of Volterra, to protect the possessions given by Gunnarius to the monastery of Monte Cassino. 1182  
CIII.—At the request of Bishop Robert, orders the church of Aversa to remain a suffragan of the Roman Church. 1183  
CIV.—Consecrates Gerald, Archbishop of Ragusa, gives him the pallium, and confirms the possessions and rights of his Church. 1184  
CV.—Commands the bishops of Upper Dalmatia, or Dioclea, to obey their metropolitan, Gerald, Bishop and Archbishop of Ragusa. 1184  
CVI.—Bull for the monastery of Volturno. 1184  
CVII.—To bishops and other faithful of the provinces of Bourges, Bordeaux, Auch, Tours, and Brittany.—Appoints Gerard, Bishop of Angoulême, apostolic legate. 1186  

[Col. 1511]

CVIII.—Receives the monastery of St. Sophia at Benevento under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1186  
CIX.—Commands Alpherada, abbess of the convent of St. Mary at Capua, to appear before him on the Thursday after the octave of Pentecost, to render an account of the right by which she had taken the church of St. Mary of Cingla from the monastery of Monte Cassino. 1189  
CX.—Confirms the privileges of the hermitage of Turrita. 1189  
CXI.—To Wulgrin, Archbishop of Bourges.—Concerning the expulsion of nuns from the convent of Carenton. 1189  
CXII.—Commands the clergy of St. Mary at Susa, under threat of excommunication, to restore that church within forty days to Arbert, provost of Oulx. 1189  
CXIII.—To Pons, Abbot of Cluny.—Assigns the church of St. Theodore to Cluny. 1189  
CXIV.—To Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela, legate of the Roman Church. 1190  
CXV.—Bull for the monastery of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul at Canterbury. 1191  
CXVI.—To Ralph, Archbishop of Canterbury. 1191  
CXVII.—At the request of Pons of Cluny, receives the convent of Marcigny under protection. 1192  
CXVIII.—Deprives the Archbishops of Pisa of the right to consecrate the bishops of Corsica. 1192  
CXIX.—Confirms the possessions of the canons of St. Lawrence at Genoa. 1194  
CXX.—Confirms the primacy of Humbald, Archbishop of Lyons. 1195  
CXXI.—Confirms the rights of the Church of Ravenna. 1195  
CXXII.—Bull concerning the establishment or restoration of a bishopric at Tres Tabernae in Calabria. 1195  
CXXIII.—Receives the monastery of Saints Philip and James and St. Walburga in the Sacred Forest under protection and confirms its property. 1197  
CXXIV.—To Widon, Bishop of Chur. 1198  
CXXV.—Secures for the monastery of Affligem the church of Bornhem. 1199  
CXXVI.—At the request of Bishop Dodona, confirms the boundaries of the bishopric of Modena and the property of its church. 1200  
CXXVII.—To A., prior of St. Frigdianus at Lucca. 1201  
CXXVIII.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Clement at Pescara. 1201  
CXXIX.—To Otto of Castello Iringi.—Grants authority to build a church and monastery under specified conditions. 1203  
CXXX.—Receives the church of St. Mary and St. Walburga at Furnes under protection and confirms its property and privileges. 1204  
CXXXI.—To all the faithful.—Announces that the city of Sutri was besieged until Burdinus the antipope and the city itself had surrendered to him. 1205  
CXXXII.—To the regular canons of Bergtestaden.—Approves their rule of life. 1206  
CXXXIII.—To Franco, Abbot of Tournus.—Privilege of immunity. 1207  
CXXXIV.—To the same.—Another privilege. 1208  
CXXXV.—Again exhorts Walter, Bishop of Maguelonne, who had already been admonished by letter in the preceding August, to judge between the brethren of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem and the monks of Aniane, disputing over the church of Saint-Sauveur-de-Rubeo. 1209  
CXXXVI.—Confirms the rights and property of the canons of Verona. 1210  
CXXXVII.—To Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela.—Concerning bishops suspended because they had not attended the council, and concerning the Archbishop of Braga deprived of his legateship. 1210  
CXXXVIII.—Writes to Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela, that the marriage of Gerald, who had taken as wife a kinswoman of his former wife, must be dissolved. 1211  
CXXXIX.—To Atto, Archbishop of Arles, Fulk, Archbishop of Aix, and the other bishops throughout Provence.—That they excommunicate Count Ildefonsus and his associates unless they make satisfaction to the monastery of St. Giles within forty days. 1211  
CXL.—To the Bishops of Uzès, Toulouse, and Nîmes.—That they declare Count Ildefonsus excommunicated unless he restores what he took from the monastery of St. Giles. 1212  
CXLI.—To Raymond of Baux, William of Sabrán, Elzéar of Castries, Raino of Castlar, and William Rainoard.—Threatens to excommunicate them as counsellors and helpers of Count Ildefonsus unless, within forty days, they cease harassing the monastery of St. Giles. 1213  

[Col. 1512]

CXLII.—To the burgesses of the monastery of St. Giles.—Releases them from the oath of fidelity given to Count Ildefonsus, who had compelled them to perjury. 1213  
CXLIII.—To Ildefonsus, Count of Toulouse.—Commands, under penalty of excommunication, that he make good the damages inflicted upon the monastery of St. Giles. 1214  
CXLIV.—Commands Pelagius, Archbishop of Braga, “to restore the honour of Blessed James in Portugal, which his predecessor Mauritius, Archbishop of Braga, had held as a benefice (*praestimonium*) from the Archbishop of Compostela, and which he himself was violently retaining.” 1214  
CXLV.—Reproves Alpherada, abbess of the convent of St. Mary at Capua, because, “after the second deadlines had passed,” she had not appeared for judgment. He threatens that, unless she comes or sends representatives, he will restore the church of Cingla to the monastery of Monte Cassino. 1215  
CXLVI.—Commends to Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela, the knight Guy, travelling to St. James. 1215  
CXLVII.—Concerning confirmation of the regular canons of the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem and their possessions. 1215  
CXLVIII.—Informs the Archbishop of Caesarea and the other bishops, abbots, etc., established throughout the province of Jerusalem, King Baldwin, etc., that he has sent the pallium to Patriarch Garmond. 1216  
CXLIX.—To Garmond, Patriarch of Jerusalem. 1217  
CL.—Writes to Mark, a Venetian cleric, that he has learned from the letters of Peter, Bishop of Porto, his legate, that Mark has offered his possessions to Blessed Peter subject to an annual payment of one Byzantine. He praises his piety and sends him the first foundation-stone for building the church. 1218  
CLI.—To Berengar, Archbishop of Narbonne, and his suffragans.—That they admonish Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse to permit the Abbot of St. Giles, whom he had expelled, to return to the monastery; otherwise, that they punish him with excommunication and interdict. 1218  
CLII.—Commands B[oso], legate of the Apostolic See, to exhort Queen Urraca, daughter of King Ildefonsus, to release Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela, from custody and restore the castles taken from him; and orders that, unless she obey within forty days, she be excommunicated, after the bishops have been summoned, and her entire land subjected to interdict. 1219  
CLIII.—To the Archbishop of Toledo, concerning the same matter. 1219  
CLIV.—Informs the archbishops and bishops of Spain concerning the foregoing letters to Cardinal Boso and Bernard, Archbishop of Toledo. 1220  
CLV.—To the queen, concerning the same matter. 1221  
CLVI.—To King Ildefonsus, concerning the same matter. 1221  
CLVII.—To Bernard, Primate of Toledo.—The rights of the primacy of Toledo. 1222  
CLVIII.—To the same.—On the same subject. 1223  
CLIX.—To the Bishops of Oviedo and León.—That they be subject to the Primate of Toledo. 1224  
CLX.—To bishops, abbots, and others in Spain.—That they obey Bernard, Primate of Toledo, as apostolic legate. 1224  
CLXI.—At the request of Louis, King of the Franks, confirms the union of the bishoprics of Noyon and Tournai. 1125  
CLXII.—At the request of Bishop Geoffrey, confirms the privileges of the Church of Miletus. 1226  
CLXIII.—To all the faithful. 1227  
CLXIV.—To Alexander, King of Scotland.—That he and the bishops obey the Archbishop of York, their metropolitan. 1229  
CLXV.—To John, Bishop of Glasgow. 1230  
CLXVI.—To the bishops of Scotland.—That they obey their metropolitan, the Archbishop of York. 1230  
CLXVII.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Germanus in the Fields. 1230  
CLXVIII.—To Emperor Henry V. 1232  
CLXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Melk. 1233  
CLXX.—To Anseric, Archbishop, and the canons of Besançon.—The privilege establishing St. John’s church as mother church over St. Stephen’s church. 1235  
CLXXI.—Papal *mundiburdium*—protective guardianship—granted to the monastery of Reichenbach. 1238  
CLXXII.—Privilege for the monastery of Zwiefalten. 1239  
CLXXIII.—Confirms the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul at Echenbrunn. 1240  
CLXXIV.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Godesberg. 1240  
CLXXV.—Receives the monastery of St. Saviour at Millstatt under protection and confirms its rights. 1242  
CLXXVI.—At the request of Benedict, Bishop of Lucca, confirms certain privileges of the Church of Lucca. 1243  
CLXXVII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Pratalia. 1243  
CLXXVIII.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of the Saviour and St. Boniface at Fulda. 1244  
CLXXIX.—Assigns to the monastery of St. Remigius at Reims the mother church of St. Martin together with half the estate of St. Remigius, and to the monastery of Montmajour the other half of the estate together with the chapel of St. Mary. 1246  
CLXXX.—To Rudolph, Archbishop of Reims.—Concerning avoidance of simony in the prebends of St. Timothy; recalling Robert, prior of St. Oriculus; and retaining monks in the church at Reitest. 1247  
CLXXXI.—Commends Otto, Count Palatine, because he repents of having served in the king’s army when Paschal II was captured. 1248  
CLXXXII.—Informs the Archbishop of Dol, his suffragans, and other prelates of churches established throughout the same province, concerning a general council to be held in Rome. 1249  
CLXXXIII.—Commands Count Raynulf, under penalty of excommunication, to restore the church of Cingla to the monastery of Monte Cassino within twenty days. 1249  
CLXXXIV.—Informs Archbishop Otto and the clergy and people of Capua of the interdict imposed on the church of Cingla and the monastery of St. Mary, and of the deposition and excommunication of Abbess Alpherada. 1249  
CLXXXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Monte Cassino. 1250  
CLXXXVI.—Bull for the monastery of St. Saviour at Leutewitz. 1254  
CLXXXVII.—Commands T[arasía], Queen of Portugal, to release Pelagius, Archbishop of Braga, whom she had captured; otherwise, from that moment pronounces upon her and her supporters a sentence of excommunication. 1255  
CLXXXVIII.—Commands D[idacus], Archbishop of Compostela, to exhort T[arasía], Queen of Portugal, to release P[elagius], Archbishop of Braga, from custody in accordance with his letters. If she does not do so within the appointed time, he orders the excommunication of the queen and the interdict of her land to be proclaimed. 1255  
CLXXXIX.—Congratulates Peter upon being made Abbot of Cluny. 1256  
CXC.—To the monks of Cluny.—Approves Peter, abbot-elect. 1256  
CXCI.—To the regular canons of Berngried.—Approves their rule of life. 1257  
CXCII.—Confirms all rights and privileges of the monastery of St. Eustace of Nervesia. 1258  
CXCVIII.—Congratulates Emperor Henry because at last he has returned to the bosom of the Church. Commends to him his legates residing with him, and wishes imperial legates to be sent to himself. 1260  
CXCIV.—Confirms certain possessions of the monastery of St. Mary at Pinerolo. 1261  
CXCV.—Privilege for the same monastery. 1261  
CXCVI.—Commands Otto, Archbishop of Capua, to exact penalties from clerics who have injured the monastery of Capua, subject to the monks of Monte Cassino. 1261  
CXCVII.—To Berengar, Bishop of Fréjus.—Against devastators of an estate belonging to the monastery of Lérins. 1261  
CXCIII.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the Hospital of St. John at Jerusalem. 1261  
CXCIX.—Exhorts the monks of Monte Cassino to obey Oderisius, abbot-elect. 1262  
CC.—Enumerates the property and rights of the monastery of St. Euphemia at Brescia, and confirms them under the protection of the holy Roman Church. 1262  
CCI.—Confirms all rights and privileges of Archpriest Frederick and the canons of Carpi. 1263  
CCII.—Confirmation of the privileges of the church of St. Rupert at Salzburg. 1265  
CCIII.—Decrees, against the petition of the monks of Nonantola, that the estate of Wilzaccara, together with the church of St. Caesarius in the district of Eutin, belongs to the regular canons. 1266  
CCIV.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Mary at Vangadice. 1267  
CCV.—To Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela. 1269  
CCVI.—Confirms the privileges and property of the canons of the church of Cremona. 1269  
CCVII.—Receives the monastery of Siena under protection and confirms its privileges. 1271  
CCVIII.—Privilege for the church of Blessed Mary at Blois. 1271  
CCIX.—Privilege for the monastery of Usinnbova. 1272  

[Col. 1514]

CCX.—At a general council, enrolls Conrad, formerly Bishop of Constance, among the saints. 1273  
CCXI.—To Gilbert, Bishop of Paris.—That all clerics and abbots of the diocese obey him; likewise, that a canon of Paris who becomes bishop of another church lose his prebend. 1274  
CCXII.—Receives the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu under protection and confirms its privileges. 1275  
CCXIII.—To John, Bishop of Thérouanne. 1276  
CCXIV.—Secures for the monastery of Holy Cross at Bordeaux the church of St. Macarius. 1276  
CCXV.—To the people and clergy of Augsburg. 1277  
CCXVI.—At the request of Bishop Nicholas, confirms the liberty and possessions of the Church of Monopoli. 1277  
CCXVII.—Commends to the people of Hamburg Adalbero, Archbishop consecrated by himself and endowed with the pallium. 1278  
CCXVIII.—Confirmation of all rights of the Church of Squillace. 1279  
CCXIX.—To Antony, Abbot of Sens. 1280  
CCXX.—To Atto, Bishop of Bamberg, apostle of the Pomeranians.—Concerning privileges granted to the Church of Bamberg. 1281  
CCXXI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Benedict at Crema. 1281  
CCXXII.—Receives the convent of St. Saviour and St. Julia at Brescia under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1283  
CCXXIII.—Privilege for the church of St. Deodatus. 1284  
CCXXIV.—Secures for the monastery of St. Ghislain certain altars granted by Burchard, Bishop of Cambrai. 1285  
CCXXV.—Bull for Albero, archdeacon and treasurer of the church of St. Stephen at Metz. 1285  
CCXXVI.—To the canons of St. John at Besançon.—Settles disputes between the churches of St. John and St. Stephen. Orders the return of the privilege of St. Stephen’s church granted by Pope Paschal. 1286  
CCXXVII.—Testifies that the privilege of the Church of Pisa to consecrate bishops of Corsica was condemned on the final day of the Lateran Council. 1287  
CCXXVIII.—To Peter, Bishop of Segovia.—At the request of his nephew King Ildefonsus, restores the ancient rights of his Church, recovered from the Saracens. 1290  
CCXXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Victor at Marseille. 1291  
CCXXX.—Privilege for the Church of Pavia. 1292  
CCXXXI.—Grants to Amadeus, Bishop of Maurienne, the provostship of the church of St. Mary at Susa and parochial jurisdiction over the city of Susa itself. 1293  
CCXXXII.—Confirms the liberty, privileges, and possessions of the monastery of St. George at Venice, imposing upon its monks an annual payment of two gold pieces. 1294  
CCXXXIII.—The monastery of St. Mary at Glastonbury, in the diocese, is received under the protection of the Apostolic See, and all its property and donations are confirmed. 1295  
CCXXXIV.—Confirms the possessions, liberty, and privileges of the monastery of All Saints at Bari. 1296  
CCXXXV.—To Louis, King of the Franks.—Commends Peter, cardinal and apostolic legate. 1297  
CCXXXVI.—Grants certain privileges to Richard, provost of Springiersbach, and his brethren. 1298  
CCXXXVII.—To the suffragan bishops and abbots of the province of Besançon.—Informs them of the sentence he has rendered concerning the mother-church status of St. John’s church. 1298  
CCXXXVIII.—To Spanish bishops, abbots, and provosts established throughout the provinces of Mérida and Braga.—That they obey Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela, his vicar. 1299  
CCXXXIX.—To all bishops, etc., dispersed throughout Europe. 1299  
CCXL.—To Pelagius, Bishop of Braga.—Concerning the privileges of the same church. 1299  
CCXLI.—Bull for the Church of Barbastro. 1300  
CCXLII.—To the Bishop of Pamplona. 1300  
CCXLIII.—Grants Benedict, Bishop of Lucca, use of the pallium. 1300  
CCXLIV.—Privilege for the monastery of Andres. 1301  
CCXLV.—To A., prior, and the brethren of St. Frigdianus at Lucca. 1303  
CCXLVI.—Forbids Berard, Bishop of Mâcon, to exercise episcopal office until he ceases from injuries against the monastery of Cluny. 1304  
CCXLVII.—Commends to Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg, A., a priest ordained by the Bishop of Augsburg. 1304  

[Col. 1515]

CCXLVIII.—Grants absolution from sins to all persons buried in the church of Compsa. 1304  
CCXLIX.—To all kings, counts, and princes.—Exhorts them to aid the afflicted Church of the Spains, grants indulgences to its helpers, and commends to them Aldegarius, Archbishop of Tarragona. 1305  
CCL.—To Geoffrey, Abbot of Vendôme.—Holds valid all privileges of the men of Vendôme. 1306  
CCLI.—To Atto, Archbishop of Arles, Raymond, Count of Barcelona, and Geoffrey Porcelet.—That they give aid to the monks of St. Giles against Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse and his supporters, whom he announces to have been excommunicated by himself. 1306  
CCLII.—To Walter, Bishop of Maguelonne, and others.—That they give aid to the monks of St. Giles against Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse and his supporters, whom he declares excommunicated by himself. 1307  
CCLIII.—Commands the Bishop of Roussillon to cease harassing the monastery of Albaron. 1307  
CCLIV.—Confirms the property, rights, and privileges of the monastery of Hugeshoffen, founded by Count Wernher of Ortenberg. 1308  
CCLV.—To John, Bishop of Glasgow. 1312  
CCLVI.—To A., prior of St. Frigdianus, and his brethren. 1312  
CCLVII.—Informs Louis, King of the Franks, that Robert, Bishop of Arras, summoned to court by Burchard, Bishop of Cambrai, at a general council, had come to him bearing the king’s letters. 1312  
CCLVIII.—Rebukes the Bishop of Roussillon because, contrary to his command, he persists in inflicting injuries upon the monastery of Albaron. 1313  
CCLIX.—Commands the monks of Cluny to think no further of Pons; commands Pons not to harass the abbey of Cluny. 1314  
CCLX.—Forbids the reimposition upon the church of St. John at Besançon of dues remitted by Count Raynald of Burgundy in the estate of Tussiacum, commonly called *marascalcia* and *canaria*. 1314  
CCLXI.—Bull confirming property belonging to the church of St. Mary. 1314  
CCLXII.—Settles the dispute between Oberto, Bishop of Cremona, and his canons. 1316  
CCLXIII.—Privilege for the abbey of Mont-des-Anges. 1317  
CCLXIV.—Privilege for the monastery of Bifurca. 1318

CCLXVI.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Der. 1320  
CCLXVII.—To Jocerannus, Bishop of Langres.—Commends the monastery of Der as subject to the Roman Church. 1320  
CCLXVIII.—Confirms the privileges of the church of St. Frigdianus at Lucca. 1321  
CCLXIX.—To Benedict, Bishop, and the canons of the Church of Lucca. 1321  
CCLXX.—Grants Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela, that the city of Mérida remain subject to the city of Compostela for all time. 1321  
CCLXXI.—To the Bishop of Salamanca, concerning the obedience owed to his lord of Compostela. 1322

CCLXXIV.—To Geoffrey of Chartres, John of Orléans, and Stephen of Paris, bishops.—That the interdict imposed on account of unlawful marriages be observed. 1323

## LETTERS OF VARIOUS PERSONS TO CALIXTUS

I.—Letter of heretics to Pope Calixtus II.—They express their assent to his election. 1337  
II.—Petition of Urban, Bishop of Llandaff, addressed to Pope Calixtus II at Reims. 1338  
III.—Louis VI, King of the Franks, to Calixtus.—Writes that he will never tolerate the subjection which the Primate of Lyons demanded from the Archbishop of Sens. 1339  
IV.—Ralph, Archbishop of Canterbury, to Calixtus.—Complains of the injury inflicted on himself and the Church of Canterbury in the consecration of the Archbishop of York. 1341  
V.—Letter of Adalbert, Archbishop of Mainz, to Calixtus.—Warns him concerning what Cono, Bishop of Strasbourg, reconciled to the Church, had suffered from the emperor. 1356  
VI.—Second letter of Adalbert, Archbishop of Mainz, to Calixtus. 1357
